detector:cosinus.name: COSINUS-1pi detector

summary.plain: COSINUS is a dark matter detector being commissioned at the Gran Sasso laboratory in Italy. It uses sodium iodide crystals, the DAMA/LIBRA material, cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero so that it senses both heat and light, to test whether DAMA's yearly signal is dark matter.

detector:cosinus.technology: Undoped NaI crystals operated as cryogenic scintillating calorimeters (phonon and light read-out) in a dry dilution refrigerator inside a water-tank shield and muon veto

intervals.label: first operation of the COSME detector (Canfranc tunnel)
second operation in the deeper, IGEX-type shield (2450 m.w.e.)
completed (detector removed from the shield; no end date published)

detector:cosme.name: COSME germanium detector

summary.plain: COSME was a small germanium crystal, about a quarter of a kilogram, in the Canfranc underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees. It was used in two runs, in the 1990s, to look for dark matter particles and for axions from the Sun, and set limits on both.

detector:cosme.technology: A 234 g natural germanium p-type coaxial HPGe crystal in a copper cryostat, built specially for low threshold and low background

intervals.label: completed (successor chamber took over the pressure vessel)

detector:coupp-2kg.name: COUPP-2kg bubble chamber

summary.plain: A small room-temperature jar of superheated CF3I that records bubbles with cameras; a nuclear recoil from a WIMP could trigger a bubble.

detector:coupp-2kg.technology: Room-temperature superheated CF3I bubble chamber with stereo cameras

intervals.label: operation (MINOS tunnel at Fermilab, then SNOLAB)

detector:coupp-4kg.name: COUPP-4kg bubble chamber

summary.plain: A two-litre jar of superheated CF3I watched by cameras and microphones; bubbles from alpha particles sound louder than those from a WIMP-like nuclear recoil.

detector:coupp-4kg.technology: Superheated CF3I bubble chamber (synthetic fused-silica jar) with cameras and piezoelectric acoustic sensors

detector:cresst.name: CRESST cryogenic calorimeter array

specs.isotope: CaWO4 (CRESST-II/III main target); sapphire (Al2O3) in CRESST-I; lithium aluminate modules also deployed in CRESST-III

summary.plain: Small crystals, some no heavier than a coin, cooled colder than outer space and watched for the tiny flash of light and warmth made when a particle bumps an atom inside.

detector:cresst.technology: Cryogenic calorimeters with tungsten transition-edge sensors (TES) on scintillating crystal absorbers (sapphire in CRESST-I; CaWO4 from CRESST-II on), reading both a phonon (heat) and a scintillation-light channel

detector:crex.name: CREX apparatus

summary.plain: The Hall A set-up used for CREX: a calcium-48 target in the electron beam and two high-resolution spectrometers measuring electrons scattered elastically at a small angle.

detector:crex.technology: Hall A high-resolution spectrometers with an enriched 48Ca target for parity-violating elastic electron scattering

intervals.label: removed from DESY; stored at SLAC

detector:crystal-ball.name: Crystal Ball detector

summary.plain: The Crystal Ball detector: 672 sodium iodide crystals arranged as a near-complete sphere around the collision point, inside which a spark chamber tracked charged particles.

detector:crystal-ball.technology: Segmented electromagnetic NaI(Tl) calorimeter of 672 crystals covering 94% of 4π, with a central spark chamber

intervals.label: LST sub-array (LST-1 to LST-4, CTAO-North) completed and inaugurated

detector:ctao.name: CTAO telescope arrays

description: Four Large-Sized Telescopes planned in the northern array (La Palma) for the lowest energies, 20 GeV to 3 TeV.
subsystems.name: Large-Sized Telescopes (LST)

description: Up to 23 Medium-Sized Telescopes distributed over both array sites, covering 80 GeV to 50 TeV.
subsystems.name: Medium-Sized Telescopes (MST)

description: Up to 37 Small-Sized Telescopes planned in the southern array (Paranal) for the highest energies, above 2 TeV.
subsystems.name: Small-Sized Telescopes (SST)

summary.plain: Two big groups of gamma-ray telescopes, one in Spain and one in Chile, coming in three different sizes so together they can see the whole range of gamma-ray energies.

detector:ctao.technology: Two ground-based arrays of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes in three size classes (Large, Medium, Small).

summary.plain: 988 crystals of tellurium dioxide, cooled to a fraction of a degree above absolute zero, arranged in towers inside a giant refrigerator under an Italian mountain.

detector:cuoricino-detector.name: CUORICINO detector

summary.plain: Sixty-two crystals of tellurium oxide stacked in thirteen layers. A decay inside a crystal warms it by a hair's breadth, and a thermistor on each crystal records the temperature pulse.

detector:cuoricino-detector.technology: A tower of TeO2 crystals used as cryogenic bolometers, cooled in a dilution refrigerator and read out by neutron-transmutation-doped thermistors

summary.plain: About 1500 crystals of lithium molybdate, designed to both flash light and register heat when a particle hits them, planned to fill CUORE's existing refrigerator under the Gran Sasso mountain.

detector:cusb.name: CUSB detector

summary.plain: The CUSB detector: a compact non-magnetic ball of sodium iodide and lead glass crystals that measured the energies of photons from Upsilon decays at the north interaction point of CESR.

detector:cusb.technology: Non-magnetic NaI and lead-glass shower detector

intervals.label: LIME 50 L prototype (PHASE 0 R&D): underground data taking at LNGS (five periods)
CYGNO-04 (0.4 m^3) demonstrator under construction in LNGS Hall F

detector:cygno.name: CYGNO optical-readout TPC (LIME and CYGNO-04)

summary.plain: CYGNO is a directional dark matter project at Gran Sasso. A gas chamber of helium and CF4 turns particle tracks into light that cameras photograph, giving 3D tracks and their direction. A 50-litre prototype ran underground; a 0.4 cubic-metre demonstrator is being built.

detector:cygno.technology: He:CF4 (60:40) atmospheric-pressure gas TPC with triple-GEM amplification and optical readout (sCMOS camera and PMTs)

detector:d0.name: D0 detector

specs.muon_system: Three outer layers of muon detectors surrounding the calorimeters
specs.tracker: Silicon detectors nested inside scintillating-fiber tracking detectors mounted on carbon-fiber supports (Run II)

summary.plain: A four-story-tall, roughly 5,500-tonne particle detector at Fermilab, named after its location on the Tevatron ring, built to trace and measure particles from proton-antiproton collisions with especially precise calorimeters.

detector:d0.technology: General-purpose collider detector with uranium/liquid-argon calorimetry, and (from Run II) silicon and fiber tracking inside a solenoidal magnet

detector:dama-libra.name: DAMA/LIBRA detector

summary.plain: Twenty-five highly radiopure sodium iodide crystals, about 250 kg in all, read by photomultiplier tubes and shielded by copper, lead, polyethylene and concrete at Gran Sasso.

detector:dama-libra.technology: Array of 25 highly radiopure NaI(Tl) scintillating crystals read by photomultiplier tubes

detector:dama-nai.name: DAMA/NaI detector

summary.plain: About 100 kg of highly radiopure sodium iodide crystals (nine crystals of 9.7 kg), read by photomultiplier tubes, inside copper, lead, polyethylene and concrete shielding at Gran Sasso.

detector:dama-nai.technology: Array of nine highly radiopure NaI(Tl) scintillating crystals read by photomultiplier tubes

detector:damic.name: DAMIC CCD array

summary.plain: A stack of camera-sensor-like silicon chips, cooled and shielded two kilometres underground at SNOLAB, watching for the faint trace of a dark matter particle bumping into a silicon atom.

detector:damic.technology: Thick, fully-depleted scientific CCDs for ionization detection, later supplemented with skipper-readout CCDs for single-electron sensitivity

detector:damic-m.name: DAMIC-M Low Background Chamber

summary.plain: A small, extremely quiet chamber of silicon chips deep under a mountain in France, sensitive enough to notice a single electron being knocked loose by a dark matter particle.

detector:damic-m.technology: Skipper-readout silicon CCDs providing single-electron ionization resolution

detector:danss-detector.name: DANSS detector

summary.plain: A block of about two and a half thousand plastic strips that glow when an antineutrino interacts, read out by light sensors, mounted on a lift so it can be moved closer to or further from the reactor.

detector:danss-detector.technology: Highly segmented plastic-scintillator spectrometer with Gd-loaded reflective strip cover, SiPM and PMT readout

detector:darkside-20k.name: DarkSide-20k detector

summary.plain: A much larger tank of liquid argon than its predecessor DarkSide-50, holding fifty tonnes, being built deep under an Italian mountain to hunt for dark matter with thousands of tiny light sensors.

detector:darkside-20k.technology: dual-phase (two-phase) liquid argon TPC with SiPM light readout

specs.shielding: 30 t organic liquid scintillator neutron veto inside a 1 kt water-Cherenkov muon veto

summary.plain: A small tank of liquid argon, about fifty kilograms of it, that watched for dark matter particles bumping into argon atoms deep under an Italian mountain.

detector:darkside-lowmass.name: DarkSide-LowMass detector

summary.plain: DarkSide-LowMass is a proposed 1.5-tonne liquid argon detector designed to detect dark matter lighter than about 10 GeV through the faint electric charge it would free in the argon. It is a project of the Global Argon Dark Matter Collaboration; the primary plan is to install it at SNOLAB in Canada.

detector:darkside-lowmass.technology: Dual-phase liquid argon TPC optimised for ionisation-only (electron-counting) analyses

detector:darksphere.name: DarkSPHERE spherical proportional counter

summary.plain: A hollow copper sphere, filled with a light gas and read out by a central sensor, that detects the tiny ionization produced when light dark matter bumps a gas atom.

detector:darksphere.technology: Electroformed-copper spherical proportional counter filled with a helium-isobutane gas mixture

detector:dasi.name: DASI interferometer

summary.plain: A 13-element microwave interferometer on a tower beside a South Pole observatory that, in 2002, made the first detection of the polarization of the Big Bang afterglow.

detector:dasi.technology: 13-element, co-planar interferometric array operating in ten 1-GHz bands spanning 26-36 GHz.

detector:daya-bay-antineutrino-detectors.name: Daya Bay antineutrino detectors

target_mass.display: 20 t Gd-doped liquid scintillator per detector

summary.plain: A set of identical tank-like detectors, each holding 20 tonnes of a liquid that glows when antineutrinos interact in it, spread across near and far halls at Daya Bay.

detector:daya-bay-antineutrino-detectors.technology: Functionally identical cylindrical antineutrino detectors filled with gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator, viewed by photomultiplier tubes

intervals.label: detector upgrades (neck flow guides, particulate removal system)

detector:deap-3600.name: DEAP-3600 detector

specs.shielding: 2 km of rock overburden (6000 m.w.e.) at SNOLAB; the detector sits inside a 7.8 m diameter shield tank of ultra-pure water instrumented with 48 PMTs that serve as a muon veto.

subsystems.description: A 5-cm-thick spherical acrylic vessel, 85 cm inner radius, holding up to 3600 kg of liquid argon (fiducial volume 1000 kg within 55 cm radius), viewed by 255 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-HQE PMTs that detect the 128 nm argon scintillation light after it is wavelength-shifted to the visible band by a tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) coating.
subsystems.name: Acrylic vessel and PMT array

summary.plain: A sphere of 3.6 tonnes of liquid argon watched by 255 light sensors, 2 km underground in Canada. It looks for the faint flash of light a dark matter particle would make if it bumped into an argon atom, using only that light (no electric charge signal) to tell signal from background.

detector:deap-3600.technology: Single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector; unlike a two-phase argon or xenon TPC, DEAP-3600 has no drift field and no ionization/charge readout. It detects only scintillation light, collected by 255 PMTs, and uses the pulse shape of that scintillation signal (pulse-shape discrimination) to separate nuclear-recoil candidates from electromagnetic backgrounds.

intervals.label: DAΦNE physics data taking (kaonic nitrogen, then hydrogen)

detector:dear.name: DEAR setup

summary.plain: The DEAR set-up at DAΦNE: a cryogenic gas-target cell where stopped kaons form kaonic atoms, viewed by 16 charge-coupled-device chips that record the atoms' X-rays.

detector:dear.technology: Pressurised cryogenic gas target cell with 16 CCD-55 charge-coupled-device X-ray detectors

detector:decam.name: Dark Energy Camera (DECam)

summary.plain: A 570-megapixel digital camera mounted at the focus of the 4-metre Blanco telescope in Chile; built for the Dark Energy Survey and still in use.

detector:decam.technology: Wide-field optical/near-infrared CCD imager: 570-megapixel focal plane of fully depleted CCDs, five-element corrector, seven filters, at the Blanco prime focus.

detector:deeme.name: DeeMe spectrometer

summary.plain: A magnet with four layers of wire chambers that measures the momentum of electrons coming from the muon target, looking for one with the energy expected from muon-to-electron conversion.

detector:deeme.technology: Compact magnetic spectrometer of a dipole magnet and four sets of multiwire proportional chambers

intervals.label: funded: DFG Research Unit 6006 (design, build and operate phase I)

detector:delight.name: DELight superfluid helium detector (phase I)

summary.plain: A cell of superfluid helium surrounded and topped by wafer-sized magnetic thermometers that register the energy of a possible dark matter collision.

detector:delight.technology: Superfluid helium-4 target instrumented with large-area magnetic microcalorimeters (MMC)

detector:delphi.name: DELPHI detector

specs.tracker: Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) detectors for full charged-particle identification, plus a high-precision silicon vertex detector

subsystems.description: Differentiates between the various secondary charged particles using Cherenkov radiation rings.
subsystems.name: Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) system

subsystems.description: Advanced silicon tracking for precise detection of very short-lived particles.
subsystems.name: Silicon vertex detector

summary.plain: A roughly 10-metre cube of instruments at LEP's Point 8, famous for being able to tell exactly which kind of charged particle flew through it using rings of light (Cherenkov radiation).

detector:delphi.technology: General-purpose collider detector with Ring Imaging Cherenkov particle identification and precision silicon vertexing

detector:desi-instrument.name: DESI instrument (corrector, focal plane, fibre system and spectrographs)

summary.plain: The fibre-fed spectroscopic machine mounted on the Mayall telescope: a wide-field lens corrector, 5,020 robotic fibre positioners and ten spectrographs.

detector:desi-instrument.technology: Prime-focus multi-object fibre spectroscopic system: 5020 robotic fibre positioners feeding ten spectrographs that record 360–980 nm at resolution 2000 to 5000.

intervals.label: continued stable operation after the physics run

detector:dm-ice17.name: DM-Ice17 detector

summary.plain: DM-Ice17 was 17 kg of sodium iodide crystals frozen into the Antarctic ice at the South Pole next to the IceCube neutrino detector, a first test in the Southern Hemisphere of the yearly signal DAMA reported. Too small to settle that question, it showed that the ice is a quiet place for such detectors.

detector:dm-ice17.technology: Two NaI(Tl) crystals with photomultiplier tubes in pressure vessels, deployed in the South Pole ice

intervals.label: data taking with three NaI(Tl) modules

summary.plain: DM32 was an early dark matter search with three sodium iodide crystals (32 kg) run by a Zaragoza group in the Canfranc underground laboratory, Spain, from 1993 to 1994. It set competitive limits and looked for a yearly modulation.

detector:dmradio.name: DMRadio apparatus (DMRadio-m3 / DMRadio-50L)

summary.plain: DMRadio is a family of experiments being built at Stanford and SLAC that use a magnet and a tuned electrical circuit, instead of a microwave cavity, to search for very light dark-matter axions.

detector:dmradio.technology: Lumped-element resonant LC-circuit axion dark-matter search: a toroidal (DMRadio-50L) or solenoidal (DMRadio-m3) magnet coupled to a high-Q LC oscillator and SQUID readout, sensitive to sub-microwave-frequency axion-induced currents rather than a resonant cavity.

intervals.label: development and surface-laboratory commissioning (10-L detector at MIT)

detector:dmtpc.name: DMTPC 10-liter detector

summary.plain: DMTPC (Dark Matter Time Projection Chamber) is a directional dark matter experiment led from MIT. A low-pressure CF4 gas chamber with camera readout images the tracks of recoiling nuclei, which could reveal the direction a dark matter particle came from. A 10-litre detector ran at MIT and then underground at WIPP.

detector:dmtpc.technology: Low-pressure (75 Torr) CF4 dual back-to-back time projection chamber with CCD optical readout and charge readout

detector:donut.name: DONUT detector

summary.plain: A stack of nuclear-emulsion sheets and iron plates, backed by electronic trackers, that caught tau neutrinos as they interacted -- the first detector ever to do so directly.

detector:donut.technology: Nuclear-emulsion target with interspersed steel sheets, combined with electronic scintillator counters and drift chambers

detector:double-chooz.name: Double Chooz detectors

summary.plain: Two similar tank-shaped detectors of gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator, one close to and one far from the Chooz reactors, catching antineutrino flashes of light.

detector:double-chooz.technology: Liquid-scintillator detector whose main detector has four nested cylindrical volumes: a gadolinium-loaded scintillator target, a gadolinium-free scintillator gamma catcher, a buffer oil and an optically separated liquid-scintillator veto

detector:drift.name: DRIFT-II detector

summary.plain: DRIFT is a family of detectors in the Boulby mine that use low-pressure gas to trace the direction of the atom a dark matter particle would knock, which could show whether it comes from the direction our Solar System moves through the Galaxy. It has run since 2001.

detector:drift.technology: Low-pressure negative-ion CS2/CF4 gas time projection chamber with directional sensitivity

detector:dune-far-detector-1.name: DUNE Far Detector Module 1 (horizontal drift)

cryostat_count.display: 1 cryostat, 15.1 m (w) x 14.0 m (h) x 62.0 m (l) internal

specs.readout: three module-length anode planes built from 150 anode plane assemblies (APAs), each 6 m high by 2.3 m wide, with three layers of active wires

total_mass.display: 17.5 kt of liquid argon per cryostat

subsystems.description: 150 wire-readout anode plane assemblies forming three 58.2 m long anode planes
subsystems.name: Anode plane assemblies (APAs)

subsystems.description: Four drift volumes at a 500 V/cm field, with a cathode high voltage of 180 kV
subsystems.name: Cathode planes and field cage

subsystems.description: Photon detectors supplementing the TPC and extending the physics reach
subsystems.name: Photon detection system

summary.plain: The first of four giant tanks of liquid argon nearly a mile underground in South Dakota. Charged particles from neutrino collisions leave trails of electrons that drift sideways onto walls of wires, producing a photograph-like picture of each event.

detector:dune-far-detector-1.technology: single-phase horizontal-drift liquid argon time projection chamber with anode plane assembly wire readout

detector:dune-far-detector-2.name: DUNE Far Detector Module 2 (vertical drift)

specs.readout: charge readout planes (CRPs) at the top and bottom of the two stacked drift volumes

summary.plain: The second DUNE far detector. It uses the same liquid argon idea as the first one, but the electrons drift up and down instead of sideways, which makes the detector simpler to build.

detector:dune-far-detector-2.technology: vertical-drift liquid argon time projection chamber with a horizontal cathode bisecting the detector and charge readout planes above and below

detector:dune-near-detector.name: DUNE Near Detector

specs.target_medium: liquid argon (ND-LAr) and high-pressure gaseous argon (ND-GAr), plus the SAND inner tracker (two options under study: plastic scintillator cubes with TPCs, or straw tubes)

subsystems.description: Modular liquid argon TPC (35 optically separated modules) based on ArgonCube technology, a critical component of the near detector
subsystems.name: ND-LAr

subsystems.description: Possible Day-1 muon spectrometer (Temporary Muon Spectrometer, TMS) in the location of ND-GAr, immediately downstream of ND-LAr
subsystems.name: TMS (Temporary Muon Spectrometer)

subsystems.description: Magnetised on-axis beam monitor with an inner tracker and electromagnetic calorimeter inside a large solenoid, reusing the KLOE magnet and calorimeter
subsystems.name: SAND

summary.plain: A set of smaller detectors on the Fermilab site, right where the neutrino beam is made. Measuring the beam before it travels lets scientists work out what changed by the time it reaches South Dakota.

detector:dune-near-detector.technology: composite near detector: a modular liquid argon TPC (ND-LAr), a muon spectrometer downstream of it, and a magnetised on-axis beam monitor (SAND)

summary.plain: The superconducting magnetic ring in which muons circled and decayed, with detectors around its edge that recorded the positrons from the decays.

detector:e949.name: E949 detector

summary.plain: The E949 detector stopped kaons inside itself and watched what happened next, looking for the rare case of a kaon turning into a pion and invisible particles.

detector:e949.technology: Stopped-kaon spectrometer: incoming kaons are brought to rest in an active target/scintillator stack, and the outgoing pion is tracked and its full decay chain (range, energy and kinematics) measured to reject backgrounds

intervals.label: ECHo-1k phase (medium-scale experiment, about 1 kBq of 163Ho)
ECHo-100k phase (aims at a sensitivity below 2 eV)

detector:echo-detector.name: ECHo metallic magnetic calorimeter arrays with implanted 163Ho

summary.plain: Chips of ultra-cold magnetic thermometers: each pixel holds a few holmium-163 atoms and heats up by a measurable amount whenever one decays.

detector:echo-detector.technology: Metallic magnetic calorimeters (MMC) with 163Ho ion-implanted in the absorber, read out by SQUIDs at millikelvin temperature

detector:edelweiss.name: EDELWEISS germanium bolometer array

summary.plain: A block of ultra-pure germanium, cooled to near absolute zero deep under the French Alps, wired to catch both the tiny jolt of heat and the trickle of electric charge freed when a particle strikes an atom inside.

detector:edelweiss.technology: Cryogenic germanium bolometers reading both ionization (charge) and phonon (heat) signals; the current sub-GeV programme uses NbSi transition-edge sensors with Neganov-Trofimov-Luke phonon amplification

intervals.label: NaI modules deployed at the Kamioka underground laboratory (first configuration)
ELEGANT V in the Oto Cosmo Observatory (16 NaI scintillators, 0.76 tons)

detector:elegant-v-nai.name: ELEGANT V NaI array

summary.plain: ELEGANT V was a 0.76-ton array of sodium iodide crystals in Japan's Oto Cosmo Observatory, an underground laboratory in Nara, used to search for dark matter alongside double-beta-decay studies. Its crystals and lead shield later served the PICO-LON dark matter project.

detector:elegant-v-nai.technology: Array of 16 NaI(Tl) scintillators (0.76 tons) inside lead and copper shields

intervals.label: collaboration formed; EIC project detector technical design

detector:epic.name: ePIC detector

summary.plain: A cylindrical detector about 9.5 metres long built around a large solenoid magnet, with silicon and gas trackers, particle-identification layers and calorimeters, plus detectors far along the beam pipes.

detector:epic.technology: Compact general-purpose collider detector: silicon and micro-pattern gas tracking in a 1.7 T solenoid, fast-timing and Cherenkov PID, electromagnetic and hadronic calorimeters, plus far-forward and far-backward detectors

detector:essnusb-far-detector.name: ESSnuSB far detector

summary.plain: A planned water tank of 540,000 tonnes, split into two huge caverns a kilometre underground in the Zinkgruvan mine, lined with about 92,000 light sensors to catch neutrinos from the beam.

detector:essnusb-far-detector.technology: Underground water Cherenkov detector (540 kton) read out by photomultiplier tubes mounted on the cavern walls

detector:essnusb-near-detector.name: ESSnuSB near detector

summary.plain: A planned smaller underground detector on the ESS site, 250 metres from the neutrino target, combining a water tank with a fine-grained tracker inside a magnet, to measure the beam and neutrino interaction rates.

detector:essnusb-near-detector.technology: 1 kt underground water Cherenkov near detector with a magnetised scintillator-cube tracker and an emulsion stack

detector:exo-200.name: EXO-200 detector

summary.plain: A cylindrical tank of liquid xenon, chilled and shielded deep in a New Mexico salt mine, that watched for a rare radioactive decay by tracking both light and electric charge from each event.

detector:exo-200.technology: Liquid-xenon time projection chamber with combined charge/light readout

detector:faser.name: FASER detector

summary.plain: A compact particle detector in a disused CERN tunnel, combining a tracking spectrometer with a special emulsion-and-tungsten neutrino detector called FASERv.

detector:faser.technology: forward spectrometer with a tracking/magnet system and the FASERv emulsion-tungsten neutrino subdetector

intervals.label: ADONE two-beam data taking for FENICE

summary.plain: The FENICE detector at ADONE, built to detect neutron-antineutron pairs from electron-positron annihilation near threshold. The sources fetched do not describe its components.

detector:finuda.name: FINUDA spectrometer

summary.plain: The FINUDA magnetic spectrometer at DAΦNE: a cylinder of tracking detectors inside a 1-tesla solenoid, surrounding eight thin targets where stopped kaons form hypernuclei, with scintillator barrels for timing and for neutrons.

detector:finuda.technology: Cylindrical magnetic spectrometer in a 1.0 T superconducting solenoid with eight thin targets, silicon microstrip detectors, low-mass drift chambers, straw tubes and scintillator time-of-flight barrels

detector:flys-eye.name: Fly's Eye air-fluorescence detector

summary.plain: A pair of mirror-and-camera "eyes" that photographed the faint glow cosmic-ray air showers leave in the night sky.

detector:flys-eye.technology: Two compound eyes of spherical mirrors with photomultiplier-tube cameras that image the fluorescence light of air showers: Fly's Eye I (67 mirrors) and Fly's Eye II (36 mirrors).

detector:frejus-detector.name: Fréjus detector

summary.plain: A stack of thin iron plates alternating with gas-filled flash chambers that photograph the tracks of charged particles from two angles, about 900 tons in all, installed deep inside the Fréjus road-tunnel mountain.

detector:frejus-detector.technology: Modular iron-plate tracking calorimeter with plastic flash chambers (5 mm cells) and Geiger-tube trigger planes

intervals.label: installation and commissioning runs (first installed July-October 2002, reinstalled autumn 2003)
backward-angle commissioning and production (March 2006 to April 2007)

detector:g0.name: G0 apparatus

summary.plain: A superconducting doughnut-shaped magnet in Hall C with eight sets of scintillator and Cherenkov detectors around the beam, plus a cryogenic hydrogen or deuterium target and fast electronics that count individual particles.

detector:g0.technology: Superconducting toroidal magnetic spectrometer with plastic scintillation and aerogel Cherenkov detectors and a cryogenic hydrogen or deuterium target

detector:gallex-gno.name: GALLEX/GNO gallium target

summary.plain: A huge tank of gallium-laced liquid buried in an Italian mountain; when a low-energy solar neutrino hits a gallium atom, it turns into a germanium atom that scientists then count.

detector:gallex-gno.technology: Radiochemical gallium detector: solar neutrinos capture on 71Ga to produce 71Ge, which is chemically extracted and counted; the target is a gallium trichloride-hydrochloric acid solution, not an electronic real-time detector

detector:gargamelle.name: Gargamelle bubble chamber

summary.plain: A giant tank of liquid freon, 4.8 metres long, in which a passing charged particle leaves a trail of bubbles that cameras photograph. Neutrinos leave no tracks, so it showed them only through the charged particles they knocked into motion.

detector:gargamelle.technology: Heavy-liquid bubble chamber filled with freon (CF3Br)

intervals.label: approved by the CERN Research Board

summary.plain: The GBAR apparatus: a small electron accelerator that makes positrons, traps for antiprotons and positrons, and a free-fall chamber where single antihydrogen atoms are released and their annihilation recorded.

intervals.label: approved by the Gran Sasso Scientific Committee; funded; built
operation with four, then six, naked Ge detectors in liquid nitrogen

detector:genius-tf.name: GENIUS-TF detector (naked Ge diodes in liquid nitrogen)

summary.plain: GENIUS-TF was a small test version of the GENIUS idea, bare germanium crystals dipped in liquid nitrogen. It ran in the Gran Sasso laboratory in Italy from 2003 to about 2006 to prove the technique and, along the way, to look for the yearly dark matter signal reported by DAMA.

detector:genius-tf.technology: Naked high-purity germanium diodes operated directly in liquid nitrogen, which is both coolant and shield

detector:gerda.name: GERDA detector

summary.plain: Bare germanium crystals submerged directly in a huge tank of ultra-cold liquid argon, deep under an Italian mountain, listening for a rare kind of radioactive decay.

detector:gerda.technology: Bare enriched-germanium point-contact detectors immersed in a liquid-argon cryostat

detector:gluex.name: GlueX detector
subsystems: Photon beam tagging (scintillator hodoscope and scintillating fiber array), pair spectrometer and triplet polarimeter
Electromagnetic calorimetry: cylindrical scintillating fiber calorimeter inside the magnet and a lead-glass array downstream

summary.plain: A hermetic detector in Jefferson Lab Hall D that tracks charged particles in a 2-tesla solenoid and measures photons and particle flight times, built to reconstruct complete photoproduction reactions.

detector:gluex.technology: Large-acceptance, nearly hermetic photoproduction spectrometer: tagged linearly polarised photon beam, central straw-tube drift chamber and planar chambers in a solenoid, barrel and forward calorimeters, time-of-flight

detector:grand.name: GRANDProto300 (GRAND prototype)

summary.plain: A prototype radio antenna array in the Gobi Desert in China, testing the technology for a much bigger planned array to detect cosmic rays and neutrinos.

detector:grand.technology: Radio antenna array detecting radio-frequency signals from inclined extensive air showers initiated by cosmic rays and neutrinos

detector:grapes-3.name: GRAPES-3 scintillator array and muon telescope

description: 3712 proportional counters in 16 modules with a total area of 560 m2, recording muons above 1 GeV.
subsystems.name: GRAPES-3 muon telescope (G3MT)

summary.plain: A field of 400 plastic scintillators and a large muon telescope in southern India.

detector:grapes-3.technology: Dense array of plastic-scintillator detectors plus a tracking muon telescope built from gas-filled proportional counters.

detector:h-e-s-s.name: H.E.S.S. telescope array

description: Four 12 m diameter imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (CT1-CT4) arranged in a square of 120 m side length, installed between 2001 and 2003.
subsystems.name: Phase I telescopes (CT1-CT4)

description: A 28 m diameter telescope (CT5) at the centre of the CT1-CT4 square, described by the collaboration as the largest of its kind; using two telescope sizes enlarges the array's sensitive energy range.
subsystems.name: CT5 (28 m telescope)

summary.plain: Five telescopes on a Namibian farm: four medium-sized ones in a square around one giant telescope, together watching for the blue flicker of light that gamma rays make hitting the atmosphere.

detector:h-e-s-s.technology: Hybrid array of four 12 m and one 28 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes.

detector:h1.name: H1 detector

summary.plain: A large, complex detector at DESY built around one of the two points on the HERA ring where electrons and protons collided, designed to catch and identify the particles produced.

detector:h1.technology: Complex general-purpose detector combining high-precision mechanical tracking, calorimetry and modern electronics/computing to detect particles from ep collisions

detector:hades.name: HADES spectrometer

summary.plain: A six-sector spectrometer around the beam line with a toroidal magnet, a ring-imaging Cherenkov detector for electrons and drift chambers for tracking, built to find rare electron-positron pairs among the particles from a collision.

detector:hades.technology: Versatile magnetic spectrometer with a ring imaging gas Cherenkov detector, six superconducting coils with a toroidal field, drift chambers and a multiplicity and electron trigger array

detector:hagar.name: HAGAR telescope array

summary.plain: Seven small telescopes laid out in a hexagon about 50 metres in radius, each made of seven round mirrors, that time the arrival of the Cherenkov light front from air showers.

detector:hagar.technology: Wavefront-sampling array of seven non-imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes in a hexagon of 50 m radius.

intervals.label: strange form factor programme (HAPPEX-I, HAPPEX-II and HAPPEX-He, HAPPEX-III)

detector:happex.name: HAPPEX apparatus (Hall A High Resolution Spectrometers)

summary.plain: Hall A's two high-resolution spectrometers, which steer elastically scattered electrons onto detectors that integrate their signal during each beam-spin setting, with liquid-hydrogen or helium targets.

detector:happex.technology: Pair of Hall A High Resolution Spectrometers focusing elastically scattered electrons onto total-absorption shower counters whose signals are integrated over each helicity period

detector:hawc.name: HAWC water-Cherenkov array

summary.plain: An array of closed water tanks on a Mexican volcano that sense the faint flashes of light left by particles from gamma-ray and cosmic-ray showers as they pass through the water.

detector:hawc.technology: Array of closed water-Cherenkov detector tanks continuously sampling extensive air showers from gamma rays and cosmic rays.

intervals.label: Phase III upgrade (multi-rod cavity) and commissioning at Yale

start.display: after Phase II data-taking ended in August 2024; start of the upgrade not separately dated

detector:haystac.name: HAYSTAC detector

summary.plain: The HAYSTAC detector uses a strong magnet and a tunable metal cavity, plus quantum-noise-reducing electronics, to search for faint signals from dark-matter axions converting into radio photons.

detector:haystac.technology: Microwave-cavity haloscope using a strong static magnetic field (inverse Primakoff conversion) with quantum-electronics/cavity-QED readout, including a squeezed-vacuum receiver to beat the standard quantum noise limit.

intervals.label: prototype detector (natural Ge crystals) at LNGS
inner crystal replaced by enriched 73Ge; final setup installed
final setup (enriched 73Ge inner crystal) taking data

detector:hdms.name: HDMS detector (nested HPGe crystals)

specs.isotope: 73Ge (enriched inner crystal of the final setup)

summary.plain: HDMS, the Heidelberg Dark Matter Search, was a germanium experiment under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy. A small germanium crystal sat inside a larger one that vetoed stray radiation, so it could look for dark matter particles recoiling off germanium nuclei. It reported limits on how strongly such particles can interact.

detector:hdms.technology: Two concentric high-purity germanium ionization detectors in one cryostat: inner target crystal inside a well-type outer anticoincidence crystal

detector:hegra.name: HEGRA air-shower and Cherenkov telescope complex

specs.energy_range: IACT gamma-ray threshold about 0.5 TeV; spectrum of the Crab measured up to 80 TeV

description: Angle-integrating Cherenkov counters: 49 detectors in a 7-by-7 grid, with 48 more added later.
subsystems.name: AIROBICC

description: More than 250 scintillation counters spread over a 180 m by 180 m area.
subsystems.name: Scintillator array

description: Seventeen muon towers of 16 m2 area each.
subsystems.name: Muon towers

summary.plain: A set of detectors over an area of about 200 by 200 metres: imaging Cherenkov telescopes, light counters, ground-level scintillators and muon detectors, all watching air showers from cosmic particles.

detector:hegra.technology: Combined air-shower complex of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, the AIROBICC angle-integrating Cherenkov counters, a scintillator array and muon towers.

detector:heidelberg-moscow-detector.name: Heidelberg-Moscow detector array

summary.plain: Five germanium crystals, enriched in germanium-76, cooled in a lead and plastic shield deep under the Gran Sasso mountain; each crystal is at once the source of the decay and the detector that records it.

detector:heidelberg-moscow-detector.technology: Five p-type high-purity germanium detectors made from germanium enriched in 76Ge, in lead and borated-polyethylene shielding under nitrogen, with pulse-shape analysis

detector:hera-b.name: HERA-B spectrometer

summary.plain: A large forward spectrometer built around thin wire targets in the proton beam halo, with a silicon vertex detector, tracking chambers, particle identification and calorimeters.

detector:hera-b.technology: Forward fixed-target spectrometer with wire targets, vertex detector and extensive tracking and particle identification

intervals.label: concept proposed (superfluid helium, calorimetric readout) and R&D
planned installation of the TESSERACT setups (including HeRALD) at LSM

detector:herald.name: HeRALD superfluid helium detector

summary.plain: A cell of superfluid helium viewed from above by superconducting sensors that register the flash of light and the helium atoms knocked out of the liquid surface by a dark matter collision.

detector:herald.technology: Superfluid helium-4 target read out by TES calorimeters (scintillation and quantum-evaporation channels)

detector:hermes.name: HERMES spectrometer

summary.plain: A forward-angle particle spectrometer built around a spin-polarised gas target inside the HERA storage ring, with tracking chambers, a magnet, particle-identification detectors and calorimetry.

detector:hermes.technology: Forward-angle spectrometer with tracking chambers on either side of a dipole magnet and an internal polarised gas target

intervals.label: HiRes prototype and MIA muon array (hybrid)

detector:hires.name: HiRes air-fluorescence detector (HiRes-I and HiRes-II)

summary.plain: Two hilltop stations of telescopes that photograph the faint ultraviolet light of cosmic-ray air showers over the Utah desert.

detector:hires.technology: Two stations of spherical-mirror telescopes with 256-PMT cameras that image nitrogen fluorescence from air showers.

intervals.label: ERC grant period: design and set-up of the experiment

detector:holmes-detector.name: HOLMES TES microcalorimeter array with ion-implanted 163Ho

summary.plain: A chip of tiny thermometers, each holding a few holmium-163 atoms in a gold absorber, cooled to a tenth of a degree above absolute zero so every decay heats it by a measurable amount.

detector:holmes-detector.technology: Transition-edge-sensor microcalorimeters with 163Ho ion-implanted in a gold absorber, operated at about 95 mK in a dilution refrigerator with microwave-multiplexed readout

detector:homestake.name: Homestake chlorine detector

summary.plain: A tank of dry-cleaning fluid, nearly a mile underground, that turned rare chlorine atoms into argon whenever a solar neutrino struck.

detector:homestake.technology: Radiochemical chlorine detector: solar neutrinos capture on 37Cl to produce 37Ar via inverse beta decay in a large tank of perchloroethylene (dry-cleaning fluid), with the argon periodically extracted and counted

intervals.label: JLab approval of 165 days of running

detector:hps.name: HPS apparatus
subsystems: Silicon micro-strip vertex tracker (SVT), PbWO4 electromagnetic calorimeter (ECal) and scintillation hodoscope (SH)

summary.plain: A compact detector squeezed into the Hall B alcove right behind a thin tungsten target: a silicon tracker inside a magnet, a crystal calorimeter and a scintillator hodoscope that together catch electron-positron pairs.

detector:hps.technology: Compact large-acceptance forward spectrometer: tungsten foil target, silicon micro-strip vertex tracker, PbWO4 electromagnetic calorimeter and scintillation hodoscope

summary.plain: The High Resolution Spectrometer, a detector at the PEP ring at SLAC that recorded electron-positron collisions at 29 GeV.

detector:hyper-kamiokande.name: Hyper-Kamiokande detector

subsystems.description: New large-aperture, high-quantum-efficiency PMTs (up to 40,000 in the comparison-table maximum design; ~20,000 stated as the photosensor count elsewhere on the same site) viewing the main tank volume.
subsystems.name: Inner Detector

subsystems.description: Up to 10,000 smaller (8 cm-class) photosensors instrumenting the outer veto region.
subsystems.name: Outer Detector

subsystems.description: About 1,000 'compound eye' modules bundling multiple 8 cm PMTs for improved timing accuracy.
subsystems.name: Compound-eye photosensors

summary.plain: A huge new water tank being built underground near Kamioka: 68 metres across and 71 metres tall, more than five times the volume of Super-Kamiokande, ringed with tens of thousands of new light sensors.

detector:hyper-kamiokande.technology: Large cylindrical water Cherenkov tank, the successor design to Super-Kamiokande, instrumented with new high-sensitivity large-aperture PMTs and multi-PMT 'compound-eye' photosensor modules.

detector:iaxo.name: IAXO / BabyIAXO detector

summary.plain: The IAXO detector design uses a large magnet aimed at the Sun to catch faint signals from hypothetical axion particles. A smaller version, BabyIAXO, is being built at DESY as a stepping stone to the full-scale instrument.

detector:iaxo.technology: Axion helioscope: a purpose-built double-bore (IAXO) / toroidal (BabyIAXO) superconducting magnet tracking the Sun, coupled to X-ray focusing optics and low-background X-ray detectors, scaling up the CAST technique.

detector:icarus-t600.name: ICARUS T600

subsystems.description: cosmic ray tagger surrounding the cryostats, needed because the detector operates at shallow depth at Fermilab
subsystems.name: Cosmic Ray Tagger

summary.plain: A 760-tonne liquid argon detector, the first of its size ever built. It worked under an Italian mountain from 2010 to 2013, was rebuilt at CERN, and now sits at Fermilab as the far detector of a search for a possible fourth kind of neutrino.

detector:icarus-t600.technology: single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber in two adjacent modules

detector:icecube.name: IceCube in-ice array

specs.energy_range: Roughly 100 GeV to the PeV scale and above in the main array; about 10 GeV with the DeepCore infill

subsystems.description: Pressure sphere holding a ten-inch photomultiplier tube with on-board digitisation electronics
subsystems.name: Digital optical module (DOM)

subsystems.description: 86 strings on a hexagonal grid with 125 m horizontal spacing, 60 DOMs each, 17 m vertical separation
subsystems.name: String geometry

subsystems.description: Surface building that receives, digitises and time-stamps the DOM data
subsystems.name: IceCube Laboratory

summary.plain: The main part of IceCube: 86 cables lowered into holes melted in the ice, each carrying 60 basketball-sized light sensors that watch a cubic kilometre of ice for neutrino flashes.

detector:icecube.technology: In-ice Cherenkov array of digital optical modules frozen into the Antarctic ice sheet

detector:icecube-deepcore.name: DeepCore

specs.energy_range: Neutrino energy threshold lowered to about 10 GeV

subsystems.description: Horizontal separation about 70 m and vertical DOM spacing 7 m, versus 125 m and 17 m in the main array
subsystems.name: Dense string geometry

summary.plain: A tightly packed cluster of sensors in the middle of IceCube. Because the sensors sit closer together, it can see much fainter, lower-energy neutrinos, which is what makes IceCube able to study how neutrinos change type.

detector:icecube-deepcore.technology: Densely instrumented in-ice Cherenkov infill at the centre of the IceCube array

detector:icetop.name: IceTop

specs.energy_range: Air showers from primary cosmic rays in the 300 TeV to 1 EeV energy range

subsystems.description: Each of the 81 stations has two ice-filled tanks, each with two downward-facing DOMs
subsystems.name: Cherenkov tank pair

summary.plain: The part of IceCube that sits on the snow surface: 81 pairs of frozen water tanks that catch the showers of particles made when cosmic rays hit the atmosphere. It also helps IceCube tell cosmic rays apart from neutrinos.

detector:icetop.technology: Surface array of ice-filled Cherenkov tanks read out by downward-facing digital optical modules

intervals.label: dark matter phase of IGEX at Canfranc (one enriched 76Ge detector)

detector:igex-dm.name: IGEX 76Ge detector (dark matter configuration)

summary.plain: IGEX-DM was the dark matter search of the International Germanium Experiment. One 2-kilogram germanium crystal, made for a rare-decay study, was used deep under the Pyrenees at Canfranc to look for dark matter particles recoiling off germanium, and set limits on their interaction.

detector:igex-dm.technology: A 2.2 kg p-type high-purity germanium detector, enriched to 86% in 76Ge, read out at low energy in a lead, polyethylene and muon-veto shield

detector:index-dm.name: InDEx detector

summary.plain: InDEx is an Indian dark matter search using small superheated droplet detectors, 555 metres underground at Jaduguda in Jharkhand. Its first two runs found no dark matter and set limits on how strongly light WIMPs could interact.

detector:index-dm.technology: Superheated emulsion (droplet) detector with tetrafluoroethane (C2H2F4) and acoustic readout

detector:ingrid.name: INGRID (T2K on-axis near detector)

summary.plain: A cross-shaped array of iron-and-scintillator modules sitting directly in the path of T2K's neutrino beam, 280 metres from where the beam is made. It checks that the beam is pointed the right way and has the expected shape, run after run.

detector:ingrid.technology: On-axis array of iron/scintillator sandwich modules that measures the neutrino beam direction and profile.

detector:jade.name: JADE detector

summary.plain: The JADE particle detector at DESY's PETRA ring: a compact magnet surrounding a drift-chamber tracker and a lead-glass calorimeter, which together identified electrons, photons and jets of particles.

detector:jade.technology: Jet chamber with 96 drift cells in three concentric rings, lead-glass calorimeter, iron-yoke muon filter with drift chambers (92% of solid angle)

detector:jinping-neutrino-experiment-det.name: Jinping neutrino detector (proposed)

summary.plain: A planned tank holding several thousand tonnes of liquid scintillator, to be built in a new tunnel of the Jinping underground laboratory, so deep that almost no cosmic rays reach it.

detector:jinping-neutrino-experiment-det.technology: Liquid scintillator or water-based slow liquid scintillator target viewed by photomultipliers, in a cylindrical or spherical vessel

intervals.label: proposed to the J-PARC programme advisory committee

detector:jparc-muon-g-2-edm.name: J-PARC muon g-2/EDM apparatus

summary.plain: A chain of devices that cools muons to almost rest and accelerates them, a small precise magnet in which they circle, and a tracker that follows the positrons from their decays.

detector:jparc-muon-g-2-edm.technology: Muon cooling and acceleration chain feeding a compact storage-ring solenoid with a silicon positron tracker

intervals.label: long physics runs with the 24 m detector

detector:jsns2-detector.name: JSNS2 detector (24 m)

summary.plain: The scintillator detector of JSNS2: a tank of gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator watched by light sensors, 24 metres from the mercury target of J-PARC's neutron source, built to catch the flash of an antineutrino striking a proton.

detector:jsns2-detector.technology: Gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator in an acrylic vessel inside a stainless-steel tank, read out by photomultipliers; inverse beta decay with a delayed Gd neutron-capture signal

intervals.label: detector support-structure, acrylic-vessel and PMT installation
filling with ultrapure water and liquid scintillator

detector:juno.name: JUNO central detector

description: A complementary array of 25,587 3-inch photomultiplier tubes providing an independent, non-saturating energy measurement alongside the 20-inch PMT array
subsystems.name: 3-inch PMT double-calorimeter array

description: A water-Cherenkov detector plus an overhead Top Tracker system used for muon detection and cosmogenic-background rejection
subsystems.name: Water Cherenkov veto and Top Tracker

summary.plain: A 20,000-tonne sphere of clear liquid, watched by more than 17,000 large light sensors and over 25,000 smaller ones, sitting inside a pool of water that screens out stray particles.

detector:juno.technology: 20-kiloton liquid-scintillator sphere viewed by large- and small-diameter photomultiplier tubes, immersed in a water-Cherenkov veto pool with an overhead Top Tracker

detector:juno-tao-detector.name: JUNO-TAO detector

summary.plain: A sphere of gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator, cooled to minus 50 degrees and covered almost entirely with silicon light sensors, inside layers of shielding in a basement at the reactor.

detector:juno-tao-detector.technology: Gd-doped liquid scintillator viewed by ~10 m^2 of silicon photomultipliers at -50 C

intervals.label: KamLAND2 upgrade: detector dismantling and rebuilding (no data taking)

detector:kamland.name: KamLAND detector

summary.plain: A giant balloon of clear liquid inside a mine in Japan, watched by nearly 1,900 light sensors, that catches antineutrinos from nuclear reactors across the country. A xenon-loaded inner balloon suspended at its centre (KamLAND-Zen) uses the same detector to search for a different rare process.

detector:kamland.technology: Liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector: 1 kton of liquid scintillator in a 13-m-diameter spherical balloon, with an oil buffer between the balloon and an 18-m-diameter spherical stainless-steel containment vessel lined with 1,879 photomultiplier tubes, surrounded by a 3.2 kton water-Cherenkov outer detector that tags cosmic-ray muons

detector:karmen.name: KARMEN detector

summary.plain: A rectangular tank holding 65 cubic metres of liquid scintillator, split into 512 separate cells and laced with gadolinium to catch neutrons, sitting 18 metres from the ISIS accelerator's beam stop.

detector:karmen.technology: Segmented liquid-scintillation calorimeter with gadolinium-loaded module walls for neutron capture

detector:kascade.name: KASCADE array, muon tracking detector and calorimeter

summary.plain: A square of particle detectors, 200 metres on a side, with a muon tracker and a hadron calorimeter at its centre.

detector:kascade.technology: Multi-detector air-shower array measuring the electromagnetic, muonic and hadronic components of each shower.

detector:kascade-grande.name: Grande array with the KASCADE detectors

summary.plain: Thirty-seven scintillator stations spread over about half a square kilometre, running together with the original KASCADE detectors.

detector:kascade-grande.technology: Array of 37 scintillator stations (10 m2 each) spread over 700 m × 700 m, operated together with the KASCADE detectors.

intervals.label: TRISTAN phase: commissioning of the new detector system

detector:katrin.name: KATRIN spectrometer

summary.plain: A huge tube-shaped spectrometer that sorts electrons by their energy, precisely measuring the fastest ones released when radioactive tritium gas decays, to work out how heavy the neutrino can be.

detector:katrin.technology: MAC-E filter electrostatic/magnetic spectrometer with a windowless gaseous tritium source

detector:keck-array.name: Keck Array

summary.plain: Five small refracting telescopes sharing one mount at the South Pole, each like BICEP2, that watched the same patch of sky at 95, 150, 220 and later 270 GHz until they were replaced in late 2019.

detector:keck-array.technology: Five BICEP2-style receivers (260 mm aperture) on a single telescope mount.

detector:kedr.name: KEDR detector

summary.plain: The KEDR detector: a universal magnetic detector with a vertex detector, drift chamber, Cherenkov and time-of-flight counters, calorimeters, a muon system and a superconducting coil.

detector:kedr.technology: Universal magnetic detector: vertex detector, central drift chamber, aerogel Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight counters, LKr and CsI calorimeters, muon system, superconducting coil

intervals.label: WIMP-search data taking with CsI(Tl) crystals
stable running of the 12-crystal (103.4 kg) array

detector:kims.name: KIMS CsI(Tl) array

summary.plain: KIMS (Korea Invisible Mass Search) was an array of cesium-iodide crystals, 103.4 kg in all, deep in a tunnel at the Yangyang power plant in South Korea, built to catch dark matter particles. It saw no signal and set limits, including on regions claimed by the DAMA experiment.

detector:kims.technology: Array of low-background CsI(Tl) scintillating crystals read out by photomultiplier tubes, with pulse-shape discrimination of nuclear recoils

intervals.label: NaI(Tl) data taking for the published limits

detector:kims-nai.name: KIMS-NaI crystals

summary.plain: KIMS-NaI was the sodium-iodide stage of the Korean KIMS programme: the team grew its own low-radioactivity crystals, tested them underground at Yangyang and set dark-matter limits with two of them. A planned 200 kg array became, together with a US group, the COSINE-100 experiment.

detector:kims-nai.technology: Low-background NaI(Tl) scintillating crystals read by two photomultiplier tubes, with pulse-shape discrimination

detector:kloe.name: KLOE detector

summary.plain: The KLOE particle detector at DAΦNE: a 4-metre drift chamber inside a lead-and-scintillating-fibre calorimeter that recorded the decays of phi mesons, later upgraded for KLOE-2 with a cylindrical inner tracker of GEM foils.

detector:kloe.technology: 4 m-diameter drift chamber surrounded by a lead-scintillating-fibre electromagnetic calorimeter; KLOE-2 added a cylindrical GEM inner tracker

aliases: Astroparticle Research with Cosmics in the Abyss

intervals.label: 51 detection units operating (current, undated official statement)

detector:km3net-arca.name: KM3NeT/ARCA

instrumented_volume.display: ~1 km3 (design, two building blocks of 115 detection units each)

string_count.display: 230 detection units (design: two building blocks of 115 each)

summary.plain: The bigger of the two KM3NeT telescopes, built for spotting very high-energy neutrinos from deep space. It sits 3500 metres down on the seabed off Sicily and, when finished, will fill about a cubic kilometre of seawater with light sensors.

detector:km3net-arca.technology: Sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: vertical strings of digital optical modules, each housing photomultiplier tubes, anchored to the Mediterranean seabed

aliases: Oscillation Research with Cosmics in the Abyss
detector:km3net-orca.name: KM3NeT/ORCA

instrumented_volume.display: ~0.007 km3 (~7 Mt of seawater; design, one building block of 115 detection units)

summary.plain: The smaller, more tightly packed of the two KM3NeT telescopes, built to study neutrinos made in Earth's atmosphere and work out how the three kinds of neutrino are ordered by mass. It sits 2450 metres down on the seabed off Toulon, France.

detector:km3net-orca.technology: Sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: vertical strings of digital optical modules with closer sensor spacing than ARCA, optimised for lower-energy atmospheric neutrinos

detector:kolar-gold-fields-phase-i-detec.name: KGF Phase I proton-decay detector

summary.plain: The first KGF proton-decay detector: 34 layers of gas-filled iron counters and iron plates, about 140 tons, installed very deep in the mine and running from the end of 1980.

detector:kolar-gold-fields-phase-i-detec.technology: Iron-walled proportional counters in crossed horizontal layers interleaved with iron plates

detector:kolar-gold-fields-phase-ii-dete.name: KGF Phase II proton-decay detector

summary.plain: A larger second proton-decay detector at KGF, about 260 tons, operating from 1985 at a slightly shallower level than the first.

detector:kolar-gold-fields-phase-ii-dete.technology: Iron-walled proportional counters in crossed horizontal layers interleaved with iron plates

detector:koto.name: KOTO detector

summary.plain: The KOTO detector is a hermetic calorimeter and veto system in Japan that watches for the tell-tale flash of a neutral kaon decaying into a neutral pion and invisible particles, with nothing else visible.

detector:koto.technology: Hermetic electromagnetic calorimeter and veto-counter system surrounding a neutral-kaon beamline, reconstructing KL → π⁰ (→ γγ) decays while vetoing all other visible particles

intervals.label: proposal submitted to the J-PARC PAC; Stage-1 status recommended

summary.plain: A proposed detector made of a large crystal calorimeter and veto counters in a 12-metre decay region, looking for two photons from a neutral pion and nothing else.

detector:ktev.name: KTeV detector

summary.plain: The KTeV detector combined a calorimeter, tracking chambers and veto systems to catch neutral kaons decaying, at Fermilab in the 1990s.

detector:ktev.technology: Neutral-kaon spectrometer with electromagnetic (CsI) calorimetry, drift chambers, a transition radiation detector system and photon/particle veto systems, used to reconstruct KL decays to two pions/photons

detector:l3.name: L3 detector

specs.calorimeters: Bismuth-germanate (BGO) electromagnetic calorimeter, plus a hadronic calorimeter
specs.tracker: Silicon strip microvertex detector and a time-expansion chamber

subsystems.description: Bismuth-germanate crystal calorimeter giving very high resolution for electrons and photons.
subsystems.name: BGO electromagnetic calorimeter

subsystems.description: A very large solenoid magnet, later reused as ALICE's central magnet at the same LEP/LHC point.
subsystems.name: Solenoid magnet

summary.plain: A detector at LEP's Point 2 built to measure electrons, muons and photons with exceptional precision, using dense bismuth-germanate crystals and one of the largest magnets ever built for a particle detector.

detector:l3.technology: Collider detector optimised for high-resolution electron, muon and photon measurement, built around a bismuth-germanate calorimeter and a very large solenoid magnet

detector:legend-200.name: LEGEND-200 detector

summary.plain: Up to 200 kilograms of enriched germanium detectors immersed in liquid argon in the same Italian underground hall used by the earlier GERDA experiment, watching for a rare radioactive decay.

detector:legend-200.technology: Enriched high-purity germanium detectors immersed in a liquid-argon active shield

detector:lhaaso.name: LHAASO multi-component array

summary.plain: A set of different kinds of ground detectors on a Chinese mountain, working together to sense cosmic-ray and gamma-ray showers in several ways at once.

detector:lhaaso.technology: Multi-component extensive-air-shower detector combining different shower-sampling techniques (electron, muon and Cherenkov/fluorescence light) at one high-altitude site.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 / ECAL and RICH enhancements

detector:lhcb.name: LHCb detector

summary.plain: The LHCb detector is a single forward-pointing spectrometer, 21 metres long, 5600 tonnes, sitting 100 metres underground at CERN. Instead of surrounding the collision point on all sides like ATLAS or CMS, it stacks its sub-detectors one behind another to catch particles thrown forward by the collision.

detector:lhcb.technology: single-arm forward spectrometer with a warm dipole magnet, vertex locator (VELO), two RICH detectors, tracking stations, calorimeters and a muon system

detector:lhcf.name: LHCf detector

summary.plain: Two small, 40-kilogram detectors placed 140 metres either side of the ATLAS collision point, catching particles thrown almost exactly along the beam direction.

detector:lhcf.technology: two compact imaging sampling calorimeters (tungsten plates, plastic scintillator, position-sensitive sensors)

detector:lsnd.name: LSND detector

summary.plain: A cylindrical tank about 8 metres long holding 167 tonnes of mineral-oil scintillator, watched by more than a thousand light sensors, 30 metres from where the Los Alamos accelerator's beam produced neutrinos.

detector:lsnd.technology: Mineral-oil liquid scintillator detecting both Cherenkov and scintillation light, viewed by photomultiplier tubes

summary.plain: A tank holding about a third of a tonne of liquid xenon, with light sensors above and below it, in the Davis Cavern a mile underground in South Dakota. It looked for the flash of light from dark matter hitting a xenon nucleus.

detector:lz.name: LZ detector

specs.shielding: Liquid xenon skin veto, a gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer detector, and an 8 m × 6 m tank of 70,000 gallons of ultrapure water, under ~1480 m of rock.

subsystems.description: Dual-phase xenon TPC about 1.5 m in diameter and height with a 145.6 cm drift region, read out by 253 top and 241 bottom 3-inch Hamamatsu R11410 PMTs.
subsystems.name: Liquid xenon time projection chamber

subsystems.description: An instrumented layer of about 2 tonnes of liquid xenon outside the TPC field cage, read out by 131 1-inch and 2-inch PMTs, used to veto gamma rays that scatter in both volumes.
subsystems.name: Xenon skin veto

subsystems.description: Acrylic tanks of gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator surrounding the cryostat, viewed by 120 Hamamatsu R5912 8-inch PMTs, tagging neutrons by capture on gadolinium.
subsystems.name: Outer detector

subsystems.description: A tank 8 m in diameter and 6 m high holding 70,000 gallons of purified water, which contains the outer detector and cryostat and suppresses gamma rays and neutrons from the cavern rock.
subsystems.name: Water shield

summary.plain: A tank of seven tonnes of cold liquid xenon, watched by hundreds of light sensors, that records the tiny flash and spark made if a dark matter particle bumps into a xenon atom. Layers of xenon, scintillator and water around it screen out ordinary radiation.

detector:lz.technology: dual-phase (two-phase) liquid xenon time projection chamber

detector:mac.name: MAC detector

summary.plain: The MAC detector at PEP: a large calorimeter of magnetised iron and detecting layers around the collision point, designed to capture all the energy of the particles from each e+e- collision.

detector:mac.technology: Large solid-angle electromagnetic/hadronic calorimeter with magnetic charged-particle tracking, muon analysis and scintillator triggering

detector:mace.name: MACE 21 m telescope

specs.energy_range: Crab Nebula detected from 80 GeV to about 5 TeV; analysis threshold 80 GeV

summary.plain: A very large dish of 356 mirror panels that focuses the blue light of gamma-ray air showers onto a camera of 1088 light sensors, high in the Himalayas.

detector:mace.technology: 21 m quasi-parabolic imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope with a 1088-PMT camera.

intervals.label: data taking with the detector under construction
data taking with the full detector

detector:macro-detector.name: MACRO detector

summary.plain: A long, low building-sized array of scintillator tanks, streamer tubes and track-etch plastic that recorded muons crossing the Gran Sasso rock, 1989 to 2000.

detector:macro-detector.technology: Three sub-detectors in a modular (supermodule) structure: liquid-scintillator counters, limited streamer tubes and nuclear-track detectors, plus a rock absorber

detector:magic.name: MAGIC telescopes

summary.plain: Two 17-metre dish telescopes on a Spanish island mountaintop, working together to catch the flicker of blue light made by gamma rays hitting the atmosphere.

detector:magic.technology: Two 17 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes operated stereoscopically.

intervals.label: construction of the experiment at MESA

detector:magix.name: MAGIX spectrometers and gas-jet target (planned)

summary.plain: A thin gas jet inside the electron beam, two compact high-resolution magnetic spectrometers with tracking chambers and a silicon strip detector for the recoiling target particles.

detector:magix.technology: Two high-resolution magnetic spectrometers with advanced tracking detectors and a trigger/veto system around an internal gas-jet target

detector:mainz-neutrino-mass-detector.name: Mainz MAC-E-filter spectrometer with frozen tritium source

description: Frozen T2 source in a tilted solenoid, guiding solenoids, a vessel with 27 electrodes and a refocussing solenoid housing the detector
subsystems.name: Frozen T2 source and MAC-E filter

summary.plain: The Mainz spectrometer: a six-metre-long vacuum vessel with strong magnets and electrodes that lets only the highest-energy electrons from decaying tritium (frozen in a thin film) through to a detector.

detector:mainz-neutrino-mass-detector.technology: Electrostatic filter with magnetic adiabatic collimation (MAC-E filter) analysing the beta spectrum of a quench-condensed molecular-tritium film

detector:majorana-demonstrator.name: Majorana Demonstrator detector

isotope_mass.display: 40.4 kg total (27.2 kg enriched to ~88% in 76Ge)

summary.plain: Two modular arrays of ultra-pure germanium crystal detectors, kept in vacuum cryostats almost a mile underground in South Dakota, listening for a rare radioactive decay.

detector:majorana-demonstrator.technology: Modular arrays of high-purity germanium point-contact detectors in vacuum cryostats

detector:mark-i.name: Mark I detector

summary.plain: The Mark I (SLAC-LBL) detector at SPEAR: a solenoid magnet around the collision point with spark chambers, scintillators and shower counters that tracked and identified the particles from electron-positron collisions.

detector:mark-i.technology: Solenoidal magnetic spectrometer: 16 cylindrical magnetostrictive-wire spark chambers, scintillator time-of-flight counters, lead-scintillator shower counters and an iron flux return with muon spark chambers

summary.plain: The Mark II detector: a solenoidal general-purpose detector that moved from SPEAR to PEP and then to the SLC, where it was the first detector to see Z boson decays at a linear collider.
The Mark III detector at SPEAR, the third general-purpose detector there, built to study D mesons and charmonium decays.
The MARK J particle detector at one of the four collision regions of DESY's PETRA ring, used to measure how the energy of e+e- collisions was shared among the produced particles.

detector:meg.name: MEG detector

summary.plain: A detector combining a tank of liquid xenon (to catch a gamma ray) with a tracking chamber (to catch a positron) at the Paul Scherrer Institute, looking for both particles appearing together from a single muon decay.

detector:meg.technology: Liquid xenon calorimeter for the gamma ray, combined with a drift chamber and timing counter spectrometer for the positron, on the PSI DC muon beamline

detector:meg-ii.name: MEG II detector

summary.plain: The upgraded version of the MEG detector: a finer liquid-xenon calorimeter and new tracking and timing detectors, at the same Swiss laboratory, still taking data.

detector:meg-ii.technology: Upgraded liquid xenon calorimeter with finer granularity, a new single-volume cylindrical drift chamber, upgraded timing counter and a new radiative decay counter, on the same PSI DC muon beamline

detector:microboone.name: MicroBooNE detector

summary.plain: A 170-tonne tank of liquid argon on the Booster neutrino beam at Fermilab that photographs neutrino collisions in three dimensions with wires instead of film. It was built to check a puzzling excess of events seen by an earlier experiment.

detector:microboone.technology: single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber

detector:milagro.name: Milagro water-Cherenkov pond and outriggers

description: An outrigger array of water tanks, instrumented with 8-inch PMTs, surrounding the central reservoir.
subsystems.name: Outrigger tank array

summary.plain: A covered pond of purified water lined with 723 light sensors in two layers, plus a ring of outlying water tanks, that sensed the faint blue flashes from air showers.

detector:milagro.technology: Water-Cherenkov air-shower array: a covered 60 m x 80 m x 8 m pond with 723 PMTs in two layers, plus an outrigger array of water tanks.

detector:mimac.name: MIMAC bi-chamber micro-TPC module

summary.plain: MIMAC is a French dark matter experiment in the Modane underground laboratory. Its low-pressure gas chambers record the three-dimensional track of the nucleus a particle knocks, aiming to show which direction a dark matter particle came from. In 2026 it published its first directional limit.

detector:mimac.technology: Low-pressure (30 mbar) gaseous micro-TPC with pixelated Micromegas anode and fast self-triggered electronics

detector:minerva.name: MINERvA detector

subsystems.description: planes of graphite, iron and lead interleaved between tracking planes upstream of the scintillator tracker
subsystems.name: Passive nuclear targets

summary.plain: A compact, finely sliced detector sitting just in front of the MINOS near detector at Fermilab. Layers of graphite, iron, lead and water let it compare how neutrinos bounce off different kinds of atomic nucleus.

detector:minerva.technology: finely segmented scintillator-strip tracker with electromagnetic and hadronic sampling calorimetry and passive nuclear targets

detector:miniboone.name: MiniBooNE detector

summary.plain: A 12-metre sphere holding 818 tonnes of clear mineral oil, watched by 1,520 light sensors, 541 metres from where Fermilab makes its Booster neutrino beam. Flashes of light reveal the particles a neutrino leaves behind.

detector:miniboone.technology: spherical mineral-oil Cherenkov and scintillation detector viewed by photomultiplier tubes

detector:miniclean.name: MiniCLEAN detector

summary.plain: MiniCLEAN was a 500 kg detector of liquid argon (or liquid neon) in the Cube Hall at SNOLAB, Canada, built to test a simple single-phase way of hunting for WIMP dark matter. A cold-gas test run took place in 2017 and SNOLAB reports decommissioning began in 2019. No dark matter result was published.

detector:miniclean.technology: Single-phase liquid argon (or neon) scintillation detector with PMTs in the cryogen

subsystems.description: 486 octagonal steel-scintillator planes arranged in two supermodules
subsystems.name: Octagonal planes

summary.plain: A 5,400-tonne stack of 486 eight-sided steel and plastic plates, magnetised so it could tell neutrinos from antineutrinos, sitting 705 metres underground in an old Minnesota iron mine 735 kilometres from the beam.

The 980-tonne little sister of the MINOS far detector, in a cavern 100 metres below Fermilab about a kilometre from where the neutrino beam is born. It recorded the beam before any neutrinos had changed type.

detector:moedal.name: MoEDAL detector

summary.plain: MoEDAL's detector is mostly passive: 125 stacks of special plastic sheets that record the tracks of heavily-charged particles, plus about a tonne of metal to trap and hold onto anything unusual.

detector:moedal.technology: passive Nuclear Track Detector (NTD) stacks plus paramagnetic trapping volumes and TimePix pixel monitors

detector:moller.name: MOLLER apparatus

summary.plain: The apparatus being installed in Hall A: a long liquid-hydrogen target, two sets of toroidal magnets that focus scattered electrons into a ring, and quartz detectors that measure the light they produce.

detector:moller.technology: Toroidal-magnet spectrometer with fused-silica Cherenkov detectors measuring the integrated Møller-electron flux per beam-helicity state

detector:mpd.name: MPD detector

summary.plain: A cylindrical detector built inside a large superconducting solenoid, with a gas-filled tracking chamber, time-of-flight walls and calorimeters, to follow the thousands of particles produced when two heavy ions collide at NICA.

detector:mpd.technology: Solenoidal general-purpose heavy-ion detector with a central time projection chamber, time-of-flight and calorimetry

detector:mu2e.name: Mu2e detector

summary.plain: A 25-metre chain of giant superconducting magnets at Fermilab, with a tracker and a fast crystal detector at the end, built to catch the single electron that would appear if a muon ever turned into one.

detector:mu2e.technology: A 25-metre chain of three superconducting solenoids (production, transport, detector) feeding a straw-tube tracker and a fast CsI crystal calorimeter, surrounded by a cosmic-ray veto

detector:mu3e.name: Mu3e detector

summary.plain: A very thin, high-speed silicon camera built from custom pixel chips, combined with fast timing detectors, being assembled at the Paul Scherrer Institute to catch three particles flying apart from a single muon.

detector:mu3e.technology: Ultra-thin silicon pixel tracker built from high-voltage monolithic active pixel sensors (HV-MAPS), combined with scintillating-fibre and scintillating-tile timing detectors

detector:mulan.name: MuLan detector and muon beamline

summary.plain: A ball of fast plastic scintillator tiles around a target where muons stopped, recording when each muon decay produced a positron.

detector:mulan.technology: Segmented, fast-timing plastic scintillator array around a stopping target with a time-structured muon beam

detector:muon-g-2.name: Muon g-2 storage ring

summary.plain: A 14-metre ring of superconducting magnet, originally built at Brookhaven and moved to Fermilab, that holds spinning muons in a very uniform magnetic field while detectors around its rim watch them wobble.

detector:muon-g-2.technology: Superconducting superferric muon storage ring with 24 electromagnetic calorimeter stations and straw tracking detectors around its circumference

detector:muse.name: MUSE spectrometer and liquid hydrogen target

summary.plain: A liquid-hydrogen target in a vacuum chamber with a large set of detectors around it that track the electrons and muons scattered by the protons.

detector:muse.technology: Large-solid-angle, non-magnetic spectrometer detecting beam particles scattering from a liquid hydrogen cell in a vacuum chamber

detector:n2edm.name: n2EDM spectrometer

summary.plain: Two storage chambers stacked one above the other, inside a room shielded from magnetic fields and surrounded by active compensation coils, in which ultracold neutron spins precess in electric fields of opposite direction.

detector:n2edm.technology: Two vertically stacked ultracold-neutron storage chambers inside a magnetically shielded room with an active magnetic shield

detector:na34-helios.name: HELIOS spectrometer and calorimeters

summary.plain: A set of calorimeters wrapped nearly all the way around the target, with silicon trackers and spectrometers, that measured the energy and particles flying out of ion collisions.

detector:na34-helios.technology: Near-4-pi uranium-scintillator and uranium-liquid-argon calorimetry with silicon detectors, drift chambers, a hadron spectrometer, photon detectors and a muon spectrometer

detector:na35.name: NA35 streamer chamber and calorimeters

detector:na35.technology: Streamer chamber in a 1.5 T vertical magnetic field followed by four calorimeters

detector:na38.name: NA38 dimuon spectrometer and calorimeter

summary.plain: A muon spectrometer with a ring-shaped magnet, plus a calorimeter and a multi-layer uranium target, that recorded pairs of muons from ion collisions at very high beam rates.

detector:na38.technology: Dimuon spectrometer (air-core toroidal magnet, multiwire proportional chambers, scintillator hodoscopes) with an electromagnetic calorimeter and a multiple active target

detector:na44.technology: Focusing magnetic spectrometer with a threshold imaging Cherenkov counter (CsI photocathodes) and time-of-flight for pi/K separation
