summary.plain: A set of ring-imaging Cherenkov counters and silicon trackers placed behind the target to pick out rare electron-positron pairs among overwhelming backgrounds, later upgraded with a radial-drift chamber.

detector:na45-ceres.technology: Two ring-imaging Cherenkov detectors with silicon drift tracking (later a radial-drift TPC) for electron-pair detection

detector:na48.name: NA48 detector

summary.plain: The NA48 detector combined a magnetic spectrometer and a calorimeter to track and measure kaon decay particles in an underground hall at CERN, confirming that CP violation happens directly in kaon decay.

detector:na48.technology: Magnetic spectrometer (helium-filled tank with two drift chambers either side of a dipole magnet) plus liquid-krypton electromagnetic calorimeter, used to reconstruct KL/KS → 2 pion decays

detector:na49.name: NA49 detector

summary.plain: A large set of gas-filled tracking chambers, two inside superconducting magnets, that recorded most of the charged particles produced in a lead-lead collision.

detector:na49.technology: Large-acceptance hadron spectrometer with Time Projection Chambers in superconducting dipole magnets

detector:na50.name: NA50 apparatus

summary.plain: A muon spectrometer behind a lead target with detectors that measure how central each collision is, so physicists could compare J/psi production with the expected normal absorption.

detector:na50.technology: Muon spectrometer with centrality detectors and a hadron absorber

detector:na57.name: NA57 pixel telescope

summary.plain: A silicon pixel telescope entirely made of pixel detectors (about a million channels) placed near the target in the Goliath magnet, imaging the tracks of strange particles from lead-lead collisions.

detector:na57.technology: Pixel telescope of about one million channels in the Goliath magnet

detector:na60.name: NA60 apparatus

summary.plain: A silicon vertex telescope right behind the target and a muon spectrometer, giving a very accurate measurement of the masses of muon pairs produced in collisions.

detector:na60.technology: Muon spectrometer coupled to a silicon-pixel vertex telescope

detector:na61-shine.name: NA61/SHINE spectrometer

summary.plain: A large detector built around four gas-filled tracking chambers, two of them inside superconducting magnets, plus time-of-flight walls and a calorimeter that measures the spectators of each collision, inherited largely from NA49.

detector:na61-shine.technology: Large-acceptance spectrometer of four Time Projection Chambers in superconducting magnets with time-of-flight walls and a projectile spectator calorimeter

subsystems.name: GigaTracker

detector:na62.technology: Decay-in-flight kaon spectrometer: beam-tracking (GigaTracker), ring-imaging Cherenkov (RICH) particle identification, liquid-krypton (LKr) electromagnetic calorimeter and photon/particle veto systems around a large vacuum vessel

detector:na64.name: NA64 detector

summary.plain: The NA64 detector tags and tracks incoming electrons, absorbs their energy in a calorimeter, and watches for cases where energy simply vanishes -- a possible sign of an invisible dark-sector particle.

detector:na64.technology: Active beam-dump / missing-energy spectrometer: incoming electron tagged and tracked, its energy deposited in an electromagnetic calorimeter, with hermetic veto systems to catch any visible secondary particles so that missing energy signals an invisible decay

detector:nab.name: Nab spectrometer and silicon detectors

summary.plain: A long magnetic spectrometer in which the electron and proton from each neutron decay are guided to two large silicon detectors, one measuring the electron energy and the other the proton arrival time.

detector:nab.technology: Long asymmetric spectrometer guiding the decay electron and proton to two large-area silicon detectors

detector:naiad.name: NaIAD detector

summary.plain: NaIAD was an array of sodium iodide crystals in the Boulby mine in north-east England that searched for dark matter from 2000 to 2003. It saw no dark matter and, for a time, set the tightest limits on dark matter that interacts through spin.

detector:naiad.technology: Array of NaI(Tl) scintillating crystals with pulse shape discrimination

detector:nd.name: ND detector

detector:nd.technology: Scintillation electromagnetic calorimeter of 168 rectangular NaI(Tl) counters arranged in four layers around the interaction region

detector:nd280.technology: Magnetized off-axis tracking detector: a water/brass Pi-Zero Detector (P0D), three gaseous time projection chambers and two fine-grained scintillator detectors as the tracker, surrounded by an electromagnetic calorimeter, all inside the recycled UA1 dipole magnet instrumented as a side muon range detector (SMRD).

detector:nedm-sns.name: nEDM@SNS apparatus

summary.plain: Two identical liquid-helium-filled cells in a strong electric field, where neutrons are cooled to ultracold energies, stored, and watched through flashes of light for a tiny change in how their spins turn.

detector:nemo-3-detector.name: NEMO-3 detector

summary.plain: A drum of thin foils holding the decaying atoms, ringed by thousands of gas-filled tracking cells and blocks of plastic scintillator. It sees each electron's path and energy, so it can tell a real decay from background.

detector:nemo-3-detector.technology: Thin double-beta source foils surrounded by a gaseous tracking detector of open drift cells operating in Geiger mode and a calorimeter of plastic scintillators, inside a solenoid and a low-radioactivity shield

detector:neutrino-4-detector.technology: Gd-doped (0.1 %) liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector divided into 50 sections, movable on rails, with active muon veto

detector:oscura.name: Oscura skipper-CCD array (10 kg)

summary.plain: A planned array of silicon CCD sensors that can count single electrons, kept cold in liquid nitrogen inside heavy shielding.

detector:oscura.technology: Skipper-CCD silicon array with sub-electron readout noise

summary.plain: Small test strings of light and water sensors lowered into the deep Pacific to check the water and prove the technology before the full P-ONE telescope is built.

detector:p-one.technology: Deep-sea water Cherenkov pathfinder mooring lines instrumenting optical background and water-property measurements ahead of the full P-ONE array

detector:p2-mesa.name: P2 apparatus (planned)

summary.plain: A solenoid-based spectrometer with Cherenkov detectors, tracking detectors and precision polarimetry that will measure the scattering of polarised electrons from hydrogen.

detector:p2-mesa.technology: Parity-violating electron scattering facility with spectrometer and precision polarimetry at MESA

detector:padme.name: PADME detector

summary.plain: The PADME detector at the Beam Test Facility: a thin active diamond target hit by the positron beam, a dipole magnet with veto counters for charged particles, and a calorimeter of 616 bismuth germanate crystals recycled from the L3 experiment at LEP.

detector:padme.technology: Active polycrystalline diamond target in vacuum, charged-particle vetoes in a dipole magnet, BGO electromagnetic calorimeter, small-angle calorimeter and TimePix3 beam monitor

detector:palo-verde-detector.name: Palo Verde detector

summary.plain: A grid of 66 long transparent cells filled with gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator, surrounded by buffers and a muon veto, in a shallow underground room near the reactors.

detector:palo-verde-detector.technology: Segmented Gd-loaded liquid-scintillator detector (66 acrylic cells) with oil and water buffers and an active muon veto

intervals.label: construction (detector components being built and deployed)

detector:panda.name: PANDA detector (planned)

summary.plain: A two-part detector around the antiproton beam: a solenoid-based target spectrometer surrounding the interaction point and a dipole forward spectrometer, for almost full solid-angle coverage with good particle identification.

detector:panda.technology: Internal-target antiproton detector at the HESR with target and forward spectrometers

summary.plain: A tank of liquid xenon -- six tonnes in total, four tonnes of it the active target -- that records flashes of light from particles hitting xenon nuclei, deep under a mountain in China.

detector:pandax-i.name: PandaX-I detector

summary.plain: PandaX-I was the first stage of the Chinese PandaX liquid xenon dark matter programme, in the Jinping underground laboratory in Sichuan. It ran for about five months in 2014 with a few tens of kilograms of xenon, saw no dark matter, and ruled out several low-mass claims.

detector:pandax-i.technology: Low-threshold dual-phase liquid xenon time projection chamber

detector:pandax-ii.name: PandaX-II detector

summary.plain: PandaX-II was the second stage of the Chinese PandaX programme: a half-tonne liquid xenon detector in the Jinping underground laboratory, running from 2016 to 2019. It saw no dark matter and, in 2016-2017, set the strongest limits then published.

detector:pandax-ii.technology: Dual-phase liquid xenon time projection chamber (500 kg)

detector:pandax-iii-detector.name: PandaX-III TPC

summary.plain: A steel vessel holding xenon gas at ten times atmospheric pressure, with a plane of tiny gas-amplifier modules at each end that image the tracks of electrons from a decay.

detector:pandax-iii-detector.technology: High-pressure gaseous xenon time projection chamber with thermal-bonding Micromegas charge-readout modules; tracks of the two electrons give topological background rejection

detector:pandax-xt.name: PandaX-xT detector

summary.plain: PandaX-xT is a proposed multi-ten-tonne liquid xenon observatory at the Jinping underground laboratory in China, an upgrade of PandaX-4T. It would search for dark matter and for neutrinoless double beta decay, and aims to reach the point where neutrinos become the main background.

detector:pandax-xt.technology: Multi-ten-tonne dual-phase liquid xenon time projection chamber (proposed)

summary.plain: The PEN detector stopped pions in a target and recorded the positrons from the two possible decay routes with a large calorimeter.

detector:pep-4-tpc.name: PEP-4 TPC detector

summary.plain: The PEP-4 time projection chamber: a gas-filled cylinder two metres long that records the ionisation trails of charged particles as three-dimensional images and identifies them by how much energy they lose.

detector:pep-4-tpc.technology: Time projection chamber: 2 m long cylinder in 80% argon / 20% methane gas at 8.5 atm with a central cathode at -75 kV, six end-cap sectors with multiwire proportional chambers and a solenoidal field

detector:perkeo-iii.name: PERKEO III spectrometer

summary.plain: An eight-metre magnet system in which the electrons and protons from neutron decays are guided to two detectors, with a pulsed neutron beam that lets the background be measured under the same conditions as the signal.

detector:perkeo-iii.technology: Magnetic spectrometer transporting electrons and protons from neutron decay to two detector systems in a symmetric set-up with almost 4π acceptance

detector:phenix.name: PHENIX detector

summary.plain: A multi-armed particle detector at Brookhaven's RHIC collider that tracked and identified particles from nuclear collisions between 2000 and 2016.

detector:phenix.technology: Multi-arm spectrometer combining central-arm tracking/calorimetry at midrapidity with forward/backward muon-arm spectrometers, each with its own magnet

detector:phobos.name: PHOBOS detector

summary.plain: A compact detector made of many silicon sensors around the collision point, which counted nearly all the charged particles and their directions, with two small magnetic spectrometers for a detailed look at a small fraction.

detector:phobos.technology: Silicon multiplicity detectors surrounding the interaction region with two high-quality magnetic spectrometers

detector:picasso.name: PICASSO superheated droplet detectors

summary.plain: Cylindrical gel-filled modules holding droplets of a fluorine-rich liquid (C4F10); the final set had 32 modules in water shielding at SNOLAB.

detector:picasso.technology: Superheated C4F10 droplet detectors with acoustic (piezoelectric) readout

detector:pico-2l.name: PICO-2L bubble chamber

summary.plain: A two-litre jar of superheated C3F8 refrigerant, filmed by cameras and listened to by microphones, deep underground.

detector:pico-2l.technology: Superheated C3F8 bubble chamber (fused-silica jar, bellows, cameras, piezoelectric acoustic sensors)

detector:pico-40l.name: PICO-40L bubble chamber

summary.plain: A bubble chamber with two nested quartz jars, upright above its bellows so that no water touches the dark-matter target; cameras and microphones record each bubble.

detector:pico-40l.technology: Right-side-up superheated C3F8 bubble chamber with two nested quartz jars, bellows and a temperature-graded thermal system

intervals.label: assembly and construction at SNOLAB (Cube Hall)

detector:pico-500.name: PICO-500 bubble chamber

summary.plain: A large upright bubble chamber, about 250 litres of superheated C3F8 in a quartz vessel, being built inside SNOLAB's Cube Hall.

detector:pico-500.technology: Right-side-up superheated C3F8 bubble chamber in a synthetic quartz vessel

C3F8 first blind exposure (1167 kg-days at 3.3 keV)

detector:pico-60.name: PICO-60 bubble chamber

summary.plain: A 30-cm-wide, 1-m-tall silica jar of superheated liquid (CF3I, then C3F8) in a water tank, watched by cameras and microphones for the tell-tale bubble of a dark matter collision.

detector:pico-60.technology: Superheated bubble chamber (CF3I, later C3F8) in a synthetic fused-silica jar with water buffer, stereoscopic cameras and piezoelectric acoustic sensors

low-background measurements in the KamLAND area of the Kamioka underground laboratory

detector:picolon.name: PICOLON NaI(Tl) detector

summary.plain: PICOLON is a Japanese search for dark matter with ultra-pure sodium iodide crystals, measured so far with a small crystal deep in the Kamioka mine. It aims to test the yearly signal reported by DAMA/LIBRA with crystals as clean as DAMA's, and plans a 250 kg detector.

detector:picolon.technology: Ultra-pure NaI(Tl) crystal read by a low-background PMT in a lead and copper shield

summary.plain: A stack of scintillators and wire chambers that stops pions, with a very large crystal calorimeter that measures the energies of the positrons from the two decay routes.

detector:pierre-auger-observatory.name: Pierre Auger Observatory hybrid detector

description: Array of 1660 water-Cherenkov detector tanks spread over 3000 km², sampling the particle density of extensive air showers at ground level.
subsystems.name: Surface Detector (SD)

description: 27 optical telescopes in four buildings overlooking the surface array, imaging the ultraviolet fluorescence light emitted by nitrogen molecules excited along an air shower's path through the atmosphere.
subsystems.name: Fluorescence Detector (FD)

summary.plain: A two-in-one detector: 1660 tanks of water spread over 3000 square kilometres sense particles from cosmic-ray showers reaching the ground, while 27 telescopes watch the same showers develop as faint ultraviolet flashes in the night sky.

detector:pierre-auger-observatory.technology: Hybrid detector: a surface array of water-Cherenkov tanks sampling air-shower particles at ground level, cross-checked by fluorescence telescopes imaging ultraviolet light from the shower's longitudinal development.

intervals.label: proposal to the PSI programme advisory committee

detector:pioneer.name: PIONEER detector (planned)

summary.plain: A planned detector with a silicon-sensor target that stops the pions and a large calorimeter around it that measures the decay positrons.

detector:pioneer.technology: Active target using Low Gain Avalanche Detectors combined with a calorimeter using liquid xenon or LYSO crystals

intervals.label: PLUTO removed from PETRA; replaced by CELLO

summary.plain: The PLUTO particle detector, moved from DESY's DORIS ring to a PETRA collision region in 1978.

detector:polarbear.name: Huan Tran Telescope and POLARBEAR receivers

summary.plain: A 2.5-metre telescope in the Chilean Andes with a succession of cameras, first POLARBEAR and then the three-telescope Simons Array, that measured the polarization of the Big Bang afterglow on small angular scales.

detector:polarbear.technology: 2.5 m off-axis Gregorian telescope (Huan Tran Telescope) with antenna-coupled TES bolometer receivers: POLARBEAR-1 (1274 bolometers, 150 GHz) and POLARBEAR-2 (95 and 150 GHz).

detector:prad.name: PRad apparatus

summary.plain: A windowless hydrogen gas target, a large hybrid calorimeter and two fine-grained gas detectors, set up 5.5 metres downstream so they could see electrons scattered at tiny angles with no magnet in the way.

detector:prad.technology: Magnetic-spectrometer-free setup: windowless hydrogen gas flow target, HyCal hybrid electromagnetic calorimeter and two GEM coordinate detectors

detector:prex.name: PREX apparatus

summary.plain: The Hall A set-up used for PREX: a thin lead target in the electron beam and two high-resolution spectrometers that picked out the electrons scattered elastically at a small angle.

detector:prex.technology: Hall A high-resolution spectrometers with a lead target for parity-violating elastic electron scattering

detector:project-8.name: Project 8 CRES apparatus

summary.plain: A small tabletop instrument built at the University of Washington that catches the faint radio hum a single electron makes as it spirals in a magnetic field, the first step toward weighing the neutrino this way.

detector:project-8.technology: Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES): single-electron microwave radiometry in a magnetic trap

detector:prospect-antineutrino-detector.name: PROSPECT antineutrino detector

summary.plain: A movable tank of liquid scintillator divided into a grid of 154 long cells, read out by photomultiplier tubes at both ends, which records antineutrinos from the reactor at several distances.

detector:prospect-antineutrino-detector.technology: Segmented 6Li-doped liquid scintillator with double-ended PMT readout and pulse-shape discrimination

intervals.label: operation in the NP02 cryostat at the CERN Neutrino Platform

detector:protodune-dp.name: ProtoDUNE-DP

summary.plain: The second DUNE prototype at CERN. It tested a design in which the electron signal is amplified in a thin layer of argon gas above the liquid, allowing a much longer drift.

detector:protodune-dp.technology: dual-phase liquid argon time projection chamber with a single homogeneous drift volume and charge amplification in the gas phase

subsystems.name: Cosmic-ray tagger

summary.plain: A full-height prototype of the DUNE far detector, built at CERN and exposed to a test beam of known particles from 2018 to 2020. It showed that the design works before the real detectors were built in South Dakota.

detector:protodune-sp.technology: single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber, a full-height prototype of the DUNE single-phase far detector module

summary.plain: A xenon gas jet inside the storage ring and a chain of detectors downstream that recognised the unique signature of an antihydrogen atom.

detector:psi-nedm.name: nEDM apparatus at PSI

summary.plain: A storage chamber for ultracold neutrons in a very uniform magnetic field with electrodes, plus mercury and caesium magnetometers that track field changes while the neutrons’ spins precess.

detector:psi-nedm.technology: Single-chamber Ramsey spectrometer with a Hg-199 co-magnetometer and an array of optically pumped caesium magnetometers

summary.plain: A transportable two-part trap for antiprotons and exotic nuclei, surrounded by particle detectors that record what comes out when they annihilate.

detector:qweak.name: Qweak apparatus

summary.plain: A custom set-up in Hall C: a long liquid-hydrogen target, a toroidal magnet and quartz detectors that counted the electrons scattered from protons for each beam-spin direction.

detector:qweak.technology: Custom apparatus installed in Hall C: liquid-hydrogen target and spectrometer measuring the parity-violating asymmetry in elastic electron-proton scattering

detector:reno.name: RENO detectors

summary.plain: Two identical tank-like detectors near and far from South Korea's Hanbit nuclear reactors, watching for antineutrinos. Data taking ran from 2011 to 2023.

detector:reno.technology: Two identical gadolinium-doped liquid-scintillator antineutrino detectors

detector:ricochet-cryocube.name: Ricochet CryoCube (Ge/Zn cryogenic calorimeter array)

summary.plain: A set of ultra-cold germanium and zinc crystals, weighing from a few dozen grams (in the test module now running) up to a planned kilogram scale, designed to catch reactor antineutrinos nudging whole atomic nuclei.

detector:ricochet-cryocube.technology: cryogenic heat-and-ionization germanium and zinc calorimeters (CryoCube)

detector:rno-g.name: RNO-G stations

subsystems.description: Three boreholes per station (a power string carrying the phased-array trigger antennas, plus two helper strings), holding 15 receiving antennas in total, down to ~100 m below the surface

summary.plain: Stations of buried and surface radio antennas, spaced more than a kilometre apart on the Greenland ice sheet, listening for the radio crackle of the highest-energy neutrinos.

detector:rno-g.technology: In-ice radio antenna stations: each with three strings of antennas ~100 m deep in the firn plus surface antennas, detecting the Askaryan radio pulse from neutrino-induced showers in ice

detector:rosebud.name: ROSEBUD bolometers

summary.plain: ROSEBUD was a set of tiny crystals cooled to a few hundredths of a degree above absolute zero, in the Canfranc underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees, built to catch the faint heat from dark matter particles hitting aluminium, oxygen or germanium nuclei. It mainly tested detector materials and cut backgrounds.

detector:rosebud.technology: Low-temperature (20 mK) bolometers with NTD-Ge thermistors: sapphire and germanium absorbers, then scintillating CaWO4, BGO and LiF absorbers with a light channel

detector:sabre-north.name: SABRE North detector array

summary.plain: SABRE North is the Italian half of a twin pair of sodium-iodide dark matter detectors, being built at the Gran Sasso laboratory. It will use ultra-pure crystals of the same material as DAMA/LIBRA to test, with lower background, the yearly signal DAMA/LIBRA reports. Its twin, SABRE South, is in Australia.

detector:sabre-north.technology: Ultra-high-purity NaI(Tl) crystals (grown from zone-refined powder) read out by photomultiplier tubes, in a passive copper and polyethylene shield

intervals.label: proposal (twin NaI(Tl) detectors at LNGS and SUPL)
installation and assembly of SABRE South in SUPL

detector:sabre-south.name: SABRE South detector

summary.plain: SABRE South is the Australian half of a twin pair of sodium-iodide dark matter detectors, being assembled 1 km underground in the Stawell gold mine, Victoria. Being in the Southern Hemisphere helps tell a real dark matter signal from seasonal effects, when tested against DAMA/LIBRA's yearly signal. Its twin, SABRE North, is in Italy.

detector:sabre-south.technology: Ultra-high-purity NaI(Tl) crystals read by photomultipliers inside a linear-alkylbenzene liquid-scintillator veto and a plastic-scintillator muon veto

detector:sage.name: SAGE gallium target

summary.plain: Tonnes of liquid gallium metal, deep in a Russian mountain, that solar neutrinos occasionally turn into germanium, which scientists then extract and count.

detector:sage.technology: Radiochemical gallium detector: solar neutrinos capture on 71Ga to produce 71Ge via inverse beta decay in liquid gallium metal, which is chemically extracted and counted in periodic campaigns

detector:sbc-lar10.name: SBC-LAr10

summary.plain: A 10-kg test chamber of superheated liquid argon in the MINOS tunnel at Fermilab, used to measure how argon responds to very small recoils.

detector:sbc-lar10.technology: Scintillating liquid-argon bubble chamber (LAr doped with Xe) with SiPM light readout, cameras and piezoelectric sensors

detector:sbc-snolab.name: SBC-SNOLAB

summary.plain: The cleaner twin of SBC-LAr10, a 10-kg superheated liquid-argon chamber being built for SNOLAB to search for light dark matter.

detector:sbc-snolab.technology: Scintillating liquid-argon bubble chamber (LAr with ~10 ppm Xe, 48 FBK VUV SiPMs, two quartz jars, liquid CF4 as hydraulic fluid)

detector:sbnd.name: SBND detector

summary.plain: A 112-tonne liquid argon camera only 110 metres from where Fermilab makes its Booster neutrino beam. Being so close, it sees about 7,000 neutrinos a day, more than any similar detector.

detector:sbnd.technology: single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber

intervals.label: Super Charm-Tau factory project at BINP

detector:sctf.name: SCTF universal magnetic detector (conceptual design)

summary.plain: The conceptual SCTF detector: a universal magnetic detector with an inner tracker, a drift chamber, aerogel Cherenkov particle identification and a calorimeter, designed for a collision rate of 300 to 400 kHz.

detector:sctf.technology: Universal magnetic detector with high momentum resolution for charged particles, high photon energy resolution and record particle identification

detector:sdss-2-5m-telescope.name: Sloan Foundation 2.5-m telescope

summary.plain: The dedicated 2.5-metre telescope at Apache Point, New Mexico, with a very wide 3-degree field of view, used for every phase of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey.

detector:sdss-2-5m-telescope.technology: 2.5-m f/5 modified Ritchey-Chrétien altitude-azimuth telescope with a 3-degree distortion-free field of view.

detector:seaquest.name: SeaQuest spectrometer

summary.plain: The SeaQuest spectrometer used magnets and tracking detectors to catch pairs of muons produced when a proton beam struck hydrogen, deuterium and other targets, revealing the makeup of the proton's antiquark sea.

detector:seaquest.technology: Muon spectrometer: a target system followed by two dipole magnets and four detector stations (hodoscopes and tracking chambers) with an FPGA-based trigger, identifying oppositely-charged dimuon pairs from the Drell-Yan process

detector:sensei.name: SENSEI Skipper-CCD detector

summary.plain: A tiny silicon chip called a skipper CCD, sensitive enough to count single electrons, sitting in a shielded underground hall at Fermilab to catch the faint signal of a very light dark matter particle.

detector:sensei.technology: Skipper charge-coupled device (CCD): a high-resistivity silicon CCD with sub-electron readout noise, counting individual ionization electrons

detector:ship.name: SHiP detector

summary.plain: The planned SHiP detector: a beam-dump target, a muon shield, an empty decay volume, and a spectrometer, built to catch the decays of hypothetical new particles that could otherwise pass through matter unnoticed.

detector:ship.technology: High-intensity proton beam-dump on a heavy target, followed by a muon shield, a large vacuum decay volume and a downstream spectrometer/calorimeter system to reconstruct decays of feebly interacting long-lived particles

detector:siddharta.name: SIDDHARTA set-up

summary.plain: The SIDDHARTA set-up at DAΦNE: 144 silicon drift detectors timed against the kaon pair produced in each phi decay, around a cryogenic gas target, replacing DEAR's untimed CCD cameras.

detector:siddharta.technology: Array of 144 silicon drift X-ray detectors recording signal amplitudes with timing information

intervals.label: DAΦNE data taking (SIDDHARTINO pilot run, then SIDDHARTA-2)

detector:siddharta-2.name: SIDDHARTA-2 apparatus

summary.plain: The SIDDHARTA-2 apparatus at DAΦNE: a cryogenic gas target surrounded by silicon drift X-ray detectors, triggered by the kaon pair from each phi decay, built to measure X-rays from kaonic deuterium and other kaonic atoms.

detector:siddharta-2.technology: Cryogenic gaseous target surrounded by silicon drift X-ray detectors (SDD)

detector:simons-observatory.name: Simons Observatory telescopes (LAT and SATs)

summary.plain: One six-metre telescope and three half-metre telescopes on a Chilean mountain, carrying about 98,000 detectors that map the Big Bang afterglow far more deeply than earlier ground-based instruments.

detector:simons-observatory.technology: One 6 m Large Aperture Telescope and three 0.5 m Small Aperture Telescopes with transition-edge-sensor bolometer cameras in six frequency bands.

detector:simonyi-survey-telescope-lsst-c.name: Simonyi Survey Telescope and LSST Camera

summary.plain: An 8.4-metre telescope with a very short, wide view and a 3.2-gigapixel camera, built to photograph the entire visible southern sky every few nights.

detector:simonyi-survey-telescope-lsst-c.technology: 8.4 m reflecting survey telescope with a 3.5-degree field of view covering a 64 cm diameter flat focal plane, carrying the 3.2-gigapixel LSST Camera.

detector:simple.name: SIMPLE superheated droplet detectors

summary.plain: Small bottles of gel holding droplets of a freon liquid (C2ClF5), sunk in a shielded water pool; each bubble that forms is recorded by microphones.

detector:simple.technology: Superheated C2ClF5 droplet detectors with acoustic readout

detector:slac-e158.name: E158 apparatus

summary.plain: A 1.57-metre liquid-hydrogen target, a magnetic spectrometer that sorts scattered electrons along a 60-metre line, and a calorimeter that measures the energy flow of the target-electron scatters for each beam pulse.

detector:slac-e158.technology: Liquid-hydrogen target, magnetic spectrometer/collimator system and a copper/fused-silica fibre sandwich calorimeter integrating the response per beam pulse

detector:sld.name: SLD detector

summary.plain: A particle detector at SLAC built around the collision point of the SLC accelerator, with a precise silicon vertex detector and a ring-imaging Cherenkov detector to identify particle types.

detector:sld.technology: CCD pixel vertex detector, drift-chamber tracking, Cherenkov ring-imaging particle identification, projective-tower calorimetry and a muon tracking system

detector:snd.name: SND detector

summary.plain: The SND detector: three layers of sodium iodide crystals shaped into a sphere around the collision point, with drift chambers inside and muon counters outside.

detector:snd.technology: Three-layer spherical NaI(Tl) calorimeter of 1632 crystals (13.5 radiation lengths, 3.6 t) with inner cylindrical drift chambers and an outer muon/veto system

detector:snd-lhc.name: SND@LHC detector

summary.plain: The SND@LHC detector sits in a disused CERN tunnel opposite FASER, built to catch neutrinos and rare particles from LHC collisions. It operated from 2022 until the LHC's current maintenance shutdown began in 2026.

detector:snd-lhc.technology: Hybrid emulsion/electronic-tracker target (tungsten plates) acting as an electromagnetic calorimeter, followed by a hadronic calorimeter and a muon identification system

detector:sno.name: SNO detector

description: An array of proportional counters strung through the heavy water in phase 3 to independently detect the neutral-current reaction via neutron capture
subsystems.name: Neutral Current Detector (NCD) array

summary.plain: A 12-metre acrylic ball full of heavy water, watched by 9,600 light sensors, sitting two kilometres underground in a Canadian mine.

detector:sno.technology: 12 m diameter acrylic vessel holding 1000 t of heavy water (D2O), viewed by 9600 photomultiplier tubes on a geodesic support structure, submerged in ordinary water inside a 2039 m deep rock cavity

detector:sno-plus.name: SNO+ detector

summary.plain: The same 12-metre acrylic ball that once held SNO's heavy water, now filled with liquid scintillator, watching for solar neutrinos, reactor antineutrinos, and a hoped-for rare nuclear decay.

detector:sno-plus.technology: The original SNO 12 m acrylic vessel, photomultiplier tubes and PMT support structure, filled first with ultrapure water and now with liquid scintillator

detector:solid-detector.name: SoLid detector

summary.plain: A block of about 12,800 small plastic cubes, each paired with a thin screen that flashes when it catches a neutron, read out by light fibres, giving a three-dimensional picture of each antineutrino interaction.

detector:solid-detector.technology: Highly granular detector whose basic unit combines two scintillators, PVT and 6LiF:ZnS(Ag), read out by MPPCs

detector:solid-jlab.name: SoLID detector (planned)

summary.plain: A planned large solenoid-based detector for Hall A, built to handle very high rates so that experiments can see rare scattering events in great detail.

detector:solid-jlab.technology: Large-acceptance forward scattering spectrometer with full azimuthal angular coverage, handling luminosities of 10^37-10^39 per cm^2 per second

detector:soudan-2-detector.name: Soudan 2 detector

summary.plain: A block of iron plates and plastic gas tubes, as tall as a small house, that photographs the tracks of particles created inside it.

detector:soudan-2-detector.technology: Iron tracking calorimeter with honeycomb geometry operating as a time projection chamber, with plastic drift tubes filled with argon-CO2 gas and an active veto shield

detector:spd-nica.name: SPD detector (planned)

summary.plain: A planned universal detector with a thousand-tonne magnet yoke, a superconducting magnet and silicon, straw-tube, calorimeter and particle-identification subsystems to be placed at the second NICA collision point.

detector:spd-nica.technology: Universal detector for polarised-beam collisions at the second NICA interaction point

detector:sphenix.name: sPHENIX detector
subsystems: Superconducting solenoid magnet (reused from BaBar at SLAC), operating at 4 K
Electromagnetic calorimeter using tungsten bricks with embedded scintillating fibers

summary.plain: A4 scattered spin-polarised electrons from hydrogen and deuterium at the Mainz microtron MAMI and counted them with a lead-fluoride calorimeter. The tiny difference between the two spin directions shows how much strange quarks contribute to the proton's electric and magnetic structure, which proved to be small.

aliases: A Broadband/Resonant Approach to Cosmic Axion Detection with an Amplifying B-field Ring Apparatus
experiment:abracadabra.name: ABRACADABRA

summary.plain: ABRACADABRA-10 cm was a small prototype at MIT that searched for the axion, a candidate dark-matter particle, using a toroidal magnet instead of the resonant cavities other experiments use. Its axion search finished around 2021.

A six-metre telescope on a mountain in northern Chile that mapped the Big Bang afterglow in fine detail from 2007 to 2022. Its final data releases agree with the standard cosmological model and measure the expansion rate.

ADMX searches for the axion, a hypothetical particle that could make up dark matter. At the University of Washington, a tunable metal cavity sits inside a powerful magnet, hunting for a faint microwave signal that dark-matter axions would produce.

A second-generation experiment at Frascati's ADONE collider that studied how electron-positron annihilation makes proton-antiproton and other baryon pairs near threshold. It took part in the 1974 study of the J/psi.

One of the four first experiments at Frascati's ADONE collider (1969), run by Bologna, CERN and Frascati. It measured pion and kaon form factors, searched for heavy leptons and in 1971 gave the final demonstration that the multiple production was hadronic.

One of the four first experiments at Frascati's ADONE collider (1969), by physicists from Frascati, Naples, Pavia and Rome. In 1970 it gave the first evidence of an anomalously high rate of multiple particle production in e+e- collisions.
One of the four first experiments at Frascati's ADONE collider (1969), by researchers from Frascati and Rome, built to study e+e- reactions with neutral particles such as photons in the final state.

The second-generation Gamma-Gamma experiment at Frascati's ADONE: a larger detector with better sampling of electromagnetic and hadronic showers. It took part in the 1974 study of the J/psi, the new 3.1 GeV particle.

The magnetic detector of Frascati's ADONE collider, a solenoid with large gap and spark chambers that measured the charge and momentum of the particles from e+e- annihilation. It took part in the 1974 study of the J/psi.

One of the four first experiments at Frascati's ADONE collider (1969), by groups from Frascati, Rome and Padua, built to measure how often electron-positron annihilation makes pairs of muons, pions and kaons.

summary.plain: A CERN experiment that aims to measure directly how antihydrogen atoms fall in Earth’s gravity. It makes pulses of antihydrogen from antiprotons and positronium atoms and will pass them through a grating system called a deflectometer.

AGASA was a 100-square-kilometre field of 111 particle detectors in the mountains of Japan. Running from 1990 to 2004, it recorded giant cosmic-ray air showers and reported cosmic rays above the expected energy cutoff.

Samuel Ting's MIT group used a precise electron-positron pair spectrometer on Brookhaven's AGS proton beam and, in late summer 1974, saw a sharp peak at 3.1 GeV: a new heavy particle he called J. This record covers the Brookhaven side only; SLAC found the same particle as psi.

Princeton physicists James Cronin and Val Fitch, with James Christenson and René Turlay, used Brookhaven's AGS to check that the long-lived neutral kaon never decays into two pions. It occasionally does, which broke the symmetry between matter and antimatter (CP).

key_specs.label: Events reported in the discovery paper

summary.plain: A Brookhaven team led by Nicholas Samios searched the first run of the lab's new 80-inch bubble chamber for a particle predicted by Murray Gell-Mann. On 31 January 1964 they found one photograph that showed it, the omega-minus, and the pattern it completed held up.

Physicists from Columbia University used Brookhaven's brand-new AGS accelerator to make the first beam of high-energy neutrinos, sent it through a thick steel wall into a spark chamber, and found that the neutrinos made muons, not electrons. Reported in 1962, it showed there are two kinds of neutrino.

experiment:aleph.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 200 GeV from 1995)
experiment:aleph.name: ALEPH

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, used to study the Z and W bosons with great precision, including proving there are exactly three kinds of light neutrino.

experiment:alice.energy_regime: Pb-Pb (and other heavy-ion) collisions at up to 5.02 TeV per nucleon pair; p-Pb collisions; pp reference collisions at LHC energies (up to 13.6 TeV in Run 3)

summary.plain: ALICE is CERN's dedicated heavy-ion experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. By colliding lead nuclei instead of protons, it recreates the quark-gluon plasma, an extremely hot and dense state of matter thought to have filled the universe microseconds after the Big Bang, and studies how ordinary matter freezes out of it.

summary.plain: An experiment at CERN that makes atoms of antihydrogen, holds them in a magnetic trap and probes them with lasers and microwaves, comparing them with ordinary hydrogen. Its vertical trap, ALPHA-g, also tests how antimatter falls under gravity.

intervals.label: Technical Design Report submitted to DESY PRC
optical-system upgrade after the first science campaign

summary.plain: ALPS II shines a laser at a light-tight wall to see whether a tiny fraction can pass through as an undetectable particle and turn back into light on the far side. This would reveal new, very light particles related to dark matter. It has been operating at DESY since 2023.

aliases: Antarctic Muon and Neutrino Detector Array
experiment:amanda.energy_regime: Atmospheric and astrophysical neutrinos with typical reconstructed energies of several hundred GeV and above
experiment:amanda.name: AMANDA

summary.plain: The pioneering telescope that froze light sensors into the ice at the South Pole to catch neutrinos. It proved the idea worked and was later absorbed into its much bigger successor, IceCube.

aliases: Apparatus for Meson and Baryon Experimental Research
experiment:amber.name: AMBER

summary.plain: AMBER is the successor to COMPASS at CERN. It directs beams of muons, protons, pions, kaons and antiprotons at targets to measure antiproton production (relevant to dark-matter searches), the proton's charge radius and the quark and gluon momenta inside pions and kaons. It started taking data in 2023.

AMoRE-I was the second stage of AMoRE: eighteen molybdate crystals (6.2 kg), cooled to about 12 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, run at the Yangyang laboratory from 2019 to 2023. It saw no sign of neutrinoless double beta decay of molybdenum-100 and set a lower limit of 2.9 x 10^24 years on its half-life.

AMoRE-II is the main, full-size stage of AMoRE, being installed at Yemilab: about 90 kg of molybdenum-100 in hundreds of lithium-molybdate crystals cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero. It aims to probe the whole range of neutrino masses expected if neutrino masses follow the so-called inverted ordering.

AMoRE-Pilot was the first, small stage of the AMoRE experiment: six calcium-molybdate crystals (1.9 kg) cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, run at the Yangyang laboratory from 2015 to 2018 to look for neutrinoless double beta decay of molybdenum-100. It found no such decay and set a limit.

The first international collaboration at KEK, with physicists from the United States, Japan, China and South Korea, led by Steven Olsen of Rochester. Its detector at the TRISTAN collider used a 3-tesla superconducting solenoid and, with VENUS and TOPAZ, tested QCD and searched for the top quark from 1987 to 1995.

intervals.label: planned experiment (up to 107 kg of NaI(Tl) at Canfranc)
first prototype (single 10.7 kg crystal) at Canfranc
ANAIS-25 prototype (two 12.5 kg Alpha Spectra modules)
ANAIS-37 prototype (ANAIS-25 plus a third module)
production and installation of the nine ANAIS-112 modules
dark matter run (annual modulation data taking)

summary.plain: ANAIS-112 was nine sodium iodide crystals, 112.5 kg in all, in the Canfranc underground laboratory in Spain. Built to check with the same material the yearly dark matter signal reported by DAMA/LIBRA, it took data from August 2017 to early 2026; its published analyses find no such modulation.

A radio antenna array flown high over Antarctica on a NASA balloon, using the entire ice sheet below as a giant listening surface for ultra-high-energy neutrinos and cosmic rays. It flew five times between 2003 and 2016.

A 26-tonne tank of gadolinium-doped water in an underground hall at Fermilab, in the Booster neutrino beam, that counts the neutrons knocked out when neutrinos hit oxygen nuclei, and tests ultra-fast light sensors for future neutrino detectors.

aliases: Astronomy with a Neutrino Telescope and Abyss environmental RESearch
experiment:antares.name: ANTARES

summary.plain: The first neutrino telescope built under the sea. For sixteen years, twelve long cables of light sensors hung nearly 2.5 kilometres deep in the Mediterranean off Toulon, France, watching for the faint blue flashes that a neutrino from space can make.

APEX searched for a hypothetical 'dark photon' by firing Jefferson Lab's electron beam at a heavy target and looking for a narrow bump in the mass of electron-positron pairs. A short 2010 test run set the first limits; a longer run followed in 2019.
A handful of radio-antenna stations buried in the ice near the South Pole, testing technology for finding the highest-energy neutrinos from space and for a future upgrade to IceCube.

intervals.label: approved as LSC EXP-08-2010 / CERN RE18
construction and surface tests at CERN, transfer to and assembly at LSC
underground commissioning with gas argon, then liquid-argon filling
liquid-argon data taking (single-phase Run I in 2015, later dual-phase run)
ArDM Run I (single phase, liquid argon)
completed (dual-phase data taking ended; hardware reused for DArTinArDM)

key_specs.label: Liquid argon filled into the vessel (February 2015)

summary.plain: ArDM was a ton-scale liquid argon detector built at CERN, then installed in the Canfranc underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees, to search for WIMP dark matter. It took liquid-argon data from 2015 and finished dual-phase running by about 2020. Its papers report detector performance and backgrounds, not a WIMP limit.

ARGO is a proposed 400-tonne liquid argon detector (300 tonnes fiducial) for the very large dark matter search planned as the last step of the Global Argon Dark Matter Collaboration. SNOLAB's Cube Hall in Canada has been selected as the prospective site. It aims to search for WIMPs down to the neutrino fog.

ARGO-YBJ covered a 6700 square metre floor on the Tibetan plateau with a single layer of particle counters to catch even small air showers. It watched the northern sky for TeV gamma rays and studied cosmic rays from 2007 to 2013.

intervals.label: commissioning in the MINOS near-detector hall
physics run in the NuMI low-energy beam

summary.plain: A small liquid-argon detector, about 170 litres, that sat in front of the MINOS near detector at Fermilab in 2009-10 to catch neutrinos from the NuMI beam. It showed that liquid-argon chambers work in a neutrino beam and made the first neutrino cross-section measurements on argon.

A detector at DESY's DORIS ring in Hamburg that studied B mesons, particles containing the bottom quark. In 1987 ARGUS made the first observation of B-meson mixing, showing that a neutral B can turn into its antiparticle; it ran until about 1993.

aliases: Antarctic Ross Ice Shelf Antenna Neutrino Array

key_specs.label: Ice shelf thickness at deployment site

experiment:arianna.name: ARIANNA

summary.plain: A small, now-shut-down array of radio antennas that once sat on the surface of Antarctica's Ross Ice Shelf, listening for the crackle of ultra-high-energy neutrinos, and testing ideas for a much bigger array that was never built.

intervals.label: data taking at the Antiproton Decelerator

summary.plain: A CERN experiment that compares matter and antimatter using atoms that contain an antiproton: antiprotonic helium and antihydrogen. It also studies what happens when antiprotons collide with ordinary atoms.

intervals.label: data taking at the Antiproton Decelerator

summary.plain: A CERN experiment that in 2002 made the first large numbers of cold antihydrogen atoms, by mixing trapped antiprotons and positrons. It ended in 2004; its successor is ALPHA.

experiment:atlas.energy_regime: Proton-proton collisions at 7-13.6 TeV centre-of-mass energy; lead-lead collisions at 5.02 TeV per nucleon pair
experiment:atlas.name: ATLAS

summary.plain: ATLAS is one of the two big general-purpose experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. Its 7000-tonne detector sits in a cavern 100 metres underground and records what comes out of proton collisions. In 2012 ATLAS and CMS announced the discovery of the Higgs boson.

intervals.label: data taking at the Antiproton Decelerator
completed (true end date not published; upper bound)

summary.plain: A CERN experiment that made and studied atoms of antihydrogen to compare them with hydrogen. It was the first to use cold positrons to cool antiprotons, building on the earlier TRAP experiment. It has now finished.

experiment:babar.energy_regime: Asymmetric e⁺e⁻ collisions at 10.58 GeV center-of-mass (the Υ(4S) resonance)
experiment:babar.name: BaBar

summary.plain: A particle detector at SLAC, near Stanford, California, built to study why matter and antimatter behave slightly differently by watching B mesons decay. It ran from 1999 to 2008 and, together with Japan's Belle experiment, confirmed a theory that won the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.
A growing underwater telescope in Lake Baikal, Siberia, that has been adding new clusters of light sensors every year since 2016 in search of neutrinos from deep space.

A four-storey building of 3,184 liquid-scintillator tanks inside Mount Andyrchi in the Caucasus, 850 metres of rock-equivalent deep. Running since 1978, it counts cosmic-ray muons and neutrinos, and has watched for a burst from an exploding star in our Galaxy since 1980.

intervals.label: antiproton runs at the Antiproton Decelerator

summary.plain: A CERN experiment that holds single antiprotons in electromagnetic traps and measures how they spin and circle in a magnetic field, to compare their magnetic moment and charge-to-mass ratio with those of the proton.

experiment:belle.energy_regime: e⁺e⁻ collisions at the Υ(4S) resonance, √s ≈ 10.58 GeV
experiment:belle.name: Belle

summary.plain: An experiment at the KEK laboratory in Japan that ran from 1999 to 2010. It watched electrons and positrons collide to make pairs of B particles, and showed that matter and antimatter behave differently — work that led to the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.

The successor to the Belle experiment at the KEK laboratory in Japan. Running since 2019, it records electron-positron collisions from the SuperKEKB machine, looking for tiny departures from the known laws of physics in the decays of heavy, short-lived particles.

The first Beijing Spectrometer, the detector at the Beijing Electron-Positron Collider from 1989 to 1995. In March 1992 it published its first physics paper, a precision measurement of the tau lepton mass that removed doubts about lepton universality.

The upgraded Beijing Spectrometer, which ran at the upgraded Beijing Electron-Positron Collider from 1998 to 2004. It measured the hadron production ratio R between 2 and 5 GeV and saw a narrow enhancement in proton-antiproton pairs near threshold in J/psi decays.

intervals.label: approval of the BEPC Upgrade Project
commissioning with the first BEPCII collisions

summary.plain: The Beijing Spectrometer III at China's BEPCII collider, built to study hadron and tau-charm physics with the highest accuracy so far. A collaboration of about 700 members from 86 institutions in 16 countries, it began taking data in 2008 and found the charged charmonium-like state Zc(3900).

key_specs.label: Proton energy needed to make an antiproton

summary.plain: In August and September 1955 Owen Chamberlain, Emilio Segrè, Clyde Wiegand and Thomas Ypsilantis used Berkeley's new Bevatron to hunt for the proton's antimatter twin. They found negative particles with the proton mass: the antiproton, a prediction of Dirac's theory.

The newest BICEP/Keck telescope at the South Pole: four refracting telescopes in six frequency bands, built to detect or limit the polarization pattern left by gravitational waves from inflation while subtracting galactic foregrounds.

aliases: Background Imaging of Cosmic Extragalactic Polarization
experiment:bicep1.name: BICEP1

summary.plain: The first BICEP telescope: a small refractor at the South Pole that spent three years (2006-2008) mapping a clean 2% of the sky in polarization, looking for the imprint of gravitational waves from inflation.

A 26-centimetre telescope at the South Pole that watched one patch of sky for three seasons. In 2014 it reported an excess of polarization attributed to gravitational waves, which a joint analysis with Planck data then traced largely to dust.
The successor to BICEP2: a larger 95 GHz telescope with 2560 detectors in a South Pole laboratory. Its maps, with Keck Array data, give the strongest limit on gravitational waves from inflation.

BM@N (Baryonic Matter at Nuclotron) is the first experiment at JINR's Nuclotron/NICA complex. It aims heavy-ion beams of up to several GeV per nucleon at fixed targets and measures the produced particles to study dense, baryon-rich nuclear matter, including strange hyperons.

intervals.label: construction (detailed proposal to completed detector structures)

summary.plain: A giant ball of ultra-pure liquid deep under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy that directly watched low-energy neutrinos streaming from the Sun's core, including two kinds no one had ever seen before.

The Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey, part of SDSS-III, measured the distances to over a million galaxies and to distant quasars. It used the faint ripples left in the universe by sound waves in the early cosmos as a ruler to track cosmic expansion.

BRAHMS was one of the four original experiments at Brookhaven's RHIC collider. Its two movable spectrometers measured charged particles over a very wide range of angles in gold-gold and other collisions, from the first RHIC run in 2000 until June 2006.

intervals.label: Bugey-4 and Bugey-3 measurements (dates of data taking not found)

summary.plain: A series of experiments at the Bugey nuclear power plant in France in the early 1990s that measured reactor antineutrinos from 15 to 95 metres away. Bugey-3 compared three identical detectors at different distances and found no oscillation; Bugey-4 gave a very precise rate measurement.

aliases: BULky and Low-threshold Kinetic Inductance Detector

intervals.label: planned installation of the 3-detector demonstrator at the LNGS cryo-platform
planned installation of the final experiment at the LNGS cryo-platform

experiment:bullkid-dm.name: BULLKID-DM

summary.plain: BULLKID-DM is a planned dark matter experiment that would use about 800 grams of silicon, cut into over 2000 tiny blocks that are each read by a superconducting sensor, to look for dark matter near the proton mass or lighter. The final detector is planned for the Gran Sasso underground laboratory in Italy in 2027.

C-4 was designed as a bigger version of CoGeNT: four germanium detectors, each about three times heavier, in a better-shielded setup in the Soudan mine, to test CoGeNT's low-energy excess. Only the design paper was read; no result or start of data taking was found.

Ninety-six cubes of calcium fluoride crystal, immersed in liquid scintillator that vetoes outside radiation, in a laboratory of the Kamioka mine. It looks for the neutrinoless double beta decay of calcium-48, whose decay energy is the highest known, above most natural radioactivity.

aliases: Collaboration of Australia and Nippon for Gamma-Ray Observation in the Outback
experiment:cangaroo.name: CANGAROO

summary.plain: Gamma-ray telescopes in the South Australian outback run by Japanese and Australian universities from 1992 to 2011, growing from one 3.8 metre mirror to an array of four 10 metre telescopes.

CAST looked for axions, hypothetical particles that might explain dark matter, by pointing a powerful magnet left over from Large Hadron Collider testing at the Sun and watching for X-rays. It ran at CERN from 2003 until the end of 2022.

intervals.label: construction of the experiment at the FAIR site

summary.plain: CBM (Compressed Baryonic Matter) is a planned heavy-ion experiment at the future FAIR facility in Darmstadt. It will record collisions at the highest interaction rates to study matter at densities like those in neutron-star cores, searching for a first-order phase transition and the QCD critical point.

intervals.label: completed (CCFR data taking; detector continued as NuTeV)

summary.plain: A series of Fermilab experiments in the 1980s in which a 690-tonne iron-and-scintillator detector recorded high-energy neutrinos from the Tevatron, used to measure how quarks are distributed inside the proton and to test the electroweak theory. Its detector was later reused by NuTeV.

A 10-ton tank of liquid argon in the Lujan neutron-source building at Los Alamos, watched by light sensors, 20 metres from a tungsten target hit by protons. It looks for sterile neutrinos and for light dark matter that the proton beam might make.

CDEX-1 was the first stage of the CDEX programme: a single 1 kg germanium crystal in the Jinping underground laboratory in China, tuned to notice the tiny energy of very light dark matter particles. It saw no dark matter, and its results disfavoured earlier claimed signals.

CDEX-10 is the second stage of the CDEX programme: ten kilograms of germanium crystals bathed in liquid nitrogen in the Jinping underground laboratory in China. It searches for very light dark matter and has set limits down to a few MeV.

CDEX-50 is a proposed next stage of the CDEX programme: 50 kilograms of germanium detectors bathed in liquid nitrogen in the expanded Jinping underground laboratory in China, aimed at very light dark matter.

intervals.label: first Tevatron proton-antiproton collisions observed by CDF
engineering run and first physics results

summary.plain: A giant particle detector at Fermilab, near Chicago, that watched protons and their antimatter twins smash together at nearly the speed of light. It helped find the top quark, the heaviest known building block of matter, and ran until the Tevatron collider it depended on shut down in 2011.

A 1250-tonne magnetised-iron detector in CERN's neutrino beams that, from 1976 to 1984, measured how neutrinos and antineutrinos scatter off iron nuclei. Led by Jack Steinberger, it pinned down cross sections, quark structure functions and electroweak parameters.

intervals.label: WIMP-search data runs at the Stanford Underground Facility

summary.plain: The first stage of the Cryogenic Dark Matter Search: germanium and silicon crystals cooled to 20 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, in a shallow tunnel under Stanford University. Its 2000 result excluded, at more than 84% confidence, the whole dark matter signal region reported by the DAMA experiment.

experiment:cdms-ii.energy_regime: keV-scale nuclear recoils, WIMP-nucleon spin-independent limit quoted near 70 GeV/c² WIMP mass
experiment:cdms-ii.name: CDMS II

summary.plain: CDMS II searched for dark matter particles using very cold germanium and silicon crystals half a mile underground in Minnesota. It ran from about 2005 to 2009 and found no convincing signal, but set some of the tightest limits of its time on how often dark matter might bump into ordinary atoms.

The fifth detector approved for DESY's PETRA collider, installed in 1980 to replace PLUTO. It recorded e+e- collisions until PETRA closed in 1986 and its detector paper describes it as a new detector for PETRA.

A 100-tonne detector of marble plates and tracking tubes at CERN's SPS, running from 1978 to 1984, built to study the neutral-current weak force in neutrino collisions and the quark structure of the nucleon.

A 692-tonne glass-target calorimeter at CERN's SPS built to catch the rare collisions in which a muon neutrino scatters off an electron, a clean way to measure the weak mixing angle. It ran from 1986 to 1991.

The first reactor experiment to hunt for neutrino oscillations over about one kilometre: a liquid-scintillator detector inside a hill near the Chooz nuclear power station in France. In 1997-98 it saw no disappearance of antineutrinos, which put the first tight upper limit on the mixing angle later called theta-13.

experiment:chorus.energy_regime: Mean neutrino energy 26 GeV (CERN SPS wide-band neutrino beam)

intervals.label: first operation (CERN Courier: began operation in 1993)

experiment:chorus.name: CHORUS

summary.plain: A hybrid detector at CERN that hunted for muon neutrinos turning into tau neutrinos, by looking for the short kink of a tau lepton in a 770 kg block of nuclear emulsion. It ran in 1994-97, saw no signal, and set a tight limit on the mixing.

experiment:clas.energy_regime: Electron and photon beams up to 6 GeV
experiment:clas.name: CLAS

summary.plain: CLAS (the CEBAF Large Acceptance Spectrometer) was a large particle detector in Hall B at Jefferson Lab that recorded what happens when electron or photon beams strike nuclei, mapping nucleon excitations and the structure of protons and neutrons from 1997 to 2012.

experiment:clas12.energy_regime: Electron beam energies up to 11 GeV
experiment:clas12.name: CLAS12

summary.plain: CLAS12 is the upgraded Hall B detector at Jefferson Lab for the 12 GeV electron beam. Its magnets and chambers follow the particles from electron collisions with protons and nuclei to study how the proton, neutron and heavier states are built from quarks and gluons.

Four microwave telescopes at 5140 metres in northern Chile that have surveyed about three quarters of the sky since 2016, measuring the largest-scale polarization of the Big Bang afterglow, which is hard to measure from the ground.

intervals.label: conception of the South Area Experiment

summary.plain: The main detector at Cornell's electron-positron ring CESR from 1979 to 2008. Upgraded five times (CLEO-1 to CLEO-c), it studied bottom and charm quarks and tau leptons, discovering B mesons in 1980 and the first charmless B decays in 1989-90.

A planned next-generation CMB experiment with large and small telescopes at the South Pole and in Chile. On 9 July 2025 the US Department of Energy and National Science Foundation said they could no longer support the project, and the project said it was proceeding with an orderly shutdown.

The first Cryogenic Magnetic Detector at the Budker Institute's VEPP-2M collider in Novosibirsk, which took data from 1979 to 1984. It began the CMD line of detectors (CMD-2, CMD-3) run by one collaboration.

The Cryogenic Magnetic Detector 2 at the VEPP-2M collider of the Budker Institute, which took data from 1992 to 2000. Among its results is a high-statistics measurement of the pion form factor between 0.6 and 1.0 GeV with 0.8% systematic uncertainty.

The Cryogenic Magnetic Detector 3 at the VEPP-2000 collider of the Budker Institute in Novosibirsk, taking data since 2010 at energies up to 2 GeV. Its measurement of the pion form factor, important for predicting the muon's magnetic moment, reaches 0.7% systematic uncertainty.

experiment:cms.energy_regime: Proton-proton (and heavy-ion) collisions at TeV centre-of-mass energies: designed for 14 TeV, 13.6 TeV delivered in LHC Run 3
experiment:cms.name: CMS

summary.plain: One of the two big general-purpose experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. Thousands of scientists use it to photograph the debris of proton collisions 40 million times a second. In 2012 it was one of the two experiments that found the Higgs boson.

intervals.label: underground installation and cooldown at Soudan
initial run (442 live days to 6 March 2011)
outage after the Soudan access-shaft fire
continuous data taking after the fire (data set analysed to 23 April 2013)

summary.plain: CoGeNT ran a single 440-gram germanium crystal in the Soudan mine in Minnesota to look for very light dark matter. It reported an unexplained excess of low-energy events and a seasonal rate change that fit light dark matter, but called their origin unknown and the significance low, and other experiments did not confirm them.

key_specs.label: CsI[Na] detector baseline (distance from neutrino source)

summary.plain: An experiment at a US national laboratory that catches neutrinos from a neutron-making machine and watches them bounce gently off whole atomic nuclei, a process predicted for decades but only directly seen for the first time in 2017.

key_specs.label: Phase-I sensitivity goal (90% C.L. upper limit)

summary.plain: An experiment being built at the J-PARC laboratory in Japan to look for a muon turning directly into an electron near an aluminium atom -- a process the Standard Model forbids. It is being built in stages, starting with a smaller first phase.

aliases: Common Muon and Proton Apparatus for Structure and Spectroscopy
experiment:compass.energy_regime: 160 GeV polarised muon beam (and hadron beams) on polarised and unpolarised fixed targets
experiment:compass.name: COMPASS

summary.plain: COMPASS fired muons and hadrons from CERN's SPS accelerator at polarised targets to study how protons and neutrons get their spin from their quarks and gluons, and to search for exotic particles. It took data from 2002 until its last run in 2021-2022.

intervals.label: engineering run with a 4 g prototype
data taking with the upgraded CCD array

summary.plain: An array of very low-noise silicon camera chips (CCDs) 30 metres from the Angra 2 nuclear reactor in Brazil, built to spot the tiny recoil of a silicon nucleus when a reactor antineutrino scatters off it coherently. It has set limits and continues to improve its sensitivity.

key_specs.label: Distance from reactor core (Leibstadt / CONUS+ phase)

summary.plain: A small, sensitive detector using ultra-pure germanium crystals to catch reactor antineutrinos gently bouncing off whole atomic nuclei, first run at a German nuclear plant and, after it closed, moved to a Swiss one under the name CONUS+.

intervals.label: detector assembly at Y2L (early 2016) and commissioning
physics data taking at Y2L (6.4 years)

summary.plain: COSINE-100 was a 106 kg array of eight sodium-iodide crystals at the Yangyang underground laboratory, built to test the long-disputed claim by the DAMA experiment of a yearly rise and fall in dark-matter-like signals, using the same kind of crystal. It ran from 2016 to 2023 and has not confirmed the DAMA signal.

intervals.label: decommissioning at Y2L, relocation, upgrade and installation at Yemilab
physics data taking at the nominal -30 C

summary.plain: COSINE-100U is the upgraded COSINE-100 experiment: the same eight sodium-iodide crystals, moved to the deeper Yemilab laboratory and re-fitted so that more of their light is collected. It aims to look for lighter dark matter and has been taking data there since September 2025.

intervals.label: R&D project and proposed NaI cryogenic calorimeter at LNGS
construction of the experimental facility at LNGS
underground run of a 3.67 g NaI remoTES prototype at LNGS
commissioning of the cryostat and facility; first physics run (COSINUS-1pi Run1) awaited

summary.plain: COSINUS is a dark matter detector being commissioned at the Gran Sasso laboratory in Italy. It uses sodium iodide crystals, the DAMA/LIBRA material, cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero so that it senses both heat and light, to test whether DAMA's yearly signal is dark matter.

intervals.label: first operation of the COSME detector (Canfranc tunnel)
second operation in the deeper, IGEX-type shield (2450 m.w.e.)
completed (detector removed from the shield; no end date published)

summary.plain: COSME was a small germanium crystal, about a quarter of a kilogram, in the Canfranc underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees. It was used in two runs, in the 1990s, to look for dark matter particles and for axions from the Sun, and set limits on both.

intervals.label: completed (successor chamber took over the pressure vessel)

key_specs.label: Depth of the MINOS near-detector hall

summary.plain: COUPP-2kg was the first dark-matter bubble chamber of the COUPP team: a small jar of superheated CF3I run in a Fermilab neutrino tunnel from 2005. It proved the technique and set improved limits on WIMPs that couple to nuclear spin.

intervals.label: operation (MINOS tunnel at Fermilab, then SNOLAB)

summary.plain: COUPP-4kg was a two-litre bubble chamber of superheated CF3I, first run in a Fermilab tunnel and then two kilometres underground at SNOLAB. Its papers report world-best limits on how strongly heavy dark matter could couple to nuclear spin.

In spring 1953 Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines took a liquid-scintillator detector to a plutonium-production reactor at Hanford, Washington, hoping to catch antineutrinos. Cosmic-ray background swamped the signal after a few months, so the result was only tentative; it led them to the cleaner Savannah River experiment.

In 1955-56 Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines put a detector beside a reactor at the Savannah River Plant in South Carolina and counted the antineutrinos pouring out of it. Their July 1956 report confirmed the neutrino, the particle Pauli proposed in 1930 and widely thought undetectable.

aliases: Cryogenic Rare Event Search with Superconducting Thermometers
experiment:cresst.energy_regime: Sub-GeV WIMPs; CRESST-III reaches nuclear-recoil thresholds of 10 eV and lower, probing masses down to ~70 MeV/c²

intervals.label: CRESST-I: construction and first run (sapphire detectors)

experiment:cresst.name: CRESST

summary.plain: CRESST looks for dark matter using crystals of calcium tungstate, cooled to a whisker above absolute zero deep under an Italian mountain. Each tiny bump from a passing particle makes both heat and a flash of light, and comparing the two tells physicists what kind of particle caused it.

CREX was PREX's sister experiment: it measured the neutron skin of calcium-48 with spin-flipped electron beams at Jefferson Lab. The skin turned out relatively thin, a result that must be reconciled with the thick skin of lead.

intervals.label: removed from DESY; stored at SLAC

summary.plain: A spherical detector of 672 sodium iodide crystals that surrounded the collision point to measure photons. Built at SLAC and used at SPEAR for charmonium spectroscopy, then moved to DESY's DORIS ring in 1982 to study bottom-quark systems, before going to Brookhaven and Mainz for later work.

intervals.label: LST sub-array (LST-1 to LST-4, CTAO-North) completed and inaugurated

summary.plain: A next-generation gamma-ray observatory being built at two sites, one in Spain and one in Chile, using dozens of telescopes of three different sizes to see the whole sky and the widest range of gamma-ray energies of any single project.

aliases: Cryogenic Underground Observatory for Rare Events
experiment:cuore.name: CUORE

summary.plain: A huge array of super-cold tellurium crystals under an Italian mountain, listening for a faint click of heat that would signal a rare radioactive decay. CUORE has been steadily collecting data since 2019.

A tower of 62 tellurium-oxide crystals chilled to about 10 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero in the Gran Sasso laboratory, listening for the heat of a neutrinoless double beta decay. It ran from 2003 to 2008 and was the pilot for CUORE.

The planned successor to CUORE: about 1500 crystals of a different material (lithium molybdate) that both glow and register heat, reusing CUORE's giant refrigerator under an Italian mountain to search for a rare radioactive process even more precisely.

intervals.label: selected by the CESR Program Advisory Committee

summary.plain: A compact detector made of sodium iodide and lead-glass crystals at the north interaction point of Cornell's CESR ring, built by Columbia and Stony Brook universities. Its photon energy resolution made it ideal for the transitions between bottom-quark Upsilon states, which it studied from 1979 to about 1990.

intervals.label: LIME 50 L prototype (PHASE 0 R&D): underground data taking at LNGS (five periods)
CYGNO-04 (0.4 m^3) demonstrator under construction in LNGS Hall F

summary.plain: CYGNO is a directional dark matter project at Gran Sasso. A gas chamber of helium and CF4 turns particle tracks into light that cameras photograph, giving 3D tracks and their direction. A 50-litre prototype ran underground; a 0.4 cubic-metre demonstrator is being built.

A giant particle detector at Fermilab, near Chicago, named after its position on the Tevatron collider ring. It watched protons and antiprotons collide from 1992 until the Tevatron shut down in 2011, and it co-discovered the top quark in 1995.

aliases: Large sodium Iodide Bulk for RAre processes
experiment:dama-libra.name: DAMA/LIBRA

summary.plain: DAMA/LIBRA was a 250 kg array of sodium iodide crystals in the Gran Sasso underground laboratory, successor to DAMA/NaI. From 2003 it recorded a yearly rise and fall in its signal that the team attributes to dark matter, and the data taking is reported to have ended in 2024. Other experiments have not confirmed the signal.

DAMA/NaI was a set of nine sodium iodide crystals, about 100 kg in all, in the Gran Sasso underground laboratory in Italy. From 1995 to 2002 it watched for a yearly rise and fall in its signal that dark matter would cause. The team reported such a seasonal signal; other experiments have not reproduced it.

experiment:damic.energy_regime: WIMPs of a few GeV/c² (silicon target); low-energy ionization excess near 100 eV under continued study

intervals.label: SNOLAB: repurposed as background test stand

experiment:damic.name: DAMIC

summary.plain: DAMIC searched for dark matter using the same kind of light-sensing chips found in digital cameras, cooled and shielded deep underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It started at Fermilab and moved to SNOLAB, later gaining even more sensitive 'skipper' chips, before the detector was repurposed as a background test stand around 2025.

aliases: DArk Matter In CCDs at Modane
experiment:damic-m.energy_regime: Hidden-sector / light dark matter, roughly 0.5-1000 MeV/c² (electron-recoil channel)

intervals.label: Low Background Chamber: status and first results

experiment:damic-m.name: DAMIC-M

summary.plain: DAMIC-M is the next generation of the DAMIC dark matter search, using very sensitive silicon chips called skipper CCDs that can count single electrons. A 20-gram prototype has been running deep under a mountain in the French Alps since 2022, hunting for very light, hidden particles.

aliases: Detector of the reactor AntiNeutrino based on Solid-state Scintillator
experiment:danss.name: DANSS

summary.plain: A movable one-cubic-metre block of plastic scintillator strips placed a few metres below an industrial reactor at the Kalinin power plant in Russia. By comparing antineutrino spectra at three distances since 2016 it has looked for, and so far excluded, much of the parameter space for a sterile neutrino.

DarkQuest is a proposed Fermilab experiment that would reuse the SeaQuest particle detector to search for hidden, dark-sector particles instead of ordinary quarks, at low cost since it builds on equipment already installed.

DarkSide-20k will be a much bigger dark matter detector, holding fifty tonnes of liquid argon, being built deep under a mountain in Italy. It is the successor of the smaller DarkSide-50 experiment and is still under construction, with data taking expected around 2026-2027.

DarkSide-50 was a dark matter detector holding fifty kilograms of liquid argon, deep under a mountain in Italy. It ran from 2013 to 2020, testing techniques later scaled up for its successor, DarkSide-20k.

DarkSide-LowMass is a proposed 1.5-tonne liquid argon detector designed to detect dark matter lighter than about 10 GeV through the faint electric charge it would free in the argon. It is a project of the Global Argon Dark Matter Collaboration; the primary plan is to install it at SNOLAB in Canada.

DarkSPHERE is a proposed detector for light dark matter: a hollow copper sphere filled with gas, made from copper grown underground at the Boulby laboratory in England. It builds on the NEWS-G experiments and aims to reach the level where neutrinos become the main background.
A compact microwave interferometer at the South Pole that measured the Big Bang afterglow on degree scales in 2000 and, in 2002, made the first detection of its polarization.

intervals.label: seven-AD configuration (one AD re-purposed for JUNO-related R&D)

summary.plain: An experiment in southern China that used clusters of detectors near and far from nuclear reactors to discover that one type of neutrino oscillation, long searched for, really happens.

aliases: Dark matter Experiment using Argon Pulse-shape discrimination

intervals.label: detector upgrades (neck flow guides, particulate removal system)

experiment:deap-3600.name: DEAP-3600

summary.plain: DEAP-3600 is a dark matter experiment 2 km underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It watches 3.6 tonnes of liquid argon for the faint flash of light a dark matter particle would make hitting an argon nucleus. It has taken data since late 2016. After detector upgrades it began a third run, which the collaboration's abstract of 21 September 2026 describes as newly initiated.

intervals.label: DAΦNE physics data taking (kaonic nitrogen, then hydrogen)

summary.plain: A tabletop experiment at Frascati's DAΦNE that stopped kaons in a hydrogen gas target and measured the X-rays from kaonic hydrogen, an exotic atom with a kaon in place of the electron. It ran in 2002 and gave the most precise values then known of how the strong force shifts the atom's lowest level.

An experiment at J-PARC in Japan that searches for a muon turning directly into an electron inside a nucleus, a process the Standard Model does not allow at a measurable rate. Its beamline and spectrometer have been built; no result has been published yet.

aliases: Direct search Experiment for Light dark matter

intervals.label: funded: DFG Research Unit 6006 (design, build and operate phase I)

experiment:delight.name: DELight

summary.plain: DELight is a planned dark matter experiment that will use superfluid helium, cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, and very sensitive magnetic thermometers to look for particles far lighter than a proton. Its first phase is planned for a shallow underground laboratory in Switzerland.

aliases: Detector with Lepton, Photon and Hadron Identification
experiment:delphi.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 209 GeV by 2000)
experiment:delphi.name: DELPHI

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, known for its Ring Imaging Cherenkov detectors that could identify the type of each charged particle produced.

A six-year photographic map of a quarter of the southern sky, made with the 570-megapixel Dark Energy Camera on a Chilean telescope. By measuring the shapes and positions of hundreds of millions of galaxies, it set out to test how dark energy and gravity shape the universe.

A spectroscopic instrument on a 4-metre telescope in Arizona that records the light of up to 5,000 galaxies and quasars at once. Measuring how far away tens of millions of them are, it maps the universe in 3D to see how dark energy shapes cosmic expansion.

intervals.label: continued stable operation after the physics run

key_specs.label: Depth in the South Pole ice

summary.plain: DM-Ice17 was 17 kg of sodium iodide crystals frozen into the Antarctic ice at the South Pole next to the IceCube neutrino detector, a first test in the Southern Hemisphere of the yearly signal DAMA reported. Too small to settle that question, it showed that the ice is a quiet place for such detectors.

intervals.label: data taking with three NaI(Tl) modules

summary.plain: DM32 was an early dark matter search with three sodium iodide crystals (32 kg) run by a Zaragoza group in the Canfranc underground laboratory, Spain, from 1993 to 1994. It set competitive limits and looked for a yearly modulation.

DMRadio is a series of experiments at Stanford and SLAC that search for very light dark-matter axions using a magnet and a tuned electrical circuit instead of a microwave cavity. It is currently being built.

intervals.label: development and surface-laboratory commissioning (10-L detector at MIT)

summary.plain: DMTPC (Dark Matter Time Projection Chamber) is a directional dark matter experiment led from MIT.
