A low-pressure CF4 gas chamber with camera readout images the tracks of recoiling nuclei, which could reveal the direction a dark matter particle came from. A 10-litre detector ran at MIT and then underground at WIPP.

aliases: Direct Observation of the NU Tau
experiment:donut.energy_regime: Tau neutrinos from charmed-meson decay in a Tevatron fixed-target proton beam dump
experiment:donut.name: DONUT

summary.plain: A Fermilab experiment that ran for a few months in 1997, aiming a proton beam from the Tevatron at a target to make tau neutrinos and catching them directly for the first time in stacks of photographic emulsion, completing the direct detection of every particle the Standard Model predicts.

intervals.label: near and far detectors both operating

summary.plain: A French experiment that watched antineutrinos from the Chooz nuclear reactors with two detectors at different distances, finding evidence that they change type on the way.

DRIFT is a family of detectors in the Boulby mine that use low-pressure gas to trace the direction of the atom a dark matter particle would knock, which could show whether it comes from the direction our Solar System moves through the Galaxy. It has run since 2001.

experiment:dune.energy_regime: GeV-scale accelerator neutrinos (wide band, 60-120 GeV protons), plus MeV-scale supernova neutrinos

intervals.label: DUNE collaboration formed from LBNE and LBNO

quantity.display: 1478 m (4850-foot level, converted from feet); sources round this to 1480-1500 m

experiment:dune.name: Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment

summary.plain: A very large experiment that will send neutrinos 1285 kilometres through the Earth from Illinois to South Dakota, where detectors filled with liquid argon a mile underground will record them. It aims to find out whether neutrinos and antineutrinos behave differently, to catch neutrinos from an exploding star, and to look for protons decaying.

The Brookhaven experiment that stored muons in a large magnetic ring and measured how fast their spin turns, giving the muon’s anomalous magnetic moment to 0.54 parts per million, fourteen times better than before. Its ring was later moved to Fermilab.

E949 was a Brookhaven National Laboratory experiment that stopped kaons in a detector to catch the same ultra-rare decay NA62 also studies -- a kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos -- continuing the earlier E787 experiment.

The Extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey, part of SDSS-IV, mapped galaxies and quasars from when the universe was 3 to 8 billion years old, a critical time when dark energy started to affect its expansion, and measured how fast space was expanding then.

intervals.label: ECHo-1k phase (medium-scale experiment, about 1 kBq of 163Ho)
ECHo-100k phase (aims at a sensitivity below 2 eV)

summary.plain: An experiment coordinated from Heidelberg that weighs the electron neutrino by watching holmium-163 atoms decay inside tiny ultra-cold magnetic thermometers. Its first phase, ECHo-1k, set a limit of 15 electron-volts; the next phase aims below 2.

aliases: Experience pour DEtecter Les WIMPs En Site Souterrain
experiment:edelweiss.energy_regime: Sub-GeV dark matter (32-100 MeV/c² via the Migdal effect) and traditional WIMP masses via nuclear recoils

intervals.label: sub-GeV / Migdal-effect programme (NbSi TES, NTL amplification)

experiment:edelweiss.name: EDELWEISS

summary.plain: EDELWEISS searches for dark matter using pure germanium crystals cooled to near absolute zero, deep under a mountain in the French Alps. Recent versions are sensitive enough to look for dark matter far lighter than a proton.

intervals.label: NaI modules deployed at the Kamioka underground laboratory (first configuration)
ELEGANT V in the Oto Cosmo Observatory (16 NaI scintillators, 0.76 tons)

summary.plain: ELEGANT V was a 0.76-ton array of sodium iodide crystals in Japan's Oto Cosmo Observatory, an underground laboratory in Nara, used to search for dark matter alongside double-beta-decay studies. Its crystals and lead shield later served the PICO-LON dark matter project.

intervals.label: collaboration formed; EIC project detector technical design

summary.plain: ePIC is the first detector for the Electron-Ion Collider. A compact, multi-layer detector with a big solenoid magnet, it will record the particles produced when electrons hit protons and nuclei, so physicists can image the quarks and gluons that make up visible matter.

aliases: European Spallation Source neutrino Super Beam
experiment:essnusb.name: ESSnuSB

summary.plain: A proposed long-baseline experiment that would use the proton accelerator of the European Spallation Source in Sweden to make the most intense neutrino beam ever, aimed at a huge underground water detector in a mine 360 kilometres away, to look for differences between neutrinos and antineutrinos.
A liquid-xenon detector buried deep in a New Mexico salt mine that also stores nuclear waste. EXO-200 searched for a rare radioactive process in xenon atoms from 2011 to 2018 and found no signal.

experiment:faser.energy_regime: LHC Run 3 proton-proton collisions at 13.6 TeV, sampled via forward particle flux along the beam axis
experiment:faser.name: FASER

summary.plain: FASER is a small experiment placed in an unused tunnel 480 metres from CERN's ATLAS detector, watching for rare, long-lived particles and neutrinos that fly straight down the LHC's beamline.

intervals.label: ADONE two-beam data taking for FENICE

summary.plain: The last particle-physics experiment at Frascati's ADONE collider (1990 to 1993). It measured the neutron's electromagnetic form factor from electron-positron annihilation into neutron-antineutron pairs, a measurement never made before.

key_specs.label: Dimuon events with mass above 5 GeV in the discovery sample

summary.plain: Leon Lederman's Columbia-Fermilab-Stony Brook team fired Fermilab's 400 GeV protons at a target and studied pairs of muons that came out. In 1977 they saw a bump at 9.5 GeV: the upsilon, the first sign of the bottom quark.

A detector at Frascati's DAΦNE collider that stopped slow negative kaons from phi-meson decays in thin targets to make hypernuclei: nuclei in which a strange Λ particle replaces a nucleon. It took data in 2003-2004 and in 2006-2007.

key_specs.label: Separation of Fly's Eye I and II

summary.plain: The original Fly's Eye was a battery of mirrors and light sensors in the Utah desert that watched the night sky for the faint ultraviolet glow of cosmic-ray air showers. In 1991 it recorded the most energetic cosmic ray ever seen, about 3 × 10²⁰ eV.

A 900-ton iron and flash-tube detector built into the Alpine Fréjus road tunnel at the Modane laboratory. From 1984 to 1988 it searched for protons and bound neutrons decaying and for atmospheric-neutrino oscillations. It saw no signal and set lower limits on nucleon lifetimes of order 10^31 to 10^32 years.

intervals.label: installation and commissioning runs (first installed July-October 2002, reinstalled autumn 2003)
backward-angle commissioning and production (March 2006 to April 2007)

summary.plain: G0 used a large superconducting magnet in Hall C of Jefferson Lab to catch particles scattered from hydrogen and deuterium by a spin-flipping electron beam. The tiny differences between the two spin states map the strange quarks' contribution to the proton's charge and magnetism across a range of momentum transfers.
An experiment in an Italian mountain lab that used 30 tonnes of gallium, dissolved in an acid solution, to catch the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos, the ones from its very first fusion step.

A 1000-tonne bubble chamber filled with freon, built at CERN to catch neutrinos from the Proton Synchrotron's beam. In 1973 the Gargamelle collaboration presented the first direct evidence of the weak neutral current, a key prediction of the theory that unifies the electromagnetic and weak forces.

intervals.label: approved by the CERN Research Board

summary.plain: A CERN experiment designed to let single antihydrogen atoms fall about 20 centimetres and record where they annihilate, comparing the fall with that of ordinary hydrogen. Its first antihydrogen atoms were made at the end of 2022.

intervals.label: approved by the Gran Sasso Scientific Committee; funded; built
operation with four, then six, naked Ge detectors in liquid nitrogen

summary.plain: GENIUS-TF was a small test version of the GENIUS idea, bare germanium crystals dipped in liquid nitrogen. It ran in the Gran Sasso laboratory in Italy from 2003 to about 2006 to prove the technique and, along the way, to look for the yearly dark matter signal reported by DAMA.

A neutrino experiment buried under a mountain in Italy that searched for a rare radioactive process in germanium atoms. Finding it would prove neutrinos are their own antiparticles. GERDA ran from 2011 to 2019 and found no signal, only setting a limit.

experiment:gluex.energy_regime: ~9 GeV linearly polarised photon beam from 12 GeV CEBAF electrons

intervals.label: first data taking (GlueX Phase I onward)

experiment:gluex.name: GlueX

summary.plain: GlueX fires a beam of high-energy polarised photons at a hydrogen target in Hall D at Jefferson Lab to map out and search for exotic hybrid mesons, particles whose quarks are bound together with an excited gluon field.

aliases: Giant Radio Array for Neutrino Detection

intervals.label: GRANDProto300 prototype deployed and taking data

experiment:grand.name: GRAND

summary.plain: A giant planned array of 200,000 radio antennas spread over a huge area, designed to catch the radio flash from ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and neutrinos. Small test versions are already up and running in China, France and Argentina.

aliases: Gamma Ray Astronomy at PeV EnergieS - phase 3
experiment:grapes-3.name: GRAPES-3

summary.plain: GRAPES-3 pairs 400 scintillator panels with a 560 square metre muon telescope in the Nilgiri hills of southern India. It studies cosmic rays and, through muons, space weather and thunderstorm electric fields.

Five telescopes on a Namibian farm that watch the southern sky for gamma rays: four medium telescopes plus one giant 28-metre telescope, the largest of its kind, run by scientists from more than a dozen countries.

A particle detector at the German laboratory DESY, in Hamburg, that watched electrons and protons collide head-on to map out what a proton is made of. It ran from 1992 until HERA, the collider it depended on, shut down in 2007.

HADES is a magnetic spectrometer at GSI in Darmstadt that records electron-positron pairs and hadrons from proton, pion and heavy-ion collisions at about 1 to 2 GeV per nucleon. It probes the hot, dense, baryon-rich matter found in neutron-star mergers. It has run since before 2004.

An array of seven small telescopes at Hanle in Ladakh, 4270 metres up in the Himalayas, that records the wavefront of the faint light flashes from gamma-ray air showers. It has been observing since 2008.

experiment:happex.energy_regime: 3.48 GeV polarised electron beam in HAPPEX-III (Q^2 = 0.624 GeV^2)

intervals.label: strange form factor programme (HAPPEX-I, HAPPEX-II and HAPPEX-He, HAPPEX-III)

experiment:happex.name: HAPPEX

summary.plain: HAPPEX measured how electrons spinning one way or the other scatter slightly differently from hydrogen and helium nuclei in Jefferson Lab's Hall A. The difference reveals whether strange quarks, absent from a proton's three main quarks, contribute to its charge and magnetism: with the other experiments, to a few percent at most.
A gamma-ray observatory on a Mexican volcano: an array of water tanks 4100 metres up that watches nearly the whole sky at once for the highest-energy light in the universe, day and night.

aliases: Haloscope At Yale Sensitive To Axion CDM

intervals.label: Phase III upgrade (multi-rod cavity) and commissioning at Yale

start.display: after Phase II data-taking ended in August 2024; start of the upgrade not separately dated

key_specs.label: Newly scanned axion mass range (Phase II, 2024-2025)

quantity.display: 18.37 ueV (17.28-19.46 ueV span, two newly scanned sub-bands)

experiment:haystac.name: HAYSTAC

summary.plain: HAYSTAC searches for the axion, a candidate dark-matter particle, at Yale University. A tunable metal cavity inside a strong magnet, cooled and read out with quantum-noise-reducing electronics, listens for a faint radio signal the axion would produce.

intervals.label: prototype detector (natural Ge crystals) at LNGS
inner crystal replaced by enriched 73Ge; final setup installed
final setup (enriched 73Ge inner crystal) taking data

key_specs.label: Exposure of the spin-dependent WIMP-neutron limit

summary.plain: HDMS, the Heidelberg Dark Matter Search, was a germanium experiment under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy. A small germanium crystal sat inside a larger one that vetoed stray radiation, so it could look for dark matter particles recoiling off germanium nuclei. It reported limits on how strongly such particles can interact.

A cluster of cosmic-ray and gamma-ray detectors on the mountaintop of La Palma that ran from 1987 to 2002. Its team of stereoscopic Cherenkov telescopes demonstrated the advantages of stereoscopic observation, continued by its successors MAGIC and H.E.S.S.

key_specs.label: Active mass of the five enriched detectors

summary.plain: A germanium experiment in the Gran Sasso tunnel that looked for neutrinoless double beta decay from 1990 to 2003. Five detectors made of germanium enriched in 76Ge served as source and detector at once. It set one of the strongest limits of its day on the Majorana neutrino mass; part of the team later claimed a signal.

HERA-B was an experiment at DESY that placed thin wires in the halo of HERA's 920 GeV proton beam so that protons struck the wires and produced B mesons and J/psi particles, built to study the matter-antimatter asymmetry (CP violation) in B meson decays. It ran from 2000 to 2003.

aliases: Helium Roton Apparatus for Light Dark Matter

intervals.label: concept proposed (superfluid helium, calorimetric readout) and R&D
planned installation of the TESSERACT setups (including HeRALD) at LSM

key_specs.label: Lowest mass reachable with the prototype threshold

experiment:herald.name: HeRALD

summary.plain: HeRALD is a dark matter detector that uses a small bath of superfluid helium, cooled to near absolute zero, and superconducting sensors that detect both flashes of light and individual helium atoms boiled off the surface. It is part of TESSERACT and is proposed for the Modane underground laboratory.

experiment:hermes.energy_regime: 27.5 GeV lepton beam of HERA on internal gas targets
experiment:hermes.name: HERMES

summary.plain: HERMES shot HERA's high-energy positron or electron beam through very thin, spin-polarised gas targets of hydrogen, deuterium and helium to study how the spins of quarks and gluons add up to the spin of the proton and neutron. It took data from 1995 to 2007.

intervals.label: HiRes prototype and MIA muon array (hybrid)

summary.plain: HiRes was a pair of fluorescence telescopes in the Utah desert, a sharper successor to Fly's Eye. Operating 1997-2006, it reported the first observation of the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin suppression of the highest-energy cosmic rays.

intervals.label: funded by the European Research Council
ERC grant period: design and set-up of the experiment

key_specs.label: Decay events recorded in the 2025 result

summary.plain: An experiment in Italy that weighs the electron neutrino by watching holmium-163 atoms decay inside ultra-cold detectors. Its first result, from two months of data in 2025, limits the neutrino mass to 27 electron-volts at 90% credibility.

A tank of dry-cleaning fluid nearly a mile underground in a South Dakota gold mine, run for decades by Ray Davis, that made the first detection of solar neutrinos and found far fewer than expected: a puzzle that lasted until the turn of the century.

intervals.label: JLab approval of 165 days of running

summary.plain: HPS fires electrons from Jefferson Lab onto a thin tungsten foil and looks for electron-positron pairs that would reveal a hypothetical 'dark photon' - a new light force carrier tied to dark matter - either as a narrow bump in mass or as a pair born a little downstream of the target.

experiment:hrs.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at 29 GeV centre-of-mass energy at PEP
experiment:hrs.name: High Resolution Spectrometer (HRS) at PEP

summary.plain: A general-purpose detector at SLAC's PEP electron-positron ring that took data from the end of 1981. It tested quantum electrodynamics and the electroweak theory, searched for scalar electrons and studied hadron production. Its end date is not documented in the sources found.

The next, much bigger version of Super-Kamiokande, being built in a newly dug cavern near the original detector. When it starts up later this decade it will use the same J-PARC neutrino beam and look for a difference between how neutrinos and antineutrinos behave, hunt for proton decay, and watch for supernovae.

IAXO is a planned next-generation axion helioscope at DESY, a much larger successor to CAST. Its intermediate prototype, BabyIAXO, is currently under construction, while the full-scale instrument remains a proposal.

The first big liquid-argon neutrino detector ever built. It ran under an Italian mountain from 2010-2013, was rebuilt at CERN, and now sits at Fermilab as the far detector in a hunt for a possible fourth kind of neutrino.

experiment:icecube.energy_regime: About 10 GeV (DeepCore threshold) to the PeV scale and above for in-ice neutrinos; 300 TeV to 1 EeV cosmic rays with IceTop
experiment:icecube.name: IceCube

summary.plain: A cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice at the South Pole turned into a telescope. More than five thousand light sensors frozen deep in the ice catch the faint flashes made when a neutrino from space crashes into the ice.

The planned successor to IceCube: about eight times the volume of ice, ten thousand light sensors and a huge radio antenna array, designed to catch many more neutrinos and the most energetic ones of all.

intervals.label: science data-taking with the rest of IceCube (planned)

summary.plain: New, more sensitive light detectors added to the middle of IceCube. They let the observatory see lower-energy neutrinos more sharply and help scientists understand the ice itself, which improves every measurement IceCube has already made.

intervals.label: dark matter phase of IGEX at Canfranc (one enriched 76Ge detector)

summary.plain: IGEX-DM was the dark matter search of the International Germanium Experiment. One 2-kilogram germanium crystal, made for a rare-decay study, was used deep under the Pyrenees at Canfranc to look for dark matter particles recoiling off germanium, and set limits on their interaction.

key_specs.label: Fiducial mass for the proton-decay search

summary.plain: A tank of ultrapure water in an Ohio salt mine, watched by 2,048 light sensors, that began taking data in 1982 to look for the decay of protons. It found none, but on 23 February 1987 it caught eight neutrinos from supernova 1987A.

InDEx is an Indian dark matter search using small superheated droplet detectors, 555 metres underground at Jaduguda in Jharkhand. Its first two runs found no dark matter and set limits on how strongly light WIMPs could interact.

intervals.label: recommended for approval; construction and installation

summary.plain: One of the four original detectors at DESY's PETRA collider, built by groups from Japan, Germany and England (the name comes from the three countries). It recorded e+e- collisions from 1979 to 1986 and contributed three-jet evidence for the gluon and an early measurement of the strong coupling.

A proposed multi-kiloton liquid-scintillator detector in the deepest underground laboratory in the world, under Jinping Mountain in Sichuan, China, to measure solar neutrinos and geoneutrinos with very low background. A one-tonne prototype has been designed.

intervals.label: proposed to the J-PARC programme advisory committee

summary.plain: A planned experiment at J-PARC in Japan that will store cooled and accelerated muons in a compact magnet to measure their magnetic anomaly and electric dipole moment by a method completely different from the Fermilab and Brookhaven experiments. Its beamline and apparatus are being built.

aliases: J-PARC Sterile Neutrino Search at J-PARC Spallation Neutron Source

intervals.label: proposal submitted to the J-PARC PAC
stage-1 approval to start of construction
long physics runs with the 24 m detector

key_specs.label: Proton beam power on the mercury target

experiment:jsns2.name: JSNS2

summary.plain: A neutrino detector on the third floor of J-PARC's neutron and muon facility in Japan. It listens for antineutrinos from muons stopping in a mercury target, to test whether a fourth, sterile kind of neutrino explains an unexplained excess seen long ago at the LSND experiment.

intervals.label: detector installation (support structure, acrylic vessel, PMTs)
final construction stage: water and liquid-scintillator filling

summary.plain: A giant underground detector in southern China that studies neutrinos from nearby nuclear power reactors. It began taking data in 2025 and aims to work out the ordering of neutrino masses and measure their oscillations with world-leading precision.

A small, very precise antineutrino detector being installed in a basement at the Taishan nuclear power plant. Cooled to minus 50 degrees and read out by silicon light sensors, it will measure the reactor spectrum with unprecedented resolution as a reference for the larger JUNO detector 53 km away.

aliases: KEK to Kamioka long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment
experiment:k2k.name: K2K (KEK to Kamioka)

summary.plain: The world's first long-baseline neutrino experiment: a beam of neutrinos made at KEK's proton accelerator was sent 250 km through the Earth to the Super-Kamiokande detector, to check whether the atmospheric neutrino puzzle Super-K had already seen was really neutrino oscillation.

quantity.display: 4500 t total (680-1040 t fiducial, depending on analysis)

summary.plain: A tank of water deep in a Japanese mine, built in 1983 to look for protons decaying. It never saw one, but in February 1987 it caught a handful of neutrinos from a supernova exploding in a nearby galaxy - the first time anyone had detected neutrinos from a star other than the Sun.

intervals.label: first-results exposure used in the 2002 discovery paper
KamLAND2 upgrade: detector dismantling and rebuilding (no data taking)

summary.plain: A huge detector in a Japanese mine that watches antineutrinos from nuclear power plants across the country, and in 2002 gave the first direct proof that they disappear the way solar-neutrino theories predicted.

aliases: Kamioka Liquid-scintillator Anti-Neutrino Detector Zero-neutrino double-beta decay search

end.display: FY2028-2029 (KamLAND2-Zen start; marked "??" on the slide)

intervals.label: KamLAND2-Zen upgrade: dismantling of KamLAND (no data taking)

experiment:kamland-zen.name: KamLAND-Zen

summary.plain: A xenon-loaded balloon of liquid suspended inside the KamLAND detector deep under a Japanese mountain, searching for a rare radioactive process in xenon atoms. Its latest result sets one of the strongest limits yet on the process.

aliases: KArlsruhe Rutherford Medium Energy Neutrino experiment
experiment:karmen.energy_regime: Stopped-pion/muon-decay neutrinos from an 800 MeV proton beam stop (few tens of MeV neutrino energies)

intervals.label: outer veto installation / start of KARMEN 2

experiment:karmen.name: KARMEN

summary.plain: A neutrino experiment at the ISIS particle accelerator in England, running from 1990 to 2001. A tank of liquid holding light sensors sat 18 metres from where the beam stopped, watching for neutrinos changing type on the way. It found no such change and helped test a puzzling result from a similar experiment in the United States.

aliases: KArlsruhe Shower Core and Array DEtector
experiment:kascade.name: KASCADE

summary.plain: KASCADE was an array of particle detectors on the Karlsruhe research campus that measured the electrons, muons and hadrons of cosmic-ray air showers. It showed the "knee" of the spectrum comes from light elements running out.

aliases: KArlsruhe Shower Core and Array DEtector - Grande
experiment:kascade-grande.name: KASCADE-Grande

summary.plain: KASCADE-Grande stretched the KASCADE array to 0.5 square kilometres with 37 scintillator stations recycled from an Italian experiment. It found a second, "heavy" knee in the cosmic-ray spectrum near 80 PeV.

intervals.label: TRISTAN phase: commissioning of the new detector system

summary.plain: A giant spectrometer in Germany that weighs neutrinos indirectly, by measuring electrons released when radioactive tritium decays. Its latest result shows the neutrino weighs no more than 0.45 electron-volts.

Five BICEP2-style telescopes on one mount at the South Pole that watched the same patch of sky as BICEP2 with more detectors and more colours, from 2012 until late 2019 when BICEP Array replaced them.

The universal magnetic detector at the Budker Institute's VEPP-4M collider in Novosibirsk, taking data since 2002. Because the beam energy is calibrated to about one part in a million by resonant depolarisation, KEDR measured the J/psi, psi(2S) and D meson masses and the tau lepton mass with record precision.

intervals.label: WIMP-search data taking with CsI(Tl) crystals
stable running of the 12-crystal (103.4 kg) array

summary.plain: KIMS (Korea Invisible Mass Search) was an array of cesium-iodide crystals, 103.4 kg in all, deep in a tunnel at the Yangyang power plant in South Korea, built to catch dark matter particles. It saw no signal and set limits, including on regions claimed by the DAMA experiment.

intervals.label: NaI(Tl) data taking for the published limits

summary.plain: KIMS-NaI was the sodium-iodide stage of the Korean KIMS programme: the team grew its own low-radioactivity crystals, tested them underground at Yangyang and set dark-matter limits with two of them. A planned 200 kg array became, together with a US group, the COSINE-100 experiment.

An experiment at Frascati's DAΦNE phi factory that took data from about 1999 to 2006. Its 4-metre drift chamber and lead-fibre calorimeter recorded phi-meson decays, giving results on kaon properties, hadronic cross sections and the muon's magnetic moment. With its successor KLOE-2 it recorded around 8 inverse femtobarns.

The upgraded KLOE experiment at Frascati's DAΦNE, which took data from November 2014 to March 2018. With KLOE it recorded about 8 inverse femtobarns, which CERN Courier called in 2018 the largest ever sample collected at the phi-resonance peak. It added a cylindrical GEM inner tracker and tested crab-waist collisions with a detector solenoid.

An experiment using two neutrino telescopes built into the floor of the Mediterranean Sea, one off Sicily and one off France, to catch faint flashes of light from neutrinos arriving from space and from Earth's atmosphere.

aliases: Kolar Gold Fields proton decay experiment

key_specs.label: Depth of the Phase I detector

experiment:kolar-gold-fields-experiments.name: Kolar Gold Fields experiments

summary.plain: Experiments in the deep Kolar Gold Fields mines of southern India, from 1960 to 1993. They recorded some of the first atmospheric neutrinos in 1965, then searched for proton decay with iron-and-counter detectors, claiming candidate events that other experiments have not confirmed.

KOTO is a Japanese experiment at J-PARC that watches for an extremely rare kaon decay into a neutral pion and two invisible neutrinos, testing the same physics as NA62 but with the neutral, longer-lived kind of kaon.

intervals.label: proposal submitted to the J-PARC PAC; Stage-1 status recommended

summary.plain: A proposed next-generation experiment at J-PARC in Japan to measure how often a long-lived neutral kaon decays into a neutral pion and two neutrinos, a very rare process that is sensitive to new physics. It was submitted in December 2024 and received first-stage recommendation in April 2025.

KTeV was a Fermilab experiment in the 1990s that studied neutral kaon decays, showing that nature's matter-antimatter asymmetry (CP violation) can happen directly inside a kaon's decay, at the same time as CERN's NA48 was making the same discovery.

experiment:l3.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 209 GeV by 2000)
experiment:l3.name: L3

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, built to measure electrons, muons and photons with exceptional precision using bismuth-germanate crystals and a huge magnet.

aliases: Large Enriched Germanium Experiment for Neutrinoless ββ Decay
experiment:legend.name: LEGEND

summary.plain: LEGEND combines the expertise of two earlier experiments, GERDA and the Majorana Demonstrator, to search for a rare radioactive process in germanium atoms deep under an Italian mountain. Its first stage, LEGEND-200, began taking data in 2023; a larger stage, LEGEND-1000, is planned.

aliases: Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory
experiment:lhaaso.name: LHAASO

summary.plain: A high-altitude Chinese observatory that measures cosmic rays and hunts for the highest-energy gamma rays in the sky, using several kinds of detectors together on a mountain 4410 metres up.

experiment:lhcb.energy_regime: Proton-proton collisions at 7-13.6 TeV centre-of-mass energy at the LHC, plus heavy-ion and fixed-target (SMOG) running

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 2 / LHCb Upgrade I installation
Long Shutdown 3 / ECAL and RICH enhancements

experiment:lhcb.name: LHCb

summary.plain: LHCb is one of the four big experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. Instead of surrounding the collision point on all sides, its detector is shaped like a single forward cone, built to catch particles containing beauty and charm quarks and study why the universe has so much more matter than antimatter.

experiment:lhcf.energy_regime: LHC proton-proton (and light-ion) collisions, run mainly during early low-luminosity periods of each LHC run
experiment:lhcf.name: LHCf

summary.plain: LHCf uses two small detectors, 140 metres either side of CERN's ATLAS collision point, to study particles thrown almost exactly forward by LHC collisions -- data used to help interpret how cosmic rays create showers when they hit Earth's atmosphere.

experiment:lsnd.energy_regime: Stopped-pion/muon-decay neutrinos from an 800 MeV LAMPF/LANSCE proton beam
experiment:lsnd.name: LSND

summary.plain: A tank of mineral oil at Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico, that watched for neutrinos changing type just 30 metres from where an accelerator beam produced them. From 1993 to 1998 it reported more electron-antineutrinos than expected, a puzzling result that later experiments tried to confirm or rule out.

LUX was a dark matter detector holding about a third of a tonne of liquid xenon, run from 2013 to 2016 in the same underground hall in South Dakota that LZ uses now. It found no dark matter, and set the tightest limits of its day.

experiment:lz.energy_regime: keV-scale nuclear recoils from WIMPs of a few GeV/c² to hundreds of TeV/c²
experiment:lz.name: LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ)

summary.plain: LZ is a dark matter experiment a mile underground in South Dakota. It watches seven tonnes of liquid xenon for the tiny flash of light expected if a dark matter particle hits a xenon nucleus. It began taking data at the end of 2021 and has seen no such particle so far.

experiment:mac.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at 29 GeV centre-of-mass energy at PEP
experiment:mac.name: MAC

summary.plain: A detector at SLAC's PEP ring that captured all the energy of electron-positron collisions in a large magnetised calorimeter. It tested quantum chromodynamics, measured electroweak effects in muon pairs and measured the lifetime of the B meson. It ran from about 1980 to 1986.

A 21 metre mirror telescope at Hanle in the Indian Himalayas that catches the faint flashes from gamma-ray air showers. At 4270 metres it is the highest telescope of its kind and has watched the Crab Nebula since 2021.

intervals.label: data taking with the detector under construction
data taking with the full detector

summary.plain: A very large detector, about 77 metres long, in a hall of the Gran Sasso laboratory under the mountain. From 1989 to 2000 it hunted magnetic monopoles and recorded muons made by atmospheric neutrinos coming up through the Earth, whose deficit fits neutrino oscillation.

aliases: Major Atmospheric Gamma Imaging Cherenkov Telescopes
experiment:magic.name: MAGIC

summary.plain: Two 17-metre telescopes on a mountain in the Canary Islands that catch the faint blue flashes gamma rays make when they hit the atmosphere.

intervals.label: construction of the experiment at MESA

summary.plain: MAGIX (Mainz Gas Injection Target Experiment) will scatter MESA's intense electron beam off a thin gas jet and detect the electrons in two high-resolution spectrometers, to study few-body systems and hadron structure, and to search for a dark photon and other dark-sector particles.

intervals.label: phase II improvement programme (new frozen-T2 source, flow cryostat, background reduction)

summary.plain: A tritium beta-decay experiment at the University of Mainz. A large electrostatic filter measured the electron spectrum just below its endpoint to weigh the electron antineutrino. Its final result, from data taken 1997-2001, limited the neutrino mass to at most 2.3 electron-volts.

A demonstration experiment nearly a mile underground in a former South Dakota gold mine, using germanium crystals to search for a rare radioactive process. It proved the low-background techniques later scaled up in the LEGEND experiment.

experiment:mark-i.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions up to about 8 GeV total energy (4.8 GeV was the maximum with useful luminosity in the first years)
experiment:mark-i.name: Mark I

summary.plain: The first large detector built to surround an electron-positron collision point, run by a SLAC and Berkeley Lab team at SLAC's SPEAR ring from 1973 to 1977. It co-discovered the J/psi particle in 1974, proving the charm quark, and in 1975 reported the first evidence for the tau lepton.

experiment:mark-ii.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at the SPEAR (7 GeV total), PEP (29 GeV) and SLC (Z pole, 91 GeV) energies
experiment:mark-ii.name: Mark II

summary.plain: The second general-purpose detector at SLAC. It started at the SPEAR ring in 1977, moved to the larger PEP ring in 1979, and in 1987 became the first detector on the Stanford Linear Collider, where it saw its first Z boson decay in April 1989.

The third general-purpose detector at SLAC's SPEAR ring, run from 1981 to 1988 by a collaboration of Caltech, SLAC, Santa Cruz, Illinois and Washington. It was built to collect large samples of D mesons, J/psi and psi-prime decays.

One of the four original detectors at DESY's PETRA collider, built by a collaboration of European, American and Chinese institutes led by Samuel Ting. Its 1979 analysis of the energy flow in e+e- collisions showed three-jet events and supported the existence of the gluon.

aliases: MAssive Timing Hodoscope for Ultra Stable neutraL pArticles

quantity.display: 11 m tall (proposed 40 m × 40 m × 11 m decay volume)

experiment:mathusla.name: MATHUSLA

summary.plain: MATHUSLA is a proposed detector that would sit on the surface at CERN, far above the LHC's underground collisions, to catch new particles so weakly interacting and long-lived that they could fly through ordinary detectors unnoticed.

An experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute in Switzerland that looked for a muon turning directly into an electron and a burst of light -- a decay the Standard Model forbids. It ran from 2009 to 2013 and did not see the decay, setting a new best limit.
The upgraded version of MEG at the same Swiss laboratory, hunting for the same forbidden muon decay with about ten times better sensitivity. It has been taking data since 2021 and is still running.

A 170-tonne liquid-argon camera on Fermilab's Booster neutrino beam, built to find out what caused an earlier experiment's mysterious signal, and along the way to measure neutrino collisions with unprecedented clarity.

key_specs.label: Lower end of gamma-ray energy range

summary.plain: A huge covered pond of water in the mountains of New Mexico, lined with light sensors, that watched the whole overhead sky day and night for TeV gamma rays and cosmic rays from 1999 until 2008. Its sensors were later reused in HAWC.

intervals.label: project initiated at LPSC Grenoble; prototype development
bi-chamber module operating at the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane
first available bi-chamber data set at Modane

key_specs.label: Angular resolution for keV proton recoils

summary.plain: MIMAC is a French dark matter experiment in the Modane underground laboratory. Its low-pressure gas chambers record the three-dimensional track of the nucleus a particle knocks, aiming to show which direction a dark matter particle came from. In 2026 it published its first directional limit.
A compact, finely sliced detector at Fermilab that measured exactly how neutrinos bounce off different atomic nuclei, data that other neutrino experiments need to interpret their own results.

A Fermilab experiment built to settle a puzzling result from an earlier Los Alamos experiment. It watched a beam of neutrinos with a 12-metre sphere of mineral oil from 2002 to 2019, and saw its own unexplained excess of signals.

intervals.label: final assembly, commissioning and cold-gas run

summary.plain: MiniCLEAN was a 500 kg detector of liquid argon (or liquid neon) in the Cube Hall at SNOLAB, Canada, built to test a simple single-phase way of hunting for WIMP dark matter. A cold-gas test run took place in 2017 and SNOLAB reports decommissioning began in 2019. No dark matter result was published.

experiment:minos.energy_regime: On-axis NuMI νμ-dominated beam, peak energy about 3 GeV
experiment:minos.name: MINOS

summary.plain: A neutrino experiment that sent Fermilab's beam 735 kilometres underground to an old iron mine in Minnesota, comparing what arrived to what was measured near the source, from 2005 to 2012.
MINOS's second act: the same two detectors kept running from 2013 to 2016 on a higher-energy beam, hunting for a hypothetical fourth kind of neutrino.

aliases: Monopole and Exotics Detector at the LHC
Monopole and Exotic Particle Detector at the LHC
experiment:moedal.energy_regime: LHC proton-proton (and heavy-ion) collisions at Point 8, 7-13.6 TeV centre-of-mass energy
experiment:moedal.name: MoEDAL

summary.plain: MoEDAL is an unusual CERN experiment that mostly just sits there: sheets of plastic and jars of special metal quietly record the trails of exotic, heavily-charged particles -- like magnetic monopoles -- that might be created in LHC collisions at the LHCb cavern.

aliases: Measurement of a Lepton-Lepton Electroweak Reaction
experiment:moller.energy_regime: 11 GeV longitudinally polarised electron beam on a liquid-hydrogen target
experiment:moller.name: MOLLER

summary.plain: MOLLER, now being installed at Jefferson Lab, will measure the tiny difference in how left- and right-spinning electrons scatter off other electrons. That reveals the electron's weak charge, a precision test of the Standard Model sensitive to new physics at multi-TeV mass scales.

intervals.label: construction and surface commissioning at Milano-Bicocca
background and neutron-sensitivity measurements underground at LNGS
completed as a dark matter search (equipment repurposed for fast neutrons)

key_specs.label: Target liquid in the 18 L vessel (LNGS)

summary.plain: MOSCAB (Materia OSCura A Bolle, 'dark matter with bubbles') was a bubble chamber of superheated fluorine-rich liquid, built to look for dark matter and tested at Milano-Bicocca and then at Gran Sasso. No dark matter result was published; in 2021 the equipment was reported as used to detect fast neutrons.

intervals.label: construction (detector components in production and assembly)

summary.plain: MPD (Multi-Purpose Detector) is the main detector for heavy-ion collisions at JINR's NICA collider. It is being assembled around a large superconducting solenoid and is to be moved to the collision point by the end of October 2026 for the collider's xenon run, to study dense nuclear matter.

intervals.label: DOE CD-3 construction approval and construction

summary.plain: An experiment being built at Fermilab that will look for a muon turning directly into an electron without any neutrinos -- something the standard laws of particle physics say should never happen. Construction is under way; no data has been taken yet.

intervals.label: research proposal approved by the PSI research committee
first integration run (parts of the detector in the magnet, beam on target)
cosmic run with a vertex-detector prototype and a fibre ribbon
June 2025 beam time: vertex, fibre and tile modules together in beam
2026 installation of the central detector station

summary.plain: An experiment being built at the Paul Scherrer Institute in Switzerland to look for a muon splitting into three lighter particles (two positrons and an electron), which the Standard Model says essentially never happens. It is still under construction.

intervals.label: proposed at PSI; precursor phase in preparation

summary.plain: A proposed experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute to search for an electric dipole moment of the muon by storing muons in a solenoid with a radial electric field tuned so that the magnetic spin precession cancels (the frozen-spin technique). Its first phase is a precursor demonstration.

An experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute that timed billions of muon decays with a ring of scintillator detectors. It gave the muon’s lifetime to one part in a million, the most precise lifetime of any particle, and from it the strength of the weak force.

intervals.label: storage ring relocated from BNL and reassembled at Fermilab (MC-1)

summary.plain: An experiment at Fermilab that stored muons in a 14-metre magnetic ring and watched them wobble, to measure one of their properties (called g-2) more precisely than ever and test whether unknown particles are secretly tugging on it.

intervals.label: design and construction (lower bound: technical design report)

summary.plain: An experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute that scatters electrons and muons off a hydrogen target at the same time, to find out whether the proton looks the same in both and to help settle the proton radius puzzle.

intervals.label: under construction at the PSI ultracold neutron source

summary.plain: The next-generation neutron electric-dipole-moment experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute, aimed at an order of magnitude better sensitivity than its predecessor. It uses two stacked storage chambers and a huge magnetically shielded room, and is being commissioned.

intervals.label: ion-beam data taking (oxygen and sulphur beams)

summary.plain: HELIOS was a CERN experiment that sent oxygen and sulphur ions into heavy targets and surrounded the target with calorimeters to measure how much energy sprayed sideways. It found energy densities near those where lattice QCD expects quarks and gluons to be freed.

intervals.label: data taking (light-ion beams at 60A and 200A GeV)

summary.plain: NA35 was one of the first CERN experiments to collide oxygen and sulphur nuclei at the SPS. Its streamer chamber photographed whole collisions and found that central sulphur-sulphur collisions produce many more strange particles than proton collisions, an early hint of quark-gluon plasma.

intervals.label: data taking (proton, oxygen and sulphur beams)

summary.plain: NA38 was a CERN experiment that counted pairs of muons produced when oxygen and sulphur ions hit uranium and other targets. It reported that J/psi particles were made less often in the most violent collisions, an early sign later linked to quark-gluon plasma.

end.display: after the 1995 lead run; not later than the end of the SPS lead programme

intervals.label: data taking (p, S and Pb beams)

start.display: after the 1995 lead run; not later than the end of the SPS lead programme

summary.plain: NA44 was a small CERN spectrometer that picked out pions, kaons and protons near mid-rapidity in proton, sulphur and lead collisions. How their momenta and pair correlations changed with system size showed that the fireball expands outward and then freezes out.

CERES (NA45) was a CERN experiment that detected pairs of electrons and positrons from heavy-ion collisions, a clean probe of the hot, dense matter. It found more low-mass electron pairs than hadron decays can explain, from sulphur-gold to lead-gold collisions, 1992 to 2000.

intervals.label: NA48 main run (direct CP violation, KL/KS beams)
NA48/2 (charged-kaon CP violation and rare decays)

summary.plain: NA48 was a CERN experiment that ran from the late 1990s to the mid-2000s, confirming that nature's matter-antimatter asymmetry (CP violation) can arise directly inside a kaon's decay, not just from how kaons mix. It was the direct predecessor of NA62 at the same underground cavern.

NA49 was a large detector at CERN's SPS that recorded lead-lead and other collisions to look for the transition to quark-gluon plasma. Its energy scan found sudden changes in particle production near 30 GeV per nucleon, evidence for where plasma formation starts.

NA50 was a CERN experiment that fired lead ions at lead targets and counted pairs of muons from J/psi particles. It found that J/psi production in central collisions was unexpectedly low, an effect called anomalous J/psi suppression and seen as a sign of quark-gluon plasma.

NA57 continued WA97's study of strange particles in lead-lead collisions at CERN after the programme moved from the West Area to the North Area, extending the centrality range and adding a lower beam energy to study how hyperon enhancement depends on energy.

NA60 was a CERN experiment that measured pairs of muons from indium-indium collisions with a vertex detector placed close to the target. It found a strong broadening of the rho meson and extra J/psi suppression in collisions with many participants, following up NA50.

aliases: SPS Heavy Ion and Neutrino Experiment

intervals.label: approved by the CERN Research Board

experiment:na61-shine.name: NA61/SHINE

summary.plain: NA61/SHINE studies what happens when protons and nuclei collide with fixed targets at CERN's SPS. It scans collision energy and system size to look for the onset of quark-gluon plasma formation and a critical point, and measures hadron production needed for neutrino and cosmic-ray experiments.

intervals.label: long shutdown / detector upgrades before Run 2

summary.plain: NA62 is a CERN experiment that fires a beam of charged kaons at a detector to catch one of the rarest particle decays known: a positive kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos. Catching enough of these decays tests the Standard Model.

NA64 is a CERN experiment that fires an electron beam into a block of material and watches for missing energy -- a sign that an invisible, unknown particle escaped. It searches for dark photons and other hidden particles.

An experiment at the Spallation Neutron Source in Oak Ridge that studies how free neutrons decay. A long magnetic spectrometer guides the decay electron and proton to two silicon detectors, to measure how they are correlated and so test the Standard Model’s weak interaction. It is being commissioned and has begun taking data.

NaIAD was an array of sodium iodide crystals in the Boulby mine in north-east England that searched for dark matter from 2000 to 2003. It saw no dark matter and, for a time, set the tightest limits on dark matter that interacts through spin.

The Neutral Detector at the VEPP-2M collider of the Budker Institute in Novosibirsk, proposed in 1977 and run from 1982 to 1987. Its calorimeter of sodium iodide crystals detected photons from electron-positron collisions and yielded many new results on light mesons. It was the forerunner of SND.

A planned neutron electric-dipole-moment experiment at the Spallation Neutron Source in Oak Ridge, aiming at a precision two orders of magnitude better than the current limit. It will make ultracold neutrons in superfluid helium at 0.5 kelvin, and is being constructed.

A cylindrical detector in the Modane laboratory, under the Frejus mountain, that followed the two electrons of double beta decay track by track. From 2003 to 2010 it studied seven isotopes, mainly molybdenum-100, and found no neutrinoless decay.

aliases: Neutrino Experiment for Oscillation at Short baseline

intervals.label: NEOS-II data taking (one full fuel cycle)

experiment:neos.name: NEOS

summary.plain: A one-tonne liquid-scintillator detector placed in a gallery 24 metres from a commercial reactor core in Korea, used to look for a hypothetical sterile neutrino. It ran in 2015-16 and again in 2018-20 and found no sign of oscillation to one.

key_specs.label: Distance range from the reactor core

summary.plain: A movable detector on rails beside a compact research reactor in Dimitrovgrad, Russia, used to look for a hypothetical sterile neutrino. Its team reported an oscillation signal of about three standard deviations, which other experiments, including PROSPECT, later disfavoured.

aliases: Failure of parity conservation in meson decays
experiment:nevis-parity-muon-decay.name: Nevis parity-violation experiment in pion and muon decay

summary.plain: In January 1957, after Chien-Shiung Wu reported at Christmas 1956 that cobalt-60 decay violated parity, Richard Garwin, Leon Lederman and Marcel Weinrich used Columbia's Nevis cyclotron to make polarized muons and saw a large asymmetry in where the decay electrons went: a clear break of mirror symmetry.

aliases: NEw generation WIMP search with an Advanced Gaseous tracking device Experiment

experiment:newage.name: NEWAGE

summary.plain: NEWAGE is a Japanese dark matter experiment in the Kamioka mine that tries to tell which way a dark matter particle came from. It tracks the recoil of a nucleus in a low-pressure CF4 gas chamber, which could show whether recoils point back along the direction of the Solar System's motion through the Galaxy.

NEWS-G hunts for very light dark matter particles using a large hollow copper ball filled with gas, deep underground. A small 60 cm version ran in France; a bigger 135 cm sphere has been running at SNOLAB in Canada since 2021.

aliases: Nuclear Emulsions for WIMP Search with directional measurement

demonstration and pilot runs at LNGS (equatorial-telescope run in progress in 2024)

experiment:newsdm.name: NEWSdm

summary.plain: NEWSdm is a directional dark matter project that uses nuclear emulsion, a photographic film with nanometre-sized grains, to record the tiny tracks of recoiling nuclei. The film sits on a telescope mount that follows the sky. Prototype runs are done at Gran Sasso; a first limit from a surface exposure appeared in 2023.

intervals.label: US-led project paused (listed by SNOLAB, December 2024)

summary.plain: A planned successor to EXO-200: a much bigger liquid-xenon detector, holding five tonnes of xenon, proposed for the SNOLAB underground laboratory in Canada. It would search for the same rare radioactive process, with far greater sensitivity.

aliases: Neutrino Experiment with a Xenon TPC
experiment:next.name: NEXT

summary.plain: A detector at an underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees that uses high-pressure xenon gas, rather than liquid, to search for a rare radioactive process. Its main detector, NEXT-100, started running in 2024.

experiment:nist-bl1.name: NIST beam neutron lifetime experiment BL1

summary.plain: The first of the NIST beam-method measurements of the neutron lifetime. It counted the decay protons from a cold-neutron beam trapped in a magnetic and electric field and, with a better calibration of the neutron counter in 2013, gave a lifetime of 887.7 seconds.

intervals.label: data taking with the BL2 apparatus

experiment:nist-bl2.name: NIST beam neutron lifetime experiment BL2

summary.plain: The second NIST beam neutron-lifetime experiment, using largely the same apparatus as the first to study systematic effects. Its 2018-2020 data led to a 2025 study of how molecular hydrogen in the vacuum could affect such measurements; no BL2 lifetime has been reported.

start.display: after the facility returns to operation, expected in 2027

experiment:nist-bl3.name: NIST beam neutron lifetime experiment BL3

summary.plain: The next-generation NIST neutron-lifetime experiment, under construction. It uses a larger magnet, proton trap and neutron beam to measure the lifetime to better than 0.3 seconds with the beam method and to test the method’s systematic effects.

intervals.label: first operation (CERN Courier: began operation in 1993)

summary.plain: A magnetic detector at CERN that looked for muon neutrinos turning into tau neutrinos by measuring every visible particle precisely and spotting the missing momentum of a tau decay. It ran in 1995-98, found no signal, and limited the mixing to below about 0.00033 at large mass differences.

experiment:nova.energy_regime: Off-axis NuMI wide-band beam peaked at 1.8 GeV

experiment:nova.name: NOvA

summary.plain: A long-distance neutrino experiment: when Fermilab's NuMI beam runs, it fires neutrinos 810 kilometres through the Earth to northern Minnesota, where NOvA watches how they change type, to learn about neutrino masses and matter-antimatter asymmetry. The beam has been off since July 2024.
A very small, super-cold detector at a French nuclear power plant, sitting closer to the reactor core than any similar experiment, built to catch antineutrinos at the gentlest nudges ever attempted.

start.display: between March 1985 and July 2004; end of data taking not stated in any source consulted

summary.plain: A 150-ton detector of iron plates and gas tubes in a cave beside the Mont Blanc road tunnel, under about five thousand metres of water-equivalent rock. It began running in 1982 to look for protons decaying, recorded a few proton-decay candidate events, none confirmed, and measured the atmospheric-neutrino flux.

A Fermilab experiment in 1996-97 that fired separate beams of almost pure neutrinos and antineutrinos at a 690-tonne detector to measure the weak mixing angle precisely. Its value came out three standard deviations away from the Standard Model prediction, a puzzle still discussed.

experiment:opal.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 209 GeV by 2000)

quantity.display: ~12 m long x 12 m high x 12 m wide

experiment:opal.name: OPAL

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, built as a layered, general-purpose apparatus about the size of a house to catch every kind of particle from the collisions.

experiment:opera.energy_regime: GeV-scale muon-neutrino beam from SPS protons on a graphite target (CNGS)
experiment:opera.name: OPERA

summary.plain: An experiment in a mountain tunnel in Italy that caught neutrinos fired 732 kilometres through the Earth from CERN in Switzerland. Its photographic-film-and-lead detector directly caught tau neutrinos appearing from a beam that started as muon neutrinos, proving they change type over the trip.

summary.plain: ORPHEUS searched for dark matter with a cloud of tiny tin grains kept just below the point where they stop being superconducting, in the University of Bern's shallow underground laboratory. A particle hit can flip one grain, which a coil senses as a magnetic change. It took data in 2002 and 2003 and published first results in 2004.

experiment:oscura.name: Oscura

summary.plain: Oscura is a proposed dark matter experiment that would use about 10 kilograms of ultra-quiet silicon CCD sensors to look for particles lighter than a proton. It is planned for SNOLAB, deep underground in Canada. Its design stage is finished, but funding for the full experiment has not been secured.

summary.plain: A planned neutrino telescope for the deep Pacific Ocean off Canada's west coast, building on an undersea science network. A small pathfinder instrument has been actively taking data there since 2019, proving the technology, while the full telescope and its first production line are still being built.

summary.plain: P2 will measure the weak mixing angle, a basic number of the Standard Model, with unprecedented precision at low energy by scattering spin-polarised electrons from the new MESA accelerator in Mainz off hydrogen and measuring the tiny parity-violating asymmetry.

experiment:padme.name: PADME

summary.plain: An experiment at Frascati's Beam Test Facility that sends pulsed positrons from the DAΦNE linac into a thin diamond target to look for a dark photon, and in 2022 scanned the beam energy for a hypothetical 17 MeV particle, the X17. It has set new limits.

A detector in a shallow underground laboratory about 800 metres from the three reactors of the Palo Verde power station in Arizona. From 1998 to 2000 it looked for antineutrinos disappearing on the way from the reactors and, like CHOOZ, found no oscillation.

intervals.label: construction (detector components being built and deployed)

summary.plain: PANDA is a planned detector at the future FAIR facility that will collide antiprotons with a hydrogen target to study how quarks and gluons form hadrons. It will search for exotic particles such as glueballs and hybrids, charm spectroscopy, hypernuclei and nucleon structure.

aliases: Particle and Astrophysical Xenon Detector 4 Ton
experiment:pandax-4t.name: PandaX-4T

summary.plain: PandaX-4T was a dark matter detector holding four tonnes of liquid xenon, deep under a mountain at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory. It took data in three runs from 2021 and was shut down in April 2026, searching for dark matter particles bumping into xenon nuclei.

PandaX-I was the first stage of the Chinese PandaX liquid xenon dark matter programme, in the Jinping underground laboratory in Sichuan. It ran for about five months in 2014 with a few tens of kilograms of xenon, saw no dark matter, and ruled out several low-mass claims.

PandaX-II was the second stage of the Chinese PandaX programme: a half-tonne liquid xenon detector in the Jinping underground laboratory, running from 2016 to 2019. It saw no dark matter and, in 2016-2017, set the strongest limits then published.

aliases: PandaX-III neutrinoless double beta decay experiment
experiment:pandax-iii.name: PandaX-III

summary.plain: A planned high-pressure xenon-gas detector for the Jinping underground laboratory in China, meant to look for neutrinoless double beta decay of xenon-136 by recording the tracks of the two electrons. The detector has been built and tested above ground; installation underground was still pending in 2023.

PandaX-xT is a proposed multi-ten-tonne liquid xenon observatory at the Jinping underground laboratory in China, an upgrade of PandaX-4T. It would search for dark matter and for neutrinoless double beta decay, and aims to reach the point where neutrinos become the main background.

An experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute that measured how often a charged pion decays to a positron instead of a muon, a very precise test of whether electrons and muons feel the weak force identically. It took data in 2008-2010; the final result has not been published.

The first big time projection chamber, invented at Berkeley Lab and used at SLAC's PEP ring from 1982 to 1990. It tracked charged particles in three dimensions and identified them from their ionisation, setting the pattern for later detectors at LEP and RHIC and now at the LHC.

A spectrometer at the Institut Laue-Langevin that studies how free neutrons decay, using a pulsed beam of cold neutrons. Its beta-asymmetry measurement gave the neutron’s weak axial coupling constant, a key number in the Standard Model.

aliases: Pioneering High Energy Nuclear Interaction eXperiment
experiment:phenix.name: PHENIX

summary.plain: PHENIX was one of the two large experiments at Brookhaven's RHIC collider, built from four merged detector proposals to study hot nuclear matter. It recorded its first collision in 2000 and stopped taking data in 2016.

PHOBOS was a compact RHIC experiment at Brookhaven that surrounded the collision point with silicon detectors to count nearly all the charged particles made in each gold-gold collision, plus two small spectrometers. It ran from 2000 to 2005.

aliases: Project In CAnada to Search for Supersymmetric Objects

intervals.label: data taking in the SNO gallery and at SNOLAB
final data taking with 32 detector modules
completed (data taking concluded; collaboration merged into PICO)

experiment:picasso.name: PICASSO

summary.plain: PICASSO searched for dark matter with many tiny droplets of a fluorine-rich liquid held in a gel about two kilometres underground at SNOLAB in Canada. A particle hitting a droplet can turn it into a bubble that sensors hear. It set limits on spin-dependent WIMP-proton interactions, and its team merged with COUPP to form PICO.

PICO-2L was the first bubble chamber installed at SNOLAB by the PICO team: two litres of superheated C3F8 refrigerant. It showed that such chambers can reach low energy thresholds and set strong limits on dark matter that couples to nuclear spin.

PICO-40L is the PICO team's current bubble chamber at SNOLAB: a jar of about 70 kg of superheated C3F8 refrigerant turned 'right-side-up' so no water buffer touches the target. It is running now; no physics-results paper has appeared yet.

intervals.label: assembly and construction at SNOLAB (Cube Hall)

summary.plain: PICO-500 is the next, much larger PICO bubble chamber: about 250 litres of superheated C3F8 refrigerant, being assembled underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It is fully funded, still under construction, and has no data yet.

intervals.label: COUPP-60 commissioning and engineering run at Fermilab (MINOS near-detector hall)
C3F8 first blind exposure (1167 kg-days at 3.3 keV)
C3F8 second blind exposure (1404 kg-days at 2.45 keV)

summary.plain: PICO-60 was the largest dark-matter bubble chamber of its day, built at Fermilab as COUPP-60 and run at SNOLAB from 2013 to 2017, first with CF3I and then with C3F8. Its results gave the strongest limits then on dark matter that couples to the spin of the proton.

intervals.label: R&D: thin multilayer NaI(Tl) detectors and radiopure crystals; first low-background measurement at Oto Cosmo Observatory (from September 2007)
low-background measurements in the KamLAND area of the Kamioka underground laboratory

key_specs.label: NaI(Tl) crystal mass of the 2021-2022 measurement

summary.plain: PICOLON is a Japanese search for dark matter with ultra-pure sodium iodide crystals, measured so far with a small crystal deep in the Kamioka mine. It aims to test the yearly signal reported by DAMA/LIBRA with crystals as clean as DAMA's, and plans a 250 kg detector.

An experiment at TRIUMF in Vancouver that compared how often a charged pion decays to a positron and to a muon. Its 2015 result agrees with the Standard Model and tested electron-muon universality to 0.1 per cent.

A giant hybrid detector in Argentina that catches the rarest, most energetic cosmic rays known: water tanks spread over 3000 square kilometres sense particle showers at ground level while telescopes watch the sky for their faint ultraviolet glow.

intervals.label: proposal to the PSI programme advisory committee

summary.plain: A next-generation experiment planned at the Paul Scherrer Institute to measure how often a charged pion decays to an electron rather than a muon, and pion beta decay, to test whether electrons and muons are treated alike. It is approved and in its demonstrator phase.

intervals.label: PLUTO removed from PETRA; replaced by CELLO

summary.plain: A detector that first recorded e+e- collisions at DESY's DORIS ring from 1974 and then moved to the PETRA collider in 1978, where it contributed to the 1979 gluon evidence. CELLO replaced it at PETRA in 1980.

A telescope on a Chilean mountain that, from 2012, measured the polarization of the Big Bang afterglow on small scales, found evidence that gravity bends that light, and was extended into the three-telescope Simons Array.

PRad fired 1.1 and 2.2 GeV electrons at a windowless hydrogen gas target in Hall B of Jefferson Lab and measured scattering at extremely small angles with a calorimeter instead of a magnetic spectrometer. It found a proton charge radius of 0.831 femtometres, smaller than the average of earlier electron-scattering results.

PREX used spinning electron beams on lead to measure the neutron skin of lead-208, how far its neutrons extend beyond its protons. The first run (2010) and the second (PREX-II, 2019) showed a thick skin that matters for the structure of neutron stars.

intervals.label: Phase I: CRES demonstration (University of Washington)

end.display: over by March 2025 (written in the past tense); end date not sourced

intervals.label: Phase II: first CRES measurement of molecular tritium

start.display: no later than December 2022 (first tritium result posted); true start not sourced

intervals.label: Phase III: apparatus R&D (cavity-CRES demonstrators, atomic-tritium source); no data-taking

start.display: 'now entering Phase III' (October 2025); true start not sourced

summary.plain: An experiment that measures the faint radio signal a single electron gives off when it spins in a magnetic field, aiming to weigh the neutrino. It began as a tabletop demonstration at the University of Washington and is now moving toward using real tritium gas.

aliases: Precision Reactor Oscillation and Spectrum Experiment
experiment:prospect.name: PROSPECT

summary.plain: A small antineutrino detector, a few metres from the compact core of a research reactor in Tennessee, used to test whether neutrinos oscillate into a hypothetical fourth "sterile" type and to measure the energy spectrum of antineutrinos from uranium-235 fission.

The CERN experiment that in 1995 made the first atoms of antimatter: nine antihydrogen atoms created in antiproton collisions with xenon in a storage ring. They lasted about forty billionths of a second.

intervals.label: data taking at the PSI ultracold neutron source (2015 to 2017)

summary.plain: The neutron electric-dipole-moment experiment that ran at the Paul Scherrer Institute until 2017. Its 2020 result found the neutron’s dipole moment consistent with zero, with an uncertainty of about one part in 10^26 of an electron charge times a centimetre.

A compact CERN experiment designed to trap antiprotons, carry them by truck to CERN’s ISOLDE facility and annihilate them on short-lived nuclei. The products show how protons and neutrons are spread at the surface of those nuclei.

Qweak measured how electrons spinning one way versus the other scatter differently from protons in a hydrogen target at Jefferson Lab. That tiny asymmetry gave the proton's weak charge, a precision test of the Standard Model, which came out in agreement with it.

A South Korean experiment with two identical detectors near and far from a group of six nuclear reactors, which observed antineutrinos disappearing exactly as neutrino oscillation theory predicts. Data taking ran from 2011 to 2023.

A reactor-neutrino experiment at a French research reactor, using ultra-cold germanium and zinc crystals just a few metres from the reactor core to catch antineutrinos bouncing off whole atomic nuclei.

end.display: drilling resumed in the 2025 season (boreholes drilled at sites 15, 25, 34, 35)

2026 season: five new stations to be brought online (planned)

summary.plain: A radio-antenna neutrino detector being built into the ice at the very top of Greenland's ice sheet, one station at a time, to catch the radio flash from the highest-energy neutrinos from space.

aliases: Rare Objects SEarch with Bolometers UndergrounD

intervals.label: WIMP search with cryogenic bolometers at the (old) Canfranc laboratory

experiment:rosebud.name: ROSEBUD

summary.plain: ROSEBUD was a set of tiny crystals cooled to a few hundredths of a degree above absolute zero, in the Canfranc underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees, built to catch the faint heat from dark matter particles hitting aluminium, oxygen or germanium nuclei. It mainly tested detector materials and cut backgrounds.

aliases: Legacy Survey of Space and Time

intervals.label: Legacy Survey of Space and Time

key_specs.label: Visits per field over the survey

experiment:rubin-lsst.name: Rubin Observatory LSST

summary.plain: A ten-year survey that photographs the whole southern sky every few nights with the largest digital camera ever built, on a Chilean mountaintop. Its repeated images chart dark matter and dark energy and reveal asteroids, exploding stars and a changing sky.

intervals.label: proposal (twin NaI(Tl) detectors at LNGS and SUPL)
PoP and PoP-dry runs with the crystal NaI-33 (prototype data taking)
SABRE North physics detector: facilities, crystal production and installation at LNGS

summary.plain: SABRE North is the Italian half of a twin pair of sodium-iodide dark matter detectors, being built at the Gran Sasso laboratory. It will use ultra-pure crystals of the same material as DAMA/LIBRA to test, with lower background, the yearly signal DAMA/LIBRA reports. Its twin, SABRE South, is in Australia.

intervals.label: proposal (twin NaI(Tl) detectors at LNGS and SUPL)
installation and assembly of SABRE South in SUPL

summary.plain: SABRE South is the Australian half of a twin pair of sodium-iodide dark matter detectors, being assembled 1 km underground in the Stawell gold mine, Victoria. Being in the Southern Hemisphere helps tell a real dark matter signal from seasonal effects, when tested against DAMA/LIBRA's yearly signal. Its twin, SABRE North, is in Italy.
An experiment deep inside a Russian mountain that uses tonnes of liquid gallium metal to catch the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos.

intervals.label: construction (SBC-LAr10 at Fermilab; SBC-SNOLAB for the dark-matter search)
SBC-LAr10 calibration chamber operating at Fermilab (MINOS tunnel)

summary.plain: SBC builds bubble chambers filled with superheated liquid argon that give both bubbles and light when something hits them. A 10-kg test chamber operates in a Fermilab tunnel; an identical, cleaner copy for a low-mass dark matter search is being built at SNOLAB.

The newest and closest of Fermilab's three short-baseline liquid-argon detectors, sitting right next to where the neutrino beam is made so it can measure the beam before anything has a chance to change.

intervals.label: Super Charm-Tau factory project at BINP

summary.plain: The experiment planned for the proposed Super Charm-Tau Factory at the Budker Institute in Novosibirsk: a universal magnetic detector to record the huge samples of charm particles and tau leptons from 2 to 5 GeV collisions. Only a 2018 preliminary design exists.

key_specs.label: Objects with spectra, first five years

summary.plain: A decades-long survey of the sky using one dedicated 2.5-metre telescope in New Mexico. Its early phases imaged half the northern sky and mapped a million galaxies in 3D; the BOSS and eBOSS phases measured cosmic expansion. The current phase maps stars and black holes.

SeaQuest was a Fermilab experiment that fired a proton beam at hydrogen and deuterium targets to measure how down and up antiquarks are distributed differently inside a proton, finishing its analysis in 2025.

experiment:sensei.energy_regime: Sub-GeV dark matter via electron recoils (roughly 500 keV to a few GeV in mass)

intervals.label: science operations at Fermilab MINOS cavern

experiment:sensei.name: SENSEI

summary.plain: SENSEI uses ultra-sensitive silicon chips called skipper CCDs to hunt for very light dark matter particles, so light that they would only knock loose a handful of electrons. It has run in a shielded underground hall at Fermilab near Chicago since 2018.

intervals.label: SPSC review of Technical and Physics Proposal

summary.plain: SHiP is a planned CERN experiment that will dump an intense proton beam into a heavy target and search the debris for new, weakly interacting particles that could explain dark matter and other mysteries. It is approved to be built in the same underground hall once used by NA48 and NA62.

aliases: Silicon Drift Detectors for Hadronic Atom Research by Timing Application

intervals.label: DAΦNE data taking (kaonic hydrogen, helium and deuterium)

experiment:siddharta.name: SIDDHARTA

summary.plain: An upgrade of DEAR at DAΦNE that replaced its charge-coupled-device X-ray cameras with fast silicon drift detectors, cutting the background. Its 2009 run gave the most precise kaonic hydrogen X-ray values and first gaseous-target kaonic helium results, and an exploratory kaonic deuterium run.

intervals.label: DAΦNE data taking (SIDDHARTINO pilot run, then SIDDHARTA-2)

summary.plain: The successor to SIDDHARTA at Frascati's DAΦNE, built to measure for the first time the X-rays of kaonic deuterium and other kaonic atoms. After a 2021 pilot run (SIDDHARTINO) it took kaonic helium, neon, hydrogen and deuterium data; a 2026 paper reports the most precise kaonic hydrogen values.

A set of four telescopes on a 5190-metre Chilean mountain, with about 98,000 detectors, that maps the Big Bang afterglow deeply and quickly. It aims to detect the polarization pattern of cosmic inflation and was reported fully online in October 2026.

aliases: Superheated Instrument for Massive ParticLe Experiments

intervals.label: operation at the LSBB (prototype 1999-2000, Phase I 2004-2007, Phase II 2009-2010)
Phase I measurements in the GESA cavern

experiment:simple.name: SIMPLE

summary.plain: SIMPLE searched for dark matter with droplets of a freon liquid held in a gel inside the Low Noise Underground Laboratory (LSBB) in southern France, half a kilometre under a mountain. A particle hit can make a droplet pop into a bubble that microphones record. Its Phase II results set limits on spin-dependent WIMP-proton interactions.

start.display: February 2001 (first shift schedule on the 2001 runs page)

summary.plain: E158 fired a 45 to 48 GeV spin-polarised electron beam into liquid hydrogen at SLAC and measured the tiny difference in scattering from the target's electrons between the two spin directions. It gave the weak mixing angle at low energy and showed that it changes with energy as the Standard Model predicts.

From 1967 MIT and SLAC physicists fired electrons from the new SLAC linear accelerator at hydrogen and deuterium targets. Hard knocks off the proton came out as if from tiny hard grains inside it, the first clear sign of the quarks.

intervals.label: final checkout on the SLC beamline

summary.plain: A general-purpose particle detector at SLAC, near Stanford, California, that used a uniquely highly polarized electron beam to make some of the most precise measurements of how the Z boson decays. It ran from 1991 to 1998.

The Spherical Neutral Detector at the Budker Institute in Novosibirsk, a ball of 1,632 sodium iodide crystals around the collision point. It ran at VEPP-2M from 1995 to 2000, was upgraded and has run at VEPP-2000 since 2010, measuring how electron-positron collisions at 0.4-2 GeV make photons and hadrons.

experiment:snd-lhc.energy_regime: LHC proton-proton collisions (Run 3, 13.6 TeV), sampled via very-forward particle flux
experiment:snd-lhc.name: SND@LHC

summary.plain: SND@LHC is a compact experiment in a disused CERN tunnel that catches neutrinos produced in LHC collisions, in a direction close to the beam that no other LHC experiment can see. It recorded collision data from 2022 until the LHC's current maintenance shutdown began in 2026.

intervals.label: detector construction (clean room, acrylic vessel, PMT support, water fill)

summary.plain: A detector two kilometres underground in a Canadian nickel mine, filled with 1000 tonnes of heavy water. Its neutral-current measurement gave direct evidence that electron neutrinos produced in the Sun change flavour, and a total solar neutrino flux consistent with solar models.
