summary.plain: SNO+ reuses the same underground cavern and acrylic ball that SNO used, now filled with liquid scintillator, to search for a hypothetical nuclear decay and to study solar and reactor neutrinos.

aliases: Search for Oscillations with a Lithium-6 detector
experiment:solid.name: SoLid

summary.plain: A detector built from thousands of small plastic-scintillator cubes, placed just metres from the compact core of the BR2 research reactor in Belgium, to look for sterile neutrinos. It collected data from 2018 to 2020 and has published constraints on the reactor antineutrino anomaly.

SoLID is a planned large detector for Jefferson Lab's Hall A that combines a big solenoid magnet with very high beam intensity. It is designed to image how quarks move inside protons and neutrons, to test the Standard Model with parity-violating scattering, and to study J/psi production near threshold.

A 963-ton iron-and-gas detector, 700 metres down in a Minnesota iron mine, built to search for protons decaying. From 1989 to 2001 it set proton-decay lifetime limits above 10^32 years for some decay modes, and recorded atmospheric neutrinos well enough to see the signature of muon-neutrino oscillation.

The Spin Physics Detector is a planned experiment at JINR's NICA collider to study the spin structure of the proton and deuteron, especially how gluons carry spin, using polarised proton and deuteron beams colliding at up to 27 GeV.

sPHENIX was a house-sized detector at Brookhaven's RHIC collider, built where PHENIX used to be, using a recycled magnet from the BaBar experiment to study the hot soup of quarks and gluons made in nuclear collisions. It took data from 2023 until RHIC's final run ended in February 2026.

intervals.label: SPICE/HeRALD R&D; proposed for LSM as a TESSERACT module
planned installation of the TESSERACT setups (including SPICE) at LSM

summary.plain: SPICE is a dark matter detector that uses small crystals of sapphire, quartz or gallium arsenide, with superconducting sensors that feel the tiniest vibrations a dark matter particle could cause. It is part of TESSERACT and is proposed for the Modane underground laboratory.

experiment:spinquest.energy_regime: 120 GeV proton beam on a polarised fixed target
experiment:spinquest.name: SpinQuest

summary.plain: SpinQuest uses Fermilab's 120 GeV proton beam on a target of spin-aligned protons or deuterons and detects muon pairs from the Drell-Yan process. It asks whether the sea of quark-antiquark pairs inside the proton orbits around the proton's spin axis. It reuses the SeaQuest spectrometer and has had no beam since summer 2024.

A ten-metre microwave telescope at the South Pole that maps the faint afterglow of the Big Bang and finds galaxy clusters in it. It has carried three cameras since 2007; the current one has about 16,000 detectors.

STAR was a house-sized, 1,200-tonne particle detector at Brookhaven National Laboratory that watched gold and other heavy atomic nuclei smash together from 2000 until RHIC's final run ended in February 2026, looking for a hot, liquid-like state of matter called the quark-gluon plasma.

The detector and collaboration for the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility in Hefei, China, a collider planned to make tau leptons and charm hadrons at 2 to 7 GeV, about 100 times more than BESIII, to study exotic hadrons, CP violation and new physics. It is in design and R&D.

A detector divided into six cells, ten metres from the compact core of the research reactor at the Institut Laue-Langevin in Grenoble, built to test whether the missing reactor antineutrinos turned into a hypothetical sterile neutrino. It ran from 2016 to 2020 and rejected that explanation.

intervals.label: SK-II (half PMT density after the 2001 accident)

summary.plain: A tank of 50,000 tonnes of ultra-pure water, a kilometre under a mountain near Kamioka, watched by more than eleven thousand light sensors. It caught the first solid evidence that neutrinos change type as they travel, has watched the Sun in neutrinos for decades, and is the distant target for neutrino beams fired from J-PARC.

experiment:supercdms.energy_regime: Low-mass WIMPs, smaller than about ten proton masses
experiment:supercdms.name: SuperCDMS

summary.plain: SuperCDMS SNOLAB looks for dark matter using silicon and germanium crystals cooled almost to absolute zero. It is the successor to an earlier version of the experiment that ran at the Soudan mine in Minnesota until 2015, and is now starting up nearly a mile underground at SNOLAB in Canada, aiming at very light dark matter particles.

aliases: Super Cryogenic Dark Matter Search at Soudan Mine
experiment:supercdms-soudan.name: SuperCDMS Soudan

summary.plain: The first-generation SuperCDMS dark matter detector, which ran in the Soudan mine in Minnesota from about 2009 until 2015, using an improved version of the CDMS II crystal detectors before the experiment moved to a larger site in Canada.

The first module of SuperNEMO, in the Modane underground laboratory. Thin selenium-82 foils sit between a gas tracker and a wall of plastic scintillators, so each decay electron is followed track by track. It recorded its first double beta event in April 2025.

intervals.label: data taking at the ILL (1998 to 2002)

summary.plain: A neutron electric-dipole-moment experiment at the Institut Laue-Langevin in Grenoble. It stored ultracold neutrons in an electric field and found no sign of a dipole moment, setting the best limit for about a decade.

quantity.display: hundreds of GeV to the PeV scale

summary.plain: A planned array of water tanks on a high plateau in Chile that would watch most of the southern sky for the most energetic gamma rays, day and night. The site is chosen, but the array is not yet built.

intervals.label: first T2K neutrino event observed at Super-Kamiokande
shutdown after the Great East Japan Earthquake
shutdown after the J-PARC hadron-hall radiation accident
T2K-II: operation with the upgraded ND280 and 760 kW beam

summary.plain: A beam of neutrinos made at the J-PARC accelerator in Tokai, on Japan's Pacific coast, is aimed 295 km across the country at the Super-Kamiokande detector under a mountain near Kamioka. By comparing what arrives with what was sent, T2K found that muon neutrinos turn into electron neutrinos, and is now comparing neutrinos with antineutrinos.

aliases: Tunka Advanced Instrument for cosmic rays and Gamma Astronomy
experiment:taiga.name: TAIGA

summary.plain: TAIGA combines three kinds of detector in a Siberian valley: light stations, imaging telescopes and particle counters. Together they hunt for PeV gamma rays and measure cosmic rays from 100 TeV to several EeV.

One of the four original detectors at DESY's PETRA collider in Hamburg. In 1979 its collaboration identified the first three-jet events, the first direct evidence of the gluon, the carrier of the strong force. It took data until PETRA closed in 1986.

A cosmic-ray observatory in the Utah desert with over 500 ground detectors spread across 700 square kilometres and telescopes at three stations, watching for the rarest, most energetic particles from space; recently made four times bigger by the TAx4 extension.

aliases: Transition Edge Sensors with Sub-eV Resolution And Cryogenic Targets

intervals.label: proposed experiment with a dedicated cryostat at LSM
planned installation of the two TESSERACT setups at LSM
planned full integration of the TESSERACT setup at LSM

key_specs.label: Lowest dark matter mass aimed at (design)

experiment:tesseract.name: TESSERACT

summary.plain: TESSERACT is a planned dark matter experiment that uses ultra-sensitive superconducting sensors to look for particles far lighter than a proton. Its detectors are proposed for the deep Modane underground laboratory in the French Alps. A surface prototype at Berkeley has already set new limits.

intervals.label: conceptual design and construction of the Kuo-Sheng laboratory
operation at Kuo-Sheng (neutrino physics from July 2001; germanium dark-matter programme added 2004)

summary.plain: TEXONO is a Taiwan-led experiment at a nuclear power plant that uses germanium detectors sensitive to energies of a few hundred electron-volts. Besides studying reactor neutrinos, it set limits on very light dark matter and tested the claim by the CoGeNT experiment.

intervals.label: air-shower array with underground muon detectors

summary.plain: A field of scintillator detectors and an underground water pool of muon detectors on the Tibetan plateau, 4300 metres up. It detected the first photons above 100 TeV from the Crab Nebula and the first diffuse sub-PeV gamma rays from the Galactic disk.

intervals.label: detector system installed at Kamioka; LiF bolometer improved
underground dark matter runs with LiF (2001-2002) and NaF (2002-2003) bolometer arrays

summary.plain: A University of Tokyo experiment in the Kamioka mine, Japan, that used small fluoride crystals (lithium fluoride, then sodium fluoride) cooled to near absolute zero to look for dark matter particles that interact through nuclear spin, and set limits on their couplings.

One of the three large general-purpose detectors at KEK's TRISTAN collider in Japan, built by a domestic Japanese team around a time-projection chamber in a superconducting solenoid. It measured hadron production and electroweak effects at the world's highest e+e- energies from 1987 to 1995.

aliases: TOTal Elastic and diffractive cross section Measurement
Total Cross Section, Elastic Scattering and Diffraction Dissociation at the LHC
experiment:totem.energy_regime: LHC proton-proton collisions, 7-13.6 TeV centre-of-mass energy
experiment:totem.name: TOTEM

summary.plain: TOTEM sits around CMS's collision point and measures protons that barely miss each other, letting physicists work out the total chance that two protons collide at all -- one of the most basic numbers in particle physics.

aliases: TPC Rare Event eXperiment for Dark Matter

commissioning and first engineering runs in Hall A

experiment:trex-dm.name: TREX-DM

summary.plain: TREX-DM looks for very light dark matter particles with a high-pressure gas chamber read out by Micromegas detectors, installed at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees. Light gases (neon or argon) make the tiny recoils detectable. Its published results so far describe detector performance and background levels.

A proposed neutrino telescope in the South China Sea: over a thousand strings of light sensors hanging 3 kilometres deep, filling several cubic kilometres of seawater, to spot cosmic neutrinos from near the equator. A pathfinder has measured the clarity of the water at the chosen site.

intervals.label: proposal of the keV sterile-neutrino search at the Troitsk nu-mass facility
keV sterile-neutrino search: first measurements and continued operation

summary.plain: A tritium beta-decay experiment near Moscow that weighed the electron antineutrino by measuring the electron spectrum with an electrostatic filter. Its final analysis limits the mass to about 2.2 electron-volts; the same setup now hunts for keV sterile neutrinos.

intervals.label: development of the advanced UCN source
commissioning of the source, first UCN production

summary.plain: A Canadian-led collaboration building a very intense source of ultracold neutrons at TRIUMF in Vancouver, to search for the neutron’s electric dipole moment with a target sensitivity of 10^-27 electron-charge centimetres. The source made its first ultracold neutrons in 2024-2025.
Tunka-133 is a field of 175 light detectors in a Siberian valley that watch, on clear moonless nights, for the blue flash of air showers made by cosmic rays near the knee of the energy spectrum.

intervals.label: data taking at TRIUMF (data from 2004 onwards)

summary.plain: An experiment at TRIUMF in Vancouver that measured how positrons are emitted when polarized muons decay, giving three parameters that test the Standard Model’s description of a purely leptonic process and limit models with a right-handed weak force.

experiment:ua1.energy_regime: Proton-antiproton collisions at 540-630 GeV centre-of-mass energy
experiment:ua1.name: UA1

summary.plain: A giant particle detector built around CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron in the early 1980s, when the machine was turned into a proton-antiproton collider. UA1 co-discovered the W and Z bosons, the carriers of the weak nuclear force.

experiment:ua2.energy_regime: Proton-antiproton collisions at 540-630 GeV centre-of-mass energy
experiment:ua2.name: UA2

summary.plain: A particle detector built around CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron in the early 1980s, alongside UA1, when the machine was turned into a proton-antiproton collider. UA2 co-discovered the W and Z bosons using precise calorimeters rather than a magnetic spectrometer.

An experiment at CERN's proton-antiproton collider (SppS) that measured elastic scattering of protons and antiprotons at very small angles, in the Coulomb-interference region. It reported the elastic and total cross sections at 540 GeV and took data until June 1985.

The first-generation streamer-chamber experiment at CERN's proton-antiproton collider (SppS), approved in February 1979 and led by John Rushbrooke. It surveyed how many particles proton-antiproton collisions produce at 200, 540 and 900 GeV, finding that the multiplicity distributions violate scaling.

intervals.label: data taking with the magneto-gravitational trap (2017 to 2022)
upgrade for the next level of precision

summary.plain: An experiment at Los Alamos that holds ultracold neutrons in a bowl made of magnets and gravity, so they cannot touch any walls, and counts how many survive. Its measured neutron lifetime is about 877.8 seconds, with an uncertainty of about 0.3 seconds. An upgrade is underway.

One of the three large general-purpose detectors at KEK's TRISTAN collider in Japan, built by a domestic Japanese team. It used a superconducting solenoid, a cylindrical drift chamber and a liquid-argon calorimeter at the ends. With AMY and TOPAZ it tested QCD and searched for the top quark from 1987 to 1995.

aliases: Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System
experiment:veritas.name: VERITAS

summary.plain: Four 12-metre telescopes on a mountain in Arizona that catch the faint flashes of light made when gamma rays hit the atmosphere, letting astronomers study exploding stars, black holes and other extreme places in the universe.

intervals.label: data taking with the Omega spectrometer (Pb beam)

summary.plain: WA97 was a CERN experiment in the SPS West Area that studied strange and multi-strange particles in lead-lead collisions using a new silicon pixel telescope placed near the target. It was the first high-energy physics experiment to use that technique, and found enhanced strangeness production.

WA98 was a CERN experiment in the SPS West Area that studied lead-lead collisions with a photon spectrometer, a hadron spectrometer and many global detectors. It made the first observation of direct photons in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions and saw suppression of high-momentum neutral pions.

intervals.label: 100-litre detector approved and funded by INFN
construction and assembly of the 100-litre detector
commissioning and technical runs of the 100-litre detector
completed (no physics run; programme ended without further reports)

key_specs.label: Sensitive liquid argon volume (100-litre detector, design)
Prototype test chamber volume (first physics results)

summary.plain: WArP (WIMP Argon Programme) was a Gran Sasso programme that pioneered two-phase liquid argon detectors for WIMP dark matter. Its 2.3-litre prototype gave the first physics results; a 100-litre detector was assembled in 2008 and tested until about 2011 but never completed a physics run.

aliases: Whipple 10 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope

key_specs.label: Lower end of operating energy range

experiment:whipple-10m.name: Whipple 10 m Gamma-Ray Telescope

summary.plain: The 10 metre mirror on Mount Hopkins, Arizona, that in 1989 detected the first source of TeV gamma rays, the Crab Nebula, and founded imaging Cherenkov astronomy. It ran from 1968 until 2013 and led to VERITAS.

XENON10 was a small prototype dark matter detector holding about 15 kg of liquid xenon, run in 2006 and 2007 in the Gran Sasso underground laboratory in Italy. It saw no dark matter, set new limits, and proved the technique that the larger XENON100, XENON1T and XENONnT detectors built on.

XENON100 was a detector holding about 160 kg of liquid xenon in a tunnel at the Gran Sasso underground laboratory in Italy. It looked for flashes of light from dark matter particles hitting xenon atoms, found none, and for a time set the tightest limits then known.

XENON1T was a tank of liquid xenon deep under a mountain in Italy that searched for dark matter particles bumping into xenon atoms. It ran from 2015 to 2018 and was for a time the most sensitive dark matter detector in the world. It is the direct predecessor of the larger XENONnT experiment now running in the same underground hall.

intervals.label: detector upgrade (new TPC electrodes, drift field 23 → 100 V/cm)

summary.plain: XENONnT is a tank of nearly six tonnes of liquid xenon deep under a mountain in Italy, watching for dark matter and other rare signals. The upgraded successor of XENON1T, it began operating in 2020, took science data from 2021, was upgraded in 2025 and, per the collaboration's 2026 talks, is being recommissioned. It has set new dark matter limits.

intervals.label: refurbishment (copper covers on PMT window seals)

summary.plain: XMASS was a detector holding 832 kg of liquid xenon in the Kamioka mine in Japan, built to look for dark matter by watching for its faint flashes of light. It ran from 2013 to 2019, saw no dark matter, and set limits on several kinds of dark matter.

One of the longest-running giant cosmic-ray detectors, in a Siberian river valley. Scintillators, underground muon counters and light detectors have recorded air showers since the 1970s, including three of the highest-energy cosmic rays ever seen.

ZEPLIN-I was the first of the ZEPLIN liquid xenon dark matter detectors, with about 3 kg of liquid xenon, run in the Boulby mine in north-east England in the early 2000s. It found no dark matter and set limits; the strength of its method was later disputed.

ZEPLIN-II was a 31 kg two-phase liquid xenon dark matter detector in the Boulby mine in north-east England, operating from 2005. It measured both light and electric charge to tell dark matter from background, and set limits.

intervals.label: construction, commissioning and installation at Boulby
upgrade: low-background PMTs, anti-coincidence veto, calibration system

summary.plain: ZEPLIN-III was a 12 kg two-phase liquid xenon dark matter detector in the Boulby mine, the third and last of the ZEPLIN detectors, run from 2006 to 2011. It saw no dark matter and closed the ZEPLIN programme.

A particle detector at the German laboratory DESY, in Hamburg, that watched electrons and protons collide head-on to map out what a proton is made of, and to search for new particles and forces. It ran from 1992 until HERA, the collider it depended on, shut down on 30 June 2007.

facility:akeno-observatory.name: Akeno Observatory
facility:akeno-observatory.operator: Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, University of Tokyo
facility:akeno-observatory.operator_text: Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, University of Tokyo

summary.plain: A University of Tokyo cosmic-ray station in the Yamanashi mountains, home of the Akeno air-shower arrays and of AGASA, once the world's largest air-shower array.

facility:amundsen-scott-south-pole-stati.name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
facility:amundsen-scott-south-pole-stati.operator_text: U.S. National Science Foundation / U.S. Antarctic Program

summary.plain: The United States research station at the South Pole. It is the southernmost place people live all year, and it supports the giant IceCube neutrino telescope buried in the ice below it.

facility:angra-npp.name: Almirante Alvaro Alberto Nuclear Power Plant (Angra)

summary.plain: The Brazilian nuclear power complex at Angra dos Reis, whose Angra 2 reactor is the source for the CONNIE experiment, which tries to catch the faintest nuclear recoils from reactor antineutrinos with silicon sensors 30 metres from the core.
An observatory in the Sacramento Mountains of southern New Mexico. Its Sloan Foundation 2.5-metre telescope has carried the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, including the BOSS and eBOSS dark-energy surveys.

facility:argonne-national-laboratory.name: Argonne National Laboratory
facility:argonne-national-laboratory.operator_text: The University of Chicago, through its subordinate UChicago Argonne LLC, for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: A United States Department of Energy multidisciplinary science laboratory near Chicago, one of the country's oldest national laboratories.

facility:baikal-deep-underwater-neutrino.name: Baikal Deep Underwater Neutrino Telescope
facility:baikal-deep-underwater-neutrino.operator_text: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INR RAS)

summary.plain: A Russian-led neutrino telescope growing year by year on the bottom of Lake Baikal, the world's deepest freshwater lake. Strings of light sensors hang beneath the ice, watching for flashes made by neutrinos from space.

intervals.label: hosting the Baksan Underground Scintillation Telescope

facility:baksan-neutrino-observatory.name: Baksan Neutrino Observatory
facility:baksan-neutrino-observatory.operator: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INR RAS)
facility:baksan-neutrino-observatory.operator_text: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INR RAS)

summary.plain: An underground laboratory dug into a mountain in the Russian Caucasus, with rock overhead equal in shielding to about 4700 metres of water at its deepest neutrino hall, built to study neutrinos from the Sun and elsewhere.

facility:bern-underground-laboratory.name: University of Bern underground laboratory
facility:bern-underground-laboratory.operator_text: University of Bern (Laboratory for High Energy Physics)

summary.plain: A shallow underground laboratory of the University of Bern's Laboratory for High Energy Physics, with about 70 metres of water equivalent of cover; it hosted the ORPHEUS dark matter detector.

facility:binp-novosibirsk.name: Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics
facility:binp-novosibirsk.operator_text: Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences (BINP SB RAS)

summary.plain: Russia's largest academic physics institute, in Akademgorodok near Novosibirsk, Siberia. It has operated electron-positron colliders for over half a century; today VEPP-2000 and VEPP-4M and their detectors CMD-3, SND and KEDR measure how particles are made at low and medium energies.

facility:boulby-underground-laboratory.name: Boulby Underground Laboratory
facility:boulby-underground-laboratory.operator_text: STFC (Science and Technology Facilities Council), in close partnership with ICL-UK

summary.plain: A deep underground science laboratory in a working mine on the English coast, more than a kilometre below ground. It hosts dark-matter searches and other experiments that need to be shielded from cosmic rays.
A now-closed German nuclear power plant on the Elbe river that hosted the CONUS reactor-neutrino experiment from 2018 until the setup moved to Switzerland in 2023.

facility:brookhaven-national-laboratory.name: Brookhaven National Laboratory
facility:brookhaven-national-laboratory.operator_text: Brookhaven Science Associates (a partnership of Stony Brook University and Battelle, with six core universities) for the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Science

summary.plain: A United States national laboratory on Long Island, New York, run for the Department of Energy. It built and operated the world's first collider able to smash together beams of gold atomic nuclei and of protons with aligned spins, and it hosts other major physics, biology and materials-science facilities.

A French nuclear power station on the Rhone near Lyon whose reactors served as the antineutrino source for the Bugey experiments of the 1990s, which measured the antineutrino rate and spectrum 15 to 95 metres from a reactor core.

intervals.label: LSC operating (research programme grew from the 1985 project)

facility:canfranc-underground-laboratory.name: Laboratorio Subterráneo de Canfranc
facility:canfranc-underground-laboratory.operator_text: A Consortium of the Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation, the Aragon Regional Government and the University of Zaragoza

summary.plain: An underground laboratory beneath a mountain in the Spanish Pyrenees, reached through a disused railway tunnel near Canfranc. Its 800 metres of rock shield sensitive experiments searching for dark matter and rare nuclear processes.

aliases: Organisation européenne pour la recherche nucléaire
facility:cern.name: CERN
facility:cern.operator_text: CERN, European Organization for Nuclear Research

summary.plain: CERN is Europe's particle physics laboratory, on the Swiss-French border near Geneva. Founded in 1954 by twelve countries, it builds and runs the accelerators that send beams of protons and ions into experiments such as ATLAS and CMS, and it is the home of the Large Hadron Collider.
A group of mountaintop telescopes in the Chilean Andes, long the main US platform for studying the southern sky. Its 4-metre Blanco telescope carries the Dark Energy Camera.

intervals.label: hosting the CHOOZ neutrino experiment (reactor-neutrino site)

summary.plain: The site near the Chooz nuclear power station in northern France where the Double Chooz experiment placed two detectors to catch antineutrinos from the reactors.

facility:cjpl.name: China Jinping Underground Laboratory
facility:cjpl.operator_text: Tsinghua University, together with Yalong River Hydropower Development Company

summary.plain: The world's deepest underground physics laboratory, built beside a hydropower tunnel under the Jinping mountains in southwest China. Over two kilometres of rock overhead make it an extremely quiet place to search for dark matter.

aliases: Cornell Laboratory for Accelerator-based Sciences and Education
facility:cornell-wilson-lab.name: Wilson Synchrotron Laboratory, Cornell University
facility:cornell-wilson-lab.operator_text: Cornell University (CLASSE, the Cornell Laboratory for Accelerator-based Sciences and Education)

summary.plain: Cornell University's accelerator laboratory in Ithaca, New York. Its electron-positron storage ring, CESR, ran from 1979, hosted the CLEO and CUSB experiments on beauty and charm particles, and now feeds the CHESS X-ray source.
The southern-hemisphere site of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory, in the Atacama Desert of Chile near ESO's Paranal Observatory.

intervals.label: operating period (six-, eight- and seven-AD configurations)

facility:daya-bay-reactor-neutrino-lab.name: Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Laboratory
facility:daya-bay-reactor-neutrino-lab.operator: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences
facility:daya-bay-reactor-neutrino-lab.operator_text: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: A set of underground experimental halls near the Daya Bay and Ling Ao nuclear power plants in Guangdong, China, built to catch antineutrinos streaming out of the reactors.

facility:desy.name: Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron
facility:desy.operator_text: A publicly funded German national research centre, member of the Helmholtz Association, financed 90% by the German Federal Ministry of Research and 10% by the City of Hamburg and the Federal State of Brandenburg

summary.plain: Germany's national laboratory for particle and accelerator physics, in Hamburg. Its HERA ring was the world's only electron-proton collider, and DESY continues to build and run major accelerator-based research facilities.

intervals.label: HiRes prototype and MIA muon array (hybrid)

facility:dugway-hires-site.name: Dugway Proving Ground (Fly's Eye and HiRes site)

summary.plain: Army test range in the Utah desert where two generations of cosmic-ray fluorescence detectors, Fly's Eye and HiRes, watched the night sky for the faint light of giant air showers from 1981 to 2006.

The world's most powerful planned neutron source, being built in Lund, Sweden, around a 5-megawatt proton linear accelerator. Its protons will make neutrons for materials research and could also drive a neutrino beam.

facility:fermilab.name: Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory
facility:fermilab.operator_text: Fermi Forward Discovery Group, LLC (FermiForward) for the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science (since 1 January 2025; Fermi Research Alliance, LLC before)

summary.plain: The United States national laboratory for particle physics, near Chicago. It builds and runs the chain of machines that produce the most intense beams of neutrinos in the world, and it hosts the DUNE experiment.

intervals.label: established as the Smithsonian Mount Hopkins Observatory

summary.plain: A mountain observatory in southern Arizona, home to the VERITAS gamma-ray telescopes among other instruments.

aliases: Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research
facility:gsi-fair.name: GSI Helmholtzzentrum für Schwerionenforschung / FAIR
facility:gsi-fair.operator_text: GSI Helmholtzzentrum für Schwerionenforschung GmbH, owned by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%), the State of Hesse (8%), Rhineland-Palatinate (1%) and Thuringia (1%); the FAIR facility is built and operated by FAIR GmbH with international partners

summary.plain: Germany's national laboratory for heavy-ion research in Darmstadt. Its UNILAC and SIS18 accelerators serve nuclear and hadron-physics experiments such as HADES, and it is building the international FAIR facility with a new 1.1 km ring, SIS100.

A very large U.S. Department of Energy site in Washington state, built in 1943 to make plutonium for nuclear weapons and now being cleaned up. In 1953 Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines made their first attempt to detect the neutrino at one of its reactors.

A very high mountain site at Hanle in Ladakh, northern India, home to two Indian gamma-ray telescopes: the HAGAR array and the 21 m MACE telescope. At about 4270 metres it hosts the highest Cherenkov telescopes in the world.
A remote farm in the Namibian highlands, about two hours from Windhoek, that hosts the H.E.S.S. gamma-ray telescopes.

facility:ihep-beijing.name: Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: China's national laboratory for particle physics, in Beijing and part of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. It built and runs the Beijing Electron-Positron Collider, whose BES detectors study the tau lepton and charm physics.

facility:ill-grenoble.name: Institut Laue-Langevin
facility:ill-grenoble.operator: Institut Laue-Langevin (an international research centre funded and managed by France, Germany and the United Kingdom)
facility:ill-grenoble.operator_text: Institut Laue-Langevin (an international research centre funded and managed by France, Germany and the United Kingdom)

summary.plain: A major research reactor in Grenoble, France, mainly used to make beams of neutrons for science, and also home to the Ricochet reactor-neutrino experiment.

facility:imb-fairport-mine.name: Fairport Harbor Morton Salt Mine (IMB site)
facility:imb-fairport-mine.operator_text: Morton Salt (host salt mine; named the "Morton-Thiokol salt mine" in the 1987 IMB paper)

summary.plain: A salt mine in Ohio that, from 1982 to 1991, housed the IMB detector, an 8,000-ton tank of ultrapure water built to look for proton decay. It recorded neutrinos from supernova 1987A and was named an APS historic site in 2024.

The Italian National Institute for Nuclear Physics' accelerator laboratory near Rome. It built the first matter-antimatter collider, AdA, then ADONE, and now runs DAΦNE, an electron-positron collider that produces phi mesons for the KLOE experiments.

facility:inr-troitsk.name: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Troitsk
facility:inr-troitsk.operator_text: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INR RAS)

summary.plain: The Moscow-region site of the Institute for Nuclear Research, where the Troitsk nu-mass experiment weighed the neutrino from tritium decay.

A pulsed particle accelerator facility in Oxfordshire, England, that fires protons at a heavy-metal target to make neutrons and muons for materials research. In the 1990s its proton beam stop also served as a source of neutrinos for the KARMEN experiment.

facility:j-parc.name: J-PARC (Japan Proton Accelerator Research Complex)
facility:j-parc.operator: Operated jointly by the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA) and the High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK)
facility:j-parc.operator_text: Operated jointly by the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA) and the High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK)

summary.plain: A large proton accelerator laboratory on the Pacific coast of Japan, run jointly by two national research organisations. Its most powerful machine drives a beam of neutrinos across the country to detectors in the mountains of western Japan.

intervals.label: in use by InDEx (earliest dated use)

summary.plain: A small underground laboratory, 555 metres down at Jaduguda in Jharkhand, India, where the InDEx experiment looks for dark matter with droplet detectors.

facility:jefferson-lab.name: Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility
facility:jefferson-lab.operator_text: SURATech, LLC (a partnership of the Southeastern Universities Research Association and Virginia Tech, with four subcontractors) for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: The U.S. national laboratory for nuclear physics in Newport News, Virginia. Its CEBAF accelerator fires a continuous beam of electrons at atomic nuclei to study the quarks and gluons that make up protons and neutrons.

facility:jinr-dubna.name: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research (JINR), Dubna
facility:jinr-dubna.operator_text: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, an international intergovernmental scientific research organisation

summary.plain: An international intergovernmental research organisation in Dubna, Russia, founded in 1956. Its Veksler and Baldin Laboratory of High Energy Physics runs the superconducting Nuclotron and is commissioning the NICA collider for heavy-ion and spin physics.

facility:johannes-gutenberg-university-m.name: Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (Institute of Physics)

summary.plain: The Institute of Physics of Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany. In the 1990s and early 2000s it hosted a tritium beta-decay experiment that limited the electron-antineutrino mass to 2.3 electron-volts.

intervals.label: detector installation (support structure, acrylic vessel, PMTs)
final construction stage: water and liquid-scintillator filling

facility:juno-jiangmen.name: Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory
facility:juno-jiangmen.operator: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences
facility:juno-jiangmen.operator_text: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: A giant underground hall in southern China, dug into a hill near Jiangmen, that holds the JUNO neutrino detector deep beneath the rock so cosmic rays cannot swamp its measurements.
A Russian nuclear power plant between Moscow and Saint Petersburg with four large pressurised-water reactors; under one of them the DANSS experiment has been catching antineutrinos since 2016.

facility:kamioka-observatory.name: Kamioka Observatory (ICRR, University of Tokyo)
facility:kamioka-observatory.operator: Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, University of Tokyo
facility:kamioka-observatory.operator_text: Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, University of Tokyo

summary.plain: An underground laboratory inside a mine in the Japanese Alps, a kilometre beneath a mountain. The rock above screens out most cosmic rays, so very rare signals from neutrinos can be seen.

aliases: National Laboratory for High Energy Physics

intervals.label: National Laboratory for High Energy Physics

facility:kek.name: KEK (High Energy Accelerator Research Organization)
facility:kek.operator: Inter-University Research Institute Corporation High Energy Accelerator Research Organization
facility:kek.operator_text: Inter-University Research Institute Corporation High Energy Accelerator Research Organization

summary.plain: Japan's national accelerator laboratory at Tsukuba, founded in 1971. Its 12 GeV proton accelerator made the first long-distance beam of neutrinos ever aimed at a detector hundreds of kilometres away.

facility:kirchhoff-institute-for-physics.name: Kirchhoff Institute for Physics, Heidelberg University

summary.plain: A physics institute of Heidelberg University, Germany, where the ECHo collaboration builds its ultra-cold magnetic calorimeters to measure the electron neutrino mass from holmium-163 decay.

intervals.label: Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe (predecessor institution on Campus North)
KIT (merger of Universität Karlsruhe and Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe)

facility:kit-karlsruhe.name: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Campus North

summary.plain: A large German research campus north of Karlsruhe that hosts the Tritium Laboratory Karlsruhe, home to the KATRIN neutrino-mass experiment.
A mountaintop observatory in southern Arizona with one of the largest collections of optical telescopes in the world. Its 4-metre Mayall telescope now serves the DESI survey of dark energy.

A research infrastructure of two neutrino detectors built into the floor of the Mediterranean Sea: ARCA off the coast of Sicily, Italy, and ORCA off Toulon, France. Strings of light sensors watch for faint flashes made by neutrinos from space and from the Earth's atmosphere.

An underground laboratory in the deep Kolar Gold Fields mines of southern India. From 1960 until the mines closed in 1993 it hosted experiments that saw the first atmospheric neutrinos and searched for proton decay.

intervals.label: design and construction of the laboratory
operating (first physics data July 2001; operational in 2026)

facility:kuo-sheng-reactor-neutrino-labo.name: Kuo-Sheng Reactor Neutrino Laboratory
facility:kuo-sheng-reactor-neutrino-labo.operator_text: Taiwan Power Company (operator of the Kuo-Sheng Nuclear Power Station that hosts the laboratory)

summary.plain: A small physics laboratory built next to a reactor core inside the Kuo-Sheng nuclear power plant on the northern coast of Taiwan. Under about thirty metres of water-equivalent shielding from the building, it hosts the TEXONO germanium detectors used for reactor-neutrino and light dark matter searches.

facility:lawrence-berkeley-national-labo.name: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
facility:lawrence-berkeley-national-labo.operator_text: University of California, for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: The U.S. Department of Energy laboratory above Berkeley, California, that grew out of Ernest Lawrence's cyclotron laboratory of the 1930s. Its Bevatron accelerator, completed in 1954, produced the first antiprotons in 1955.
A Swiss nuclear power plant on the Rhine that has hosted the CONUS+ reactor-neutrino experiment since late 2023.

aliases: Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory site
facility:lhaaso-daocheng.name: LHAASO (Daocheng)
facility:lhaaso-daocheng.operator: Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
facility:lhaaso-daocheng.operator_text: Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: A high-altitude observatory on Haizi Mountain in Sichuan, China, that catches cosmic rays and the highest-energy gamma rays yet seen, using several kinds of ground detectors at once.

The largest underground research laboratory in the world, built beside a motorway tunnel under the Gran Sasso mountain in central Italy. About 1400 metres of rock overhead cut the shower of cosmic particles by a factor of a million, which lets very quiet experiments run there.

facility:los-alamos-national-laboratory.name: Los Alamos National Laboratory
facility:los-alamos-national-laboratory.operator_text: Triad National Security, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA)

summary.plain: A United States national laboratory in the mountains of New Mexico, founded during the Manhattan Project. Its LANSCE accelerator produces intense beams of protons and neutrons used for nuclear and particle physics, including past neutrino experiments.

aliases: Laboratoire Souterrain à Bas Bruit de Rustrel-Pays d'Apt

intervals.label: operating as a civilian underground laboratory (earliest dated use found)

facility:lsbb-rustrel.name: Laboratoire Souterrain à Bas Bruit
facility:lsbb-rustrel.operator_text: CNRS and Avignon Université (Unité d'Appui et de Recherche UAR 3538)

summary.plain: A low-noise underground laboratory at Rustrel in southern France, made from a former underground missile control centre. About 500 m of rock shields it from cosmic rays, and it hosted the SIMPLE dark matter search.

facility:mainz-mami.name: Institute of Nuclear Physics, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (MAMI and MESA)
facility:mainz-mami.operator_text: Institute of Nuclear Physics, Faculty 08 Physics, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz

summary.plain: The nuclear-physics institute of Mainz University in Germany operates MAMI, an electron microtron delivering precise electron beams up to 1.5 GeV for hadron-structure experiments (A1, A2), and is building the new MESA accelerator for precision electroweak and dark-sector experiments.
The NASA balloon-launch site near McMurdo Station, Antarctica, where the ANITA neutrino instrument was launched on each of its long, high-altitude balloon flights.

MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) is a university in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its physics department built ABRACADABRA, a small experiment that searched for the axion, a hypothetical dark-matter particle.

facility:modane-underground-laboratory.name: Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane
facility:modane-underground-laboratory.operator_text: CNRS/IN2P3 and Universite Grenoble-Alpes; a national IN2P3 platform attached to the Laboratoire de Physique Subatomique et Cosmologie (LPSC) in Grenoble since 2019

summary.plain: An underground physics laboratory built into the middle of a road tunnel through the French Alps, under 1700 metres of rock. It is the deepest underground laboratory in Europe and hosts sensitive searches for dark matter and rare nuclear decays.

An underground laboratory in a cave beside the Mont Blanc road tunnel between France and Italy, under about five thousand metres of water-equivalent rock. Its first documented experiment was NUSEX, a 150-ton detector that looked for proton decay from 1982.

Columbia University's particle-physics laboratory at Irvington, New York. Its cyclotron gave physicists beams of pions and muons, and in January 1957 it was where Garwin, Lederman and Weinrich showed that parity is violated in pion and muon decay.

intervals.label: reactor shut down after the 3 February 2021 fuel-element incident

facility:nist-center-for-neutron-researc.name: NIST Center for Neutron Research
facility:nist-center-for-neutron-researc.operator_text: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)

summary.plain: The neutron research centre of the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology in Gaithersburg, Maryland. Its research reactor first went critical in 1967 and supplies neutron beams, including those used to measure how long a free neutron lives. It was shut down in 2021 and resumed operating in 2026.

facility:oak-ridge-national-laboratory.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory
facility:oak-ridge-national-laboratory.operator_text: UT-Battelle, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: The United States' largest multiprogram science laboratory, in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. It runs the Spallation Neutron Source, whose intense proton beam also produces one of the world's best sources of neutrinos for the COHERENT experiment.

aliases: Cosmic Ray Laboratory, Raj Bhavan, Ooty
facility:ooty-cosmic-ray-laboratory.name: Cosmic Ray Laboratory, Ooty

summary.plain: An Indian cosmic-ray laboratory in the Nilgiri hills at Ooty, home of the GRAPES-3 air-shower array and muon telescope.

facility:oto-cosmo-observatory.name: Oto Cosmo Observatory
facility:oto-cosmo-observatory.operator_text: Research Center for Nuclear Physics (RCNP), Osaka University

summary.plain: A small underground laboratory of Osaka University in the middle of a road tunnel in Nara prefecture, Japan, about 100 km south of Osaka. Dark matter and double-beta-decay detectors of the ELEGANT series ran there from 1997.

intervals.label: hosting the Palo Verde neutrino experiment

summary.plain: The largest nuclear power station in the United States, in the Arizona desert, with three reactors; a shallow underground laboratory about 800 metres from them housed the Palo Verde neutrino experiment in 1998-2000.

intervals.label: first CMB telescope operating in the park area (ACT)
territorial concession presented; park opened by CONICYT

facility:parque-astronomico-atacama.name: Parque Astronómico Atacama
facility:parque-astronomico-atacama.operator: CONICYT (Comisión Nacional de Investigación Científica y Tecnológica), holder of the park's territorial concession
facility:parque-astronomico-atacama.operator_text: CONICYT (Comisión Nacional de Investigación Científica y Tecnológica), holder of the park's territorial concession

summary.plain: A high-altitude desert park in northern Chile reserved for astronomy. Several microwave telescopes that map the afterglow of the Big Bang stand on and near Cerro Toco inside it, including the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, the Simons Observatory, POLARBEAR/Simons Array and CLASS. The planned SWGO gamma-ray observatory is to be built on a nearby plateau in the same park.

A giant outdoor laboratory in the Argentine pampas that catches ultra-high-energy cosmic rays: tanks of water spread over an area the size of Rhode Island, watched by telescopes that see the faint light of particle showers in the night sky.

facility:psi.name: Paul Scherrer Institute
facility:psi.operator_text: Part of the ETH Domain, the group of Swiss federal research institutions that also includes ETH Zurich, EPFL, WSL, Empa and Eawag

summary.plain: Switzerland's largest research institute for natural and engineering sciences, home to one of the world's most powerful proton accelerators. It produces intense beams of muons used in precision searches for new physics.

aliases: Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos
facility:roque-de-los-muchachos-observat.name: Roque de los Muchachos Observatory
facility:roque-de-los-muchachos-observat.operator: Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (host observatory); CTAO-North hosted here per CTAO's own site listing
facility:roque-de-los-muchachos-observat.operator_text: Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (host observatory); CTAO-North hosted here per CTAO's own site listing

summary.plain: A mountaintop observatory on the Spanish Canary Island of La Palma that hosts several gamma-ray telescopes, including MAGIC and the northern half of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory.

facility:savannah-river-site.name: Savannah River Site
facility:savannah-river-site.operator_text: U.S. Department of Energy; management and operations contract awarded to Savannah River Nuclear Solutions in 2008

summary.plain: A very large U.S. Department of Energy site in South Carolina, built in the early 1950s to make nuclear-weapons materials. Its P Reactor gave Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines the intense stream of antineutrinos with which they detected the neutrino in 1956.

The Belgian Nuclear Research Centre at Mol, whose BR2 research reactor burns highly enriched uranium in a compact core; the SoLid experiment placed an antineutrino detector next to it from 2018 to 2020.

A gamma-ray observatory on the slopes of the Sierra Negra volcano in Mexico, high enough (4100 metres) that ground-based tanks of water can catch particle showers from gamma rays hitting the atmosphere.

facility:slac.name: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
facility:slac.operator_text: Stanford University for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: The United States' national laboratory for accelerator-based science, run by Stanford University in Menlo Park, California. It built a two-mile-long linear accelerator and later ran two colliders, SLC and PEP-II. Work at the laboratory has won Nobel Prizes in Physics.

facility:sm-3-reactor-dimitrovgrad.name: SM-3 research reactor, Dimitrovgrad (RIAR)
facility:sm-3-reactor-dimitrovgrad.operator: State Science Center Research Institute of Atomic Reactors (RIAR), JSC
facility:sm-3-reactor-dimitrovgrad.operator_text: State Science Center Research Institute of Atomic Reactors (RIAR), JSC

summary.plain: A compact, highly enriched uranium research reactor in the Russian city of Dimitrovgrad, run by the Research Institute of Atomic Reactors, where the Neutrino-4 experiment measured antineutrinos from 6 to 12 metres away.

facility:snolab.name: SNOLAB
facility:snolab.operator_text: SNOLAB Institute (governed by a Board of Directors whose member institutions are Carleton University, Laurentian University, Queen's University, University of Alberta and the Université de Montréal)

summary.plain: A deep underground physics laboratory two kilometres below the surface in an active nickel mine near Sudbury, Canada. The thick rock overhead blocks nearly all cosmic rays, letting scientists search for dark matter and study neutrinos in an extremely quiet environment.

aliases: Soudan Underground Mine State Park laboratory

intervals.label: Soudan 2 data taking in the underground laboratory
MINOS far detector hall in operation

facility:soudan-underground-laboratory.name: Soudan Underground Laboratory

summary.plain: A laboratory dug into a disused iron mine in northern Minnesota, about 700 metres below ground. The rock above it screens out most of the particles raining down from the sky, which let it host the far detector of the MINOS neutrino experiment and a dark matter search.

intervals.label: hosting the CDMS I and first-tower CDMS II detectors
scientific use of the tunnel by CDMS ended

summary.plain: A shallow tunnel, about ten metres below the Stanford University campus in California, where the first stages of the Cryogenic Dark Matter Search ran in the late 1990s and early 2000s before moving to the deeper Soudan mine.

facility:stawell-underground-physics-lab.name: Stawell Underground Physics Laboratory
facility:stawell-underground-physics-lab.operator_text: SUPL Ltd, a not-for-profit company limited by guarantee (founding members: the Australian National University, the University of Melbourne, Adelaide University, Swinburne University of Technology and ANSTO)

summary.plain: Australia's first deep underground physics laboratory, inside the Stawell Gold Mine in Victoria, about a kilometre below the surface. The rock overhead blocks cosmic rays, so it can host very sensitive experiments such as SABRE South, a dark matter search in the Southern Hemisphere.

intervals.label: STCF project (proposed 2011; Hefei named as the site in the project documents)

facility:stcf-hefei.name: Super Tau-Charm Facility site, Hefei (proposed)
facility:stcf-hefei.operator_text: University of Science and Technology of China (leads the project)

summary.plain: The proposed home of China's Super Tau-Charm Facility, an electron-positron collider planned for the Future Big Science City of Hefei and led by the University of Science and Technology of China. It has not been approved or built.

facility:summit-station-greenland.name: Summit Station, Greenland
facility:summit-station-greenland.operator_text: Battelle Arctic Research Operations (ARO), funded by the NSF Section for Arctic Sciences (ARC)

summary.plain: A high, remote research station at the very top of the Greenland ice sheet, more than three kilometres above sea level, where the RNO-G neutrino detector is being built into the ice.

intervals.label: South Dakota Science and Technology Authority formed

facility:surf.name: Sanford Underground Research Facility
facility:surf.operator_text: South Dakota Science and Technology Authority

depth.display: 1478 m (4850-foot level); sources round this to about 1500 m

summary.plain: A laboratory built in a former gold mine in Lead, South Dakota. Nearly a mile of rock above it blocks cosmic rays, so experiments there can look for very rare events, including the giant DUNE neutrino detectors.

intervals.label: candidate host of JUNO-TAO (conceptual design report)

summary.plain: A nuclear power plant on the coast of Guangdong, China, with two of the world's most powerful reactors; a small detector, TAO, is being installed in a basement about 44 metres from one core to measure its antineutrinos precisely for the nearby JUNO experiment.

A cosmic-ray observatory in the Utah desert, near Delta: 507 detector stations spread across about 700 square kilometres, watched by three telescope stations, to catch the rarest and most energetic particles from space.

intervals.label: selected site for the TRIDENT telescope

facility:trident-south-china-sea-site.name: TRIDENT site, north-eastern South China Sea

summary.plain: An area of the deep seabed in the north-eastern South China Sea, about 3.5 kilometres down on a flat abyssal plain, chosen after an expedition as the home of the proposed TRIDENT neutrino telescope.

facility:triumf.name: TRIUMF
facility:triumf.operator_text: TRIUMF Inc., owned by a consortium of 21 Canadian member universities

summary.plain: Canada’s national particle accelerator centre, on the University of British Columbia campus in Vancouver. Founded in 1968, it hosts research in particle and nuclear physics, materials science and the life sciences.
The Siberian valley near Lake Baikal where the Tunka-133 cosmic-ray array, the Tunka radio array and the hybrid TAIGA gamma-ray detectors operate.
The University of Milano-Bicocca in Milan, home of the HOLMES neutrino-mass experiment, which measures the electron neutrino mass from the decay of holmium-163 with ultra-cold detectors.

facility:university-of-washington-cenpa.name: Center for Experimental Nuclear Physics and Astrophysics (CENPA)

summary.plain: CENPA is a physics research lab at the University of Washington in Seattle. It hosts ADMX, an experiment that searches for a hypothetical dark-matter particle called the axion using a large magnet and a supercooled resonant cavity.

facility:vera-c-rubin-observatory.name: Vera C. Rubin Observatory
facility:vera-c-rubin-observatory.operator: NSF NOIRLab and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
facility:vera-c-rubin-observatory.operator_text: NSF NOIRLab and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory

summary.plain: A new observatory on Cerro Pachón in Chile, named for astronomer Vera Rubin. Its telescope and the largest digital camera ever built photograph the southern sky every few nights.

A small shallow underground laboratory in the Vue-des-Alpes road tunnel in the Swiss Jura mountains near Neuchâtel, under about 235 metres of rock. It houses the GeMSE gamma-ray screening facility and is the planned first-phase home of the DELight dark matter experiment.

facility:wipp.name: Waste Isolation Pilot Plant
facility:wipp.operator_text: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Environmental Management (operating contractor: Salado Isolation Mining Contractors, LLC)

summary.plain: An underground salt-bed site in New Mexico built by the U.S. Department of Energy to store nuclear waste. Its deep, quiet tunnels also hosted the EXO-200 physics experiment from 2011 to 2018.
The dark outback site near Woomera, South Australia, where the Japanese-Australian CANGAROO collaboration ran its gamma-ray telescopes from 1992 until 2011.

facility:yakutsk-eas-array.name: Yakutsk Extensive Air Shower Array
facility:yakutsk-eas-array.operator: Yu.G. Shafer Institute of Cosmophysical Research and Aeronomy, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences
facility:yakutsk-eas-array.operator_text: Yu.G. Shafer Institute of Cosmophysical Research and Aeronomy, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: One of the oldest giant cosmic-ray observatories, in the Lena river valley in Siberia, run by the Shafer Institute in Yakutsk.

Wright Laboratory is a Yale University physics building in New Haven, Connecticut. It hosts several fundamental-physics experiments, including HAYSTAC, which searches for the axion, a candidate particle for dark matter.

aliases: Yangbajing High Altitude Cosmic Ray Laboratory
facility:yangbajing-cosmic-ray-observato.name: Yangbajing Cosmic Ray Observatory

summary.plain: A Sino-Japanese and Sino-Italian high-altitude research site on the Tibetan plateau, 4300 metres above sea level, hosting air-shower arrays that study cosmic rays and gamma rays.

intervals.label: Y2L-A5 (~200 m2) built by IBS CUP

facility:yangyang-underground-laboratory.name: Yangyang Underground Laboratory
facility:yangyang-underground-laboratory.operator_text: Center for Underground Physics (CUP), Institute for Basic Science (IBS), Korea; the space is provided by the operator of the Yangyang pumped-storage power plant (thanked in the papers as Korea Midland Power Co. and Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power, KHNP)

summary.plain: A small underground laboratory in the tunnels beside a pumped-storage hydroelectric power plant under Mount Jumbong in Yangyang, South Korea, about 700 metres below the surface. Korean teams ran the KIMS, COSINE-100 and AMoRE experiments here before moving to the new, deeper Yemilab.

facility:yemilab.name: Yemilab
facility:yemilab.operator_text: Institute for Basic Science (IBS), Korea (Center for Underground Physics / Center for Yemilab Operation), inside the Handuk iron mine of SM Handuk Iron Mine Co., Ltd.

summary.plain: A deep underground laboratory about 1,000 metres below Mount Yemi in Jeongseon, South Korea, built inside an active iron mine and completed in 2022. It succeeds the Yangyang laboratory and hosts the upgraded COSINE-100U dark-matter detector and the AMoRE-II double-beta-decay experiment now being installed.
The site near the Hanbit (formerly Yonggwang) nuclear power plant in South Korea where the RENO experiment placed two detectors to catch antineutrinos from six reactors.

place.region: Antofagasta Region (Cerro Toco, near San Pedro de Atacama)

summary.plain: The mountainside on Cerro Toco, in northern Chile, where the six-metre Atacama Cosmology Telescope stood until it was decommissioned after it took its final data in 2022.
The mountain research station in Yamanashi, Japan, where the 100-square-kilometre AGASA array of particle detectors recorded giant cosmic-ray air showers from 1990 to 2004.
A temporary laboratory in a shipping container beside the Angra 2 reactor building in Brazil, 30 metres from the reactor core, where the CONNIE silicon-sensor array sits with no rock cover.

A patch of seabed in the Mediterranean Sea, about 40 kilometres off the coast of Toulon, France, nearly 2.5 kilometres below the surface. Here the ANTARES neutrino telescope hung its cables of light sensors from 2006 until it was switched off in 2022.
The mountaintop site in the Sacramento Mountains of New Mexico where the Sloan Foundation 2.5-metre telescope of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey stands.
The main Argonne National Laboratory campus near Lemont, Illinois, southwest of Chicago.

site:ash-river-nova-far-detector.name: Ash River NOvA far detector laboratory

summary.plain: A large surface building in the forest near Ash River, Minnesota, close to the Canadian border. It holds the NOvA far detector, 810 kilometres from the neutrino beam at Fermilab, with only a thin layer of concrete and heavy mineral above it.
A spot near the shore of the southern end of Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, where strings of light sensors are anchored more than a kilometre deep in the world's deepest lake.
The excavated hall in Mount Andyrchi, in the Northern Caucasus, that holds the Baksan scintillation telescope, 550 metres inside the tunnel under about 850 metres of water-equivalent rock.

depth.display: ~2100 m of rock above the laboratory

summary.plain: A chamber under more than two kilometres of rock in a mountain in the Russian Caucasus, holding tonnes of liquid gallium metal to catch solar neutrinos.
The shallow underground laboratory of the University of Bern's physics institutes, in the city of Bern.

site:binp-novosibirsk-akademgorodok.name: Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics campus (Akademgorodok, Novosibirsk)

summary.plain: The campus of the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics in Akademgorodok, Novosibirsk, Siberia, home of the VEPP electron-positron colliders and their detectors.
The experimental hall at RHIC interaction point 10, at the 10 o'clock position of the collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory, where PHOBOS recorded heavy-ion collisions.
The experimental hall at RHIC interaction point 2, at the 2 o'clock position of the collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory, where BRAHMS recorded heavy-ion collisions.
The experimental hall on the RHIC particle-collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory where the STAR detector records the debris of particle collisions.

site:bnl-rhic-ip8-phenix-sphenix.name: RHIC Interaction Point 8 (PHENIX / sPHENIX experimental hall)

summary.plain: The experimental hall on the RHIC particle-collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory that housed the PHENIX detector and later its successor, sPHENIX.

The main Brookhaven National Laboratory campus in Upton, on Long Island, New York — a large research site built on the former Camp Upton army base, home to the laboratory's accelerators, detectors and other scientific facilities.

depth.display: 1.1 km beneath the North York Moors

site:boulby-mine.name: Boulby Mine (site of the underground laboratory)

summary.plain: An underground laboratory inside a working mine on the North Yorkshire coast of England, more than a kilometre below the North York Moors.
A now-closed nuclear power plant on the Elbe river in northern Germany, where the CONUS experiment sat just 17 metres from the reactor core to catch its antineutrinos.

site:bugey-npp-detector-halls.name: Bugey Nuclear Power Plant detector halls

summary.plain: Rooms and a gallery at the Bugey nuclear power plant in eastern France, from 15 to 95 metres from a reactor core, where the Bugey detectors recorded reactor antineutrinos in the early 1990s.

place.region: Cascadia Basin, off Vancouver Island, British Columbia

summary.plain: A deep patch of the Pacific Ocean floor off the west coast of Vancouver Island, Canada, more than 2.6 kilometres down, where a planned neutrino telescope will one day be built using an existing undersea cable network.
The surface hall on CERN’s Meyrin site that houses the Antiproton Decelerator, the ELENA ring and the experiments that make and study antimatter.
The building at CERN's Point 8, on the French side of the CERN site, where the CAST experiment's cryogenic equipment is sited and where CAST searched for axions from the Sun until the end of 2022.
An underground cavern in CERN's North Area, on the French side of the laboratory, that has held a succession of kaon-decay experiments: NA48, then NA62, and reserved for the future SHiP experiment.

Experimental Hall North 2, a large surface hall in CERN's North Area at Prévessin in France, where the COMPASS and AMBER spectrometers on the M2 beam line study the structure of protons and other hadrons.

The underground cavern at Point 2 of the LEP ring, near the French village of Sergy, where the L3 detector recorded electron-positron collisions from 1989 to 2000. The same cavern and L3's huge magnet were later reused for the ALICE experiment.
The underground cavern at Point 4 of the LEP ring, near the French village of Echenevex, where the ALEPH detector recorded electron-positron collisions from 1989 to 2000.

The underground cavern at Point 8 of the LEP ring, near the French town of Ferney-Voltaire, where the DELPHI detector recorded electron-positron collisions from 1989 to 2000. The same cavern now houses the LHCb experiment.

CERN's main campus, an 80-hectare site that straddles the Swiss-French border next to the village of Meyrin outside Geneva. Most of the laboratory's offices, workshops, computer centre and visitor buildings are here, and the ATLAS experiment sits underground at its edge.
A large hall at CERN, on the French side of the laboratory, where full-size prototypes of the DUNE detectors were built and tested in a particle beam.

The underground cavern at the edge of CERN's Meyrin campus where the ATLAS detector sits, about 100 metres below ground. It is one of the eight access points around the 27-kilometre Large Hadron Collider ring and the place where two of the LHC's proton beams are made to collide inside ATLAS.

The underground cavern at Point 2 of the Large Hadron Collider, near the French village of St Genis-Pouilly, where the ALICE experiment records lead-ion and proton collisions. The cavern previously housed the L3 experiment during CERN's earlier LEP collider.
The place where the CMS experiment sits: a cavern about 100 metres below the village of Cessy in France, on the ring of the Large Hadron Collider just across the border from Geneva.
The underground cavern at Point 8 of the LHC ring, near the French town of Ferney-Voltaire, where the LHCb detector sits about 100 metres below ground.

site:cern-prevessin-north-area.name: CERN SPS North Area experimental-hall zone (hall not identified)

summary.plain: CERN's Prévessin site on the French side of the border, where the SPS North Area experimental halls are located; a general location used for historical North Area experiments whose exact hall is not documented.

site:cern-prevessin-north-area.technical: Campus-grade location for the SPS North Area experimental-hall zone at Prévessin: the midpoint of the EHN1 and EHN2 building outlines in CERN's MapCERN layer; used for North Area heavy-ion experiments whose hall is not identified in the sources fetched.

summary.plain: The underground hall on CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron ring where the UA2 detector sat to catch head-on collisions between protons and antiprotons.
The underground hall on CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron ring where the UA1 detector sat to catch head-on collisions between protons and antiprotons.
An unused service tunnel at CERN, 480 metres from the ATLAS collision point, that now holds the FASER experiment, searching for rare particles thrown straight down the beamline.

An unused service tunnel at CERN, on the opposite side of the ATLAS collision point from FASER, that houses the SND@LHC experiment, which studies neutrinos and searches for rare particles produced in LHC collisions.
The summit dome on Cerro Pachón in northern Chile that houses the 8.4-metre Simonyi Survey Telescope of the Rubin Observatory.
The dome on Cerro Tololo in the Chilean Andes that houses the 4-metre Blanco telescope, which carries the Dark Energy Camera used for the Dark Energy Survey.
A location very close to the reactor core at the Chooz nuclear power plant in France, where the NUCLEUS experiment is being built to catch antineutrinos with extremely sensitive cryogenic detectors.

aliases: China Jinping Underground Laboratory Phase I
site:cjpl-i.name: CJPL-I

summary.plain: The original hall of the China Jinping Underground Laboratory, reached from a hydropower station tunnel under more than two kilometres of mountain rock in Sichuan, China.

aliases: China Jinping Underground Laboratory Phase II
site:cjpl-ii.name: CJPL-II

summary.plain: A newer, larger extension of the Jinping underground laboratory, about half a kilometre from the original hall along the same tunnel, also under more than two kilometres of rock.

place.region: Antofagasta Region (Cerro Toco, near San Pedro de Atacama)

summary.plain: The high-desert site on Cerro Toco, in northern Chile, where the four CLASS telescopes survey the polarization of the Big Bang afterglow over most of the sky.
The Wilson Synchrotron Laboratory on the Cornell University campus in Ithaca, New York, which houses the Cornell Electron Storage Ring and, for 1979 to 2008, the CLEO and CUSB experiments.
The underground halls near Shenzhen, China, where Daya Bay's detectors sat close to nuclear reactors to catch antineutrinos.
DESY's main campus in the Bahrenfeld district of Hamburg, Germany.
The experimental hall on the HERA ring at DESY where the H1 detector recorded electron-proton collisions.
The experimental hall on the HERA ring at DESY where the ZEUS detector recorded electron-proton collisions.
A hall inside a hill near the Chooz nuclear plant in France, over a kilometre from the reactors, shielded by rock from cosmic rays.
The hall close to the Chooz nuclear reactors in France where Double Chooz placed its near detector.

aliases: Fly's Eye I and II site
site:dugway-flys-eye.name: Fly's Eye site, Dugway Proving Ground (approximate)

summary.plain: The Utah desert area on the Dugway Proving Ground where the original Fly's Eye cosmic-ray detector stood in the 1980s and early 1990s.
The first station of the High Resolution Fly's Eye cosmic-ray fluorescence detector, on a hilltop in the Utah desert, on the U.S. Army Dugway Proving Ground.

site:dugway-hires-ii.name: HiRes-II site, Camel's Back Ridge, Dugway Proving Ground

summary.plain: The second station of the HiRes cosmic-ray fluorescence detector, on Camel's Back Ridge in the Utah desert, about 13 km from the first station.

The site of the European Spallation Source on the northeastern edge of Lund, Sweden, where its proton accelerator and target station are being built and where the ESSnuSB near detector would sit 250 metres from the target.
The construction area next to the GSI campus in Darmstadt where the FAIR accelerator facility is being built, including the new SIS100 ring and the halls for the CBM and PANDA experiments.

The interaction hall on the Fermilab Tevatron ring where the CDF detector sat, in Batavia, Illinois. Its position is the centroid of the hall building as traced in OpenStreetMap, not a surveyed point.
The interaction hall on the Fermilab Tevatron ring where the D0 detector sat, in Batavia, Illinois. Its position is the centroid of the hall building as traced in OpenStreetMap, not a surveyed point.
The Fermilab experimental hall where the KTeV experiment studied rare kaon decays and CP violation in the 1990s.
The 27-square-kilometre laboratory site west of Chicago where Fermilab accelerators, the neutrino beamlines and the DUNE near detector are located.
The building at Fermilab, near Chicago, that holds the 14-metre superconducting ring used by the Muon g-2 experiment to measure a tiny wobble in spinning muons.
The building at Fermilab, near Chicago, where the Mu2e experiment is being built: a chain of three giant superconducting magnets that will search for a muon turning directly into an electron.
The Fermilab hall used by the SeaQuest Drell-Yan experiment, and proposed as the home of its DarkQuest successor.
A stretch of the Gobi Desert north of the city of Dunhuang, China, where a prototype array of radio antennas is testing technology for the giant GRAND project.
The campus of the GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research in Darmstadt, Germany, home of the UNILAC linear accelerator, the SIS18 heavy-ion synchrotron and experiments such as HADES.

A gallery under the wall of the reactor containment building at the Hanbit nuclear power complex in Korea, ten metres below ground, where the NEOS detector sat about 24 metres from the core of the unit-5 reactor.
The Hanford Site, a very large U.S. Department of Energy reservation in southeastern Washington on the Columbia River, where Cowan and Reines made their first attempt to detect the neutrino in 1953.

site:hanle-gamma-ray-site.name: Hanle gamma-ray telescope site (MACE and HAGAR)
